problem.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Every weekday, the island children eat breakfast together in the cabin of the ferry that carries them to the mainland school.

For years the meal had followed its own quiet order: Pell poured the tea, the twins split the bread, and no one spoke until the engine changed pitch at the harbor mouth. Then, one gray morning in March, Miss Arden, the new schoolteacher, stepped aboard with a tin of oranges and sat down among them. The cabin seemed brighter, as though she had carried a lamp inside, yet the children hardly knew where to put their hands.

A literary critic argues that the story presents Miss Arden's arrival as making the children's breakfast both more vivid and less settled than before.

Which finding from the story, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
problem.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Every weekday, the island children eat breakfast together in the cabin of the ferry that carries them to the mainland school.

For years the meal had followed its own quiet order: Pell poured the tea, the twins split the bread, and no one spoke until the engine changed pitch at the harbor mouth. Then, one gray morning in March, Miss Arden, the new schoolteacher, stepped aboard with a tin of oranges and sat down among them. The cabin seemed brighter, as though she had carried a lamp inside, yet the children hardly knew where to put their hands.

A literary critic argues that the story presents Miss Arden's arrival as making the children's breakfast both more vivid and less settled than before.
problem.question: Which finding from the story, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: Pell, peeling one of Miss Arden's oranges, notices that its scent fills the cabin, and he decides to bring fruit of his own to the next morning's meal so that the breakfast will stay just as it was.
Pell, noticing Miss Arden's tin of oranges, remembers that his mother once packed fruit for him, and he quietly pours the tea at the usual moment while the twins split the bread as always.
Pell, holding one of Miss Arden's oranges up to the window light, laughs aloud before the engine changes pitch, then stops, unsure whether he has broken a rule no one ever stated.
Pell, watching Miss Arden take a seat among them, wishes the cabin were brighter, and he resolves to ask the captain for a lamp before the next morning's crossing.
problem.explanation: 비평가는 선생님의 등장으로 아침 식사가 '더 생생해지는 동시에 덜 안정된다'고 주장하므로 두 측면이 함께 드러나는 발견이 필요하다. C에서 Pell은 빛에 비친 오렌지를 보고 엔진 소리가 바뀌기 전에 웃는데, 이는 생생함이자 침묵 규칙을 깬 것이며, 이어지는 망설임은 불확실함을 보여 준다. A는 생생함은 있지만 식사를 그대로 유지하려 하므로 '덜 안정됨'이 없다. B는 기억이 떠오를 뿐 의식이 평소대로 진행되어 변화가 드러나지 않는다. D는 오히려 선실이 밝아지지 않았다고 느끼는 것이라 지문 속 '더 밝아짐'과도 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The critic claims the breakfast becomes both more vivid and less settled, so you need a finding that shows both at once. In C, Pell laughs at the orange glowing in the window light, which is vivid, and he does it before the engine changes pitch, breaking the silence rule; his hesitation afterward shows uncertainty. A has vividness, but Pell wants the breakfast to stay the same, so nothing is less settled. B gives Pell a memory, but the ritual goes on exactly as usual, so no change appears. D has Pell wishing the cabin were brighter, which actually contradicts the text's point that the cabin seemed brighter.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A schoolteacher's unexpected arrival at the island boat's morning meal transforms the children's quiet ritual into something luminous and uncertain.

hardJudge.note: 비평가 주장은 '더 생생함 + 덜 안정됨' 두 요소. C만이 빛에 비친 오렌지·웃음(생생함)과 엔진 소리 전 침묵 규칙 위반 후 망설임(불안정)을 동시에 충족. A는 생생함만 있고 현상 유지를 택해 '덜 안정됨' 결여, B는 의식이 평소대로 진행되어 변화 없음, D는 '선실이 더 밝아 보였다'는 지문과 모순. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 논리 정확. 두 조건을 모두 확인해야 하므로 medium 적합. 지문은 창작물로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: C만 '더 생생함'(빛·웃음)과 '덜 안정됨'(엔진 소리 전 침묵 규칙 위반·망설임)을 함께 충족한다. A는 생생함만 있고 안정 유지를 추구하며, B는 변화가 없다. D는 지문 내용과 모순되어 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 부분 근거를 가진 오답이 A와 B 두 개라 medium 기준에 부합한다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
In Ilse Varga's novel The Tidewright, young Maren steers her uncle's skiff in the island's annual ferry-crossing regatta. She misreads the current, drifts far east of the course, and sees Corran Bank, her family's ancestral fishing ground, from the mainland side for the first time. From there the bank looks small and ordinary, just a pale patch of water among many others. Maren says nothing for the rest of the race, and that silence marks a break: she has outgrown the legends her family built around the place.

Text 2
Varga makes sure the reader sees Corran Bank shrink under Maren's unexpected view; the narration even compares it to "a thumbprint on glass." But reading Maren's quiet as a rejection overlooks what comes next. On the ferry home, she traces the bank's outline from memory on the back of her ticket and gets every shoal right. The strange angle has not cut her off from the grounds. It has shown her that her bond with them is something she will have to keep up by remembering, not something she simply inherits.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about what Maren's silence reveals?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
In Ilse Varga's novel The Tidewright, young Maren steers her uncle's skiff in the island's annual ferry-crossing regatta. She misreads the current, drifts far east of the course, and sees Corran Bank, her family's ancestral fishing ground, from the mainland side for the first time. From there the bank looks small and ordinary, just a pale patch of water among many others. Maren says nothing for the rest of the race, and that silence marks a break: she has outgrown the legends her family built around the place.

Text 2
Varga makes sure the reader sees Corran Bank shrink under Maren's unexpected view; the narration even compares it to "a thumbprint on glass." But reading Maren's quiet as a rejection overlooks what comes next. On the ferry home, she traces the bank's outline from memory on the back of her ticket and gets every shoal right. The strange angle has not cut her off from the grounds. It has shown her that her bond with them is something she will have to keep up by remembering, not something she simply inherits.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 about what Maren's silence reveals?
options: By accepting that Maren's silence shows she has outgrown her family's legends, while arguing that her drift off course is an accident rather than a meaningful event in the novel
By disputing that Corran Bank appears small from the mainland side, while agreeing that Maren's silence signals a break with her family
By accepting both that the bank appears diminished and that Maren is withdrawing, while citing her sketch on the ticket as further proof of her detachment
By accepting that the bank appears diminished from Maren's new angle, while arguing that a later moment shows her silence reflects a changed but continuing attachment
problem.explanation: Text 2의 저자는 "a thumbprint on glass"라는 비유를 들어 둑이 작아 보인다는 점은 인정한다. 그러나 귀항하는 페리에서 Maren이 기억만으로 둑의 윤곽을 그리는 장면을 근거로, 그녀의 침묵이 거부가 아니라 형태가 바뀐 애착이라고 주장한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 Text 2가 반박하는 '침묵=단절'이라는 해석을 오히려 받아들이고 있다. B는 Text 2가 인정한 '둑이 작아 보인다'는 점을 부정하므로 틀렸고, C는 스케치 장면을 정반대 의미(애착이 아닌 거리 두기)로 읽었다.
problem.explanationEn: The author of Text 2 agrees that the bank looks smaller and quotes the "thumbprint on glass" comparison as support. However, the author points to the later scene in which Maren draws the bank accurately from memory and argues that her silence reflects a changed, ongoing attachment rather than a rejection. That makes D the answer. A is wrong because it accepts the "silence equals break" reading that Text 2 rejects. B is wrong because it denies the shrinking that Text 2 actually accepts, and C is wrong because it treats the sketch as a sign of detachment, when Text 2 uses it to show the opposite.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — During the ferry crossing's annual regatta, a miscalculated route causes an islander to witness her family's ancestral fishing ground from an angle she never imagined.

hardJudge.note: Text 2 explicitly concedes the bank's diminished appearance ("thumbprint on glass") and then rebuts the "silence = rejection" reading via the ticket-sketch scene, framing the bond as changed but continuing — exactly D. A wrongly has Text 2 accepting the "outgrown" claim (and invents an "accident" argument); B contradicts Text 2's concession about the bank shrinking; C inverts the meaning Text 2 assigns to the sketch. Korean and English explanations align with each other and with the letter references; English explanation contains no Hangul. Fictional novel/critic, no copyright concern. Two-step (identify concession + identify rebuttal) with distractors each half-right fits medium.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 옳다. 오답 A·B·C는 각각 일부만 맞는 근거를 가지고 있어 두 텍스트를 비교해야 배제된다. 따라서 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
The letter from the Halvorsen Academy had been folded and refolded so many times that its creases had gone soft as cloth. Katrina, sitting at the stern of the school boat while the island's gray cliffs shrank into the mist behind ______ understood that if she signed it, every return to the harbor would be a visit rather than a homecoming.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The letter from the Halvorsen Academy had been folded and refolded so many times that its creases had gone soft as cloth. Katrina, sitting at the stern of the school boat while the island's gray cliffs shrank into the mist behind ______ understood that if she signed it, every return to the harbor would be a visit rather than a homecoming.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: her,
her—
her;
her
problem.explanation: 주어 Katrina 뒤의 "sitting at the stern ... behind her"는 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 삽입구이므로, 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 동사 understood와 이어진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 대시는 삽입구를 닫는다는 점은 맞지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호가 서로 짝이 맞지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 있어야 쓸 수 있는데, 앞부분 "Katrina, sitting ..."에는 본동사가 없어서 독립절이 아니다. D처럼 아무 부호도 쓰지 않으면 삽입구가 닫히지 않아 문장 구조가 흐트러진다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "sitting at the stern ... behind her" is a nonessential modifier that opens with a comma right after the subject Katrina, so you need a matching comma to close it before the verb "understood." That makes A correct. B is right that the phrase needs to be closed at this point, but a dash can't close a phrase that started with a comma, because the two marks have to match. C fails because a semicolon has to join two independent clauses, and "Katrina, sitting ..." has no main verb, so it isn't one. D leaves the phrase open, which muddles the structure of the sentence.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On the school boat heading home, Katrina must decide whether to accept the scholarship that would carry her away from the island forever.

hardJudge.note: Comma-opened nonessential participial phrase ("sitting at the stern ... behind her") between subject Katrina and verb understood must be closed with a matching comma; A is correct. B (dash) mismatches the opening comma, C (semicolon) lacks an independent clause before it, D leaves the modifier unclosed. Korean and English explanations agree, reference the correct letters, and contain no errors. Long interrupting phrase plus matching-punctuation rule makes this standard medium difficulty.

advisory.note: 삽입구 안에 while절이 끼어 있어 여는 쉼표를 놓치기 쉽다. 그래서 짝 맞추기 판단이 필요하고 medium 난이도에 맞는다. 대시 오답도 그럴듯하다.

problem.passage:
Thorvald had walked for two frozen days along the coast road, sleet stinging his face and the harbor lights of the next port nowhere in sight. When he finally pushed open the door of the pawn shop, the owner, a thin man with ink-stained cuffs who squinted at every stranger, looked up from his ledger______ in a velvet tray behind the counter lay the small garnet ring his daughter had lost.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Thorvald had walked for two frozen days along the coast road, sleet stinging his face and the harbor lights of the next port nowhere in sight. When he finally pushed open the door of the pawn shop, the owner, a thin man with ink-stained cuffs who squinted at every stranger, looked up from his ledger______ in a velvet tray behind the counter lay the small garnet ring his daughter had lost.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , there,
. There,
there,
and there,
problem.explanation: 긴 동격구 뒤의 주절 'the owner ... looked up from his ledger'는 독립절이고, 'there ... lay the ... ring'도 도치된 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표로 나누어야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 구두점 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 접속사 and를 썼지만 두 독립절 사이 and 앞에 필요한 쉼표가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: After the long appositive, the main clause "the owner ... looked up from his ledger" is a complete independent clause, and "there ... lay the ... ring" is another independent clause with inverted word order. Two independent clauses like these can be split with a period, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "and" but leaves out the comma that has to come before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Thorvald, an Icelandic fisherman, travels two frozen days through winter storms to retrieve his daughter's lost wedding ring from a pawn shop in the next port.

hardJudge.note: B는 명확히 정답이며 A(쉼표 오용), C(무종지문)는 확실한 오답. 그러나 D("ledger and there, in a velvet tray ... lay the ring")는 두 독립절을 등위접속사 and로 연결한 문장으로, 쉼표 누락만을 근거로 배제하는 것은 논쟁의 여지가 있어(짧은 절 사이에서는 쉼표 생략이 널리 허용됨) 정답 유일성이 다소 취약하다. 실제 SAT에서는 보통 이런 거리로는 변별하지 않으므로 D를 다른 명백한 오류(예: 세미콜론 오용, 'and' 없이 접속부사 사용 등)로 교체하는 것이 바람직하다. 난이도는 긴 동격구가 삽입되어 주절 경계를 파악해야 하므로 medium에 부합한다.

advisory.note: B가 유일한 정답이다. D(쉼표 없이 'and'를 쓴 경우)는 SAT 관례로 보면 오답이 맞지만, 짧은 절에서는 쉼표 생략을 허용하는 견해도 있어 다소 논쟁의 여지가 있다. 다만 이 문장에서는 두 절이 길기 때문에 배제가 타당하다. 동격구가 길어서 주어와 동사를 추적하는 단계가 필요하므로 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
For eleven autumns, Ramón and Diego had carried their squash to the village plaza, each certain the judges would finally favor his. This year a late frost forced them to share a single greenhouse, and on the third cold night Diego broke the silence. His father, a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor ______ taught him to pinch off the first blossoms so that the vines would send their strength into the roots. Ramón listened, then knelt and showed Diego the crushed eggshells his own father had buried beneath every seedling.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: For eleven autumns, Ramón and Diego had carried their squash to the village plaza, each certain the judges would finally favor his. This year a late frost forced them to share a single greenhouse, and on the third cold night Diego broke the silence. His father, a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor ______ taught him to pinch off the first blossoms so that the vines would send their strength into the roots. Ramón listened, then knelt and showed Diego the crushed eggshells his own father had buried beneath every seedling.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; had
— had
, had
had
problem.explanation: "a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor"는 주어 "His father"를 설명하는 비필수 동격어구로, 앞에 쉼표가 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 하고 그 뒤에 동사 "had taught"가 이어진다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론을 써서 주어와 동사를 갈라놓고, 세미콜론 앞부분은 독립절이 아니다. B는 대시로 닫아 쉼표로 연 동격어구와 문장부호가 맞지 않는다. D는 닫는 문장부호가 없어서 삽입 어구가 어디서 끝나는지 표시되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject "His father." It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "had taught" continues the sentence. That makes C correct. A uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb, and the words before the semicolon don't form an independent clause. B closes with a dash, which doesn't match the comma that opened the appositive. D leaves out the closing punctuation entirely, so the reader can't tell where the inserted phrase ends.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In a harvest village, Ramón and Diego, rival farmers competing for the year's best crop, end up teaching each other techniques their fathers had kept secret.

hardJudge.note: 검산: "His father, a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor, had taught him..." — 쉼표로 연 비필수 동격어구를 쉼표로 닫는 C가 유일하게 정확. A는 세미콜론 앞이 독립절이 아니고 주어-동사 분리, B는 쉼표/대시 짝 불일치, D는 닫는 구두점 누락. 해설(한/영) 모두 C를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 난이도: 여는 쉼표를 찾아 짝을 맞추는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, B(대시)·D(무구두점)가 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능해 medium 적합. 지문은 독창적 서사로 저작권 의심 없음. 사소한 형식 참고: D 선택지가 " had"로 앞 공백만 있어 '구두점 없음' 의도는 전달되나 시각적으로 다소 어색함(감점 수준 아님).

advisory.note: C는 쉼표로 연 동격어구를 쉼표로 닫는다. 그러면 "His father, a stubborn man who had trusted no neighbor, had taught him..."이 된다. 학생은 먼저 동격어구가 어디서 끝나는지 찾고, 이어서 연 부호와 닫는 부호가 같은지 확인해야 한다. 이 두 단계 판단이 medium 난이도에 맞다. D는 "had trusted ... had taught"처럼 had가 이어져 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉽다. B는 대시도 삽입 부호라서 그럴듯해 보이므로 함정으로 잘 작동한다.

problem.passage:
From the back seat of the swaying matatu, Kamau watched the old leather worker guide the teenager's fingers along the edge of a stiff brown hide, pressing the awl through it with a patience that seemed older than Nairobi itself______ earbuds in, stared past him at the traffic crawling along Thika Road. Kamau wondered who, years from now, would remember the old man's hands.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: From the back seat of the swaying matatu, Kamau watched the old leather worker guide the teenager's fingers along the edge of a stiff brown hide, pressing the awl through it with a patience that seemed older than Nairobi itself______ earbuds in, stared past him at the traffic crawling along Thika Road. Kamau wondered who, years from now, would remember the old man's hands.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; the boy,
, the boy,
; the boy
the boy,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 "Kamau watched ... itself"까지 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the boy ... stared past him"도 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 세미콜론이 필요하다. 또한 "earbuds in"은 비필수 삽입구라서 "the boy" 뒤에 쉼표가 있어야 뒤 쉼표와 짝을 이룬다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 삽입구 쉼표는 맞지만 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 세미콜론은 맞지만 삽입구 앞 쉼표가 빠져 쉼표 짝이 맞지 않고, D는 구두점 없이 두 절을 이어 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, "Kamau watched ... Nairobi itself," is a complete independent clause, and "the boy ... stared past him at the traffic" is also an independent clause, so you need a semicolon between them. "Earbuds in" is a nonessential interrupting phrase, so it needs a comma after "the boy" to pair with the comma that follows "in." That makes A correct. B sets off the interrupter correctly, but it joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C uses the semicolon correctly but leaves out the opening comma of the interrupter, so the commas don't pair up. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On a Nairobi matatu, Kamau watches an elderly leather worker train a disinterested teenager in a dying craft, wondering who will remember the old man's hands.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "Kamau watched ... Nairobi itself"는 완전한 독립절, 뒤 "the boy, earbuds in, stared past him..."도 독립절 → 세미콜론 필요. "earbuds in"은 절대구(삽입구)로 앞뒤 쉼표 짝이 필요하므로 "the boy," 형태가 맞음. A 정답 확인. B는 comma splice, C는 삽입구 앞 쉼표 누락, D는 run-on으로 모두 배제됨. 해설(한/영) 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조이며 모순 없음. 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. matatu·Thika Road 등 배경 사실 문제 없음. 난이도: 독립절 판별 + 삽입구 쉼표 짝 확인의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, B·C가 각각 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 medium에 적합. 사소한 점: 선택지 D 앞 공백이 두 칸으로 표기된 것은 표기 정리 수준의 문제로 판정에 영향 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞다. 앞은 독립절이고 뒤도 독립절이며 earbuds in은 쉼표 짝으로 감싼 삽입구다. 'the teenager'를 'the boy'로 받는 지시 관계도 자연스럽다. 경계 판단과 삽입구 판단의 두 단계가 필요해 medium 난이도에 맞다. 다만 D(구두점 없음)는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
Rashid had worked beside the stranger at the tannery vats for three mornings before she spoke of the merchant. Her name was Fadela, and the story she told, a rambling account of a leather trader who had once bartered a saddle for a bride's silver anklet______ the very tale Rashid's grandfather had recited every winter, decades earlier, to a room full of cousins.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Rashid had worked beside the stranger at the tannery vats for three mornings before she spoke of the merchant. Her name was Fadela, and the story she told, a rambling account of a leather trader who had once bartered a saddle for a bride's silver anklet______ the very tale Rashid's grandfather had recited every winter, decades earlier, to a room full of cousins.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , and was
, was
; was
was
problem.explanation: "the story she told" 뒤의 "a rambling account ... anklet"은 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 동격어구이므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤에 주어 story의 동사 was가 와야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 and가 등위절을 만드는 것처럼 보이지만 앞에 동사가 없어 주어 story와 동사 was를 부적절하게 끊는다. C의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사 사이에 쓸 수 없으며, 앞부분은 독립절도 아니다. D는 동격어구를 여는 쉼표만 있고 닫는 쉼표가 없어 삽입구의 경계가 불완전하다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "a rambling account ... anklet" is a nonessential appositive. It opens with a comma after "the story she told," so it must close with a matching comma before the verb "was," which goes with the subject "story." That makes B correct. A adds "and" as if it were joining two predicates, but the subject "story" has no verb earlier in the sentence, so "and" breaks the sentence apart. C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and a semicolon can only join independent clauses. D leaves the appositive open because the closing comma is missing.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Rashid and Fadela, strangers at the tannery vats, discover they once knew each other's families through a leather merchant's tale told decades ago.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 주어 "the story she told" + 긴 비필수 동격어구(쉼표로 열림) + 동사 "was". 닫는 쉼표가 필요하므로 B가 유일하게 옳다. A는 선행 동사 없이 and로 술어를 접속하는 오류, C는 주어–동사 사이 세미콜론(앞부분이 독립절 아님), D는 동격어구를 닫지 않음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 정확하다. 긴 삽입구 때문에 훑어 읽으면 D(쉼표 생략)나 A를 고르기 쉬워 medium에 적합. 창작 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 동격어구 안에 관계절(who had once bartered...)이 들어 있어 주어와 동사가 멀리 떨어져 있다. 그래서 동격어구가 쉼표로 열린 지점을 찾고, 닫는 쉼표를 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium 난이도에 맞다.

The letter, creased along its folds and weighted beneath a dented tin cup on the shelter's back ______ been addressed to someone named Eli, and its first line, "I should have said this at the trailhead," was not meant for her at all.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: By the time Mara reached the shelter again, her headlamp had dimmed to a weak yellow circle. She had walked three miles in darkness to retrieve the envelope she had glimpsed that afternoon. The letter, creased along its folds and weighted beneath a dented tin cup on the shelter's back ______ been addressed to someone named Eli, and its first line, "I should have said this at the trailhead," was not meant for her at all.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: bench had
bench—had
bench, had
bench; had
problem.explanation: "creased along its folds and weighted beneath ... bench"는 주어 "The letter"와 동사 "had been addressed" 사이에 끼어든 비필수 수식어이고, 앞에서 쉼표로 열렸으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 닫는 쉼표가 없어 "bench"가 동사 "had"의 주어처럼 읽힌다. B는 대시를 쓰는데, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 세미콜론으로 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "creased along its folds and weighted beneath ... bench" is a nonessential modifier that sits between the subject "The letter" and its verb "had been addressed." It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too, which makes C correct. A leaves out the closing comma, so "bench" looks like the subject of "had." B closes the phrase with a dash, but a phrase that opens with a comma can't close with a dash, because the punctuation has to match. D puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and the words before it can't stand alone as an independent clause.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — A hiker at a shelter walks three miles in darkness to retrieve a forgotten love letter someone else left behind, only to realize it wasn't meant for them.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The letter"와 동사 "had been addressed" 사이 쉼표로 열린 비필수 분사구를 쉼표로 닫는 C가 유일하게 옳음. A는 닫는 쉼표 누락, B는 쉼표-대시 불일치, D는 주어·동사 사이 세미콜론. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 오류 없음. 삽입구 범위 파악 + 짝 맞추기의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 오답들이 그럴듯해 medium 적합.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Back at the truck, he worked the swollen bottom drawer loose and found a bundle of envelopes tied with baling twine, each addressed in his grandfather's slanted hand to a woman named Ruth Avila ______ of them had ever been stamped.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , none
; none
none
and, none
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "he worked ... Ruth Avila"는 긴 수식어(tied with..., each addressed...)를 포함하지만 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "none of them had ever been stamped"도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. 앞의 쉼표 수식어들 때문에 쉼표가 자연스러워 보이지만 접속사가 없다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 and와 그것이 연결하는 절을 부당하게 분리한다.
problem.explanationEn: Even with its long modifiers ("tied with baling twine," "each addressed..."), the part before the blank is still a complete independent clause, and "none of them had ever been stamped" is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. The commas earlier in the sentence can make a comma look right here, but there's no conjunction. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it's a run-on sentence. D places a comma after "and," which wrongly cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At a ranch auction, Elias buys a repaired wooden desk and discovers love letters his grandfather wrote but never mailed still tucked in a drawer.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞은 긴 분사·동격 수식어를 포함하지만 "he worked ... and found a bundle of envelopes ..."로 완결된 독립절이고, 뒤 "none of them had ever been stamped"도 독립절이므로 세미콜론(B)이 유일하게 옳다. A는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 "and," 로 접속사와 절을 분리하여 오답. 앞의 쉼표 수식어들이 A를 그럴듯하게 만들고 D도 접속사 사용이라는 부분적 근거를 가지므로 medium 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 정답·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 원작 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 빈칸 앞은 긴 수식어가 붙어 있어도 독립절이고, 뒤의 "none of them had ever been stamped"는 정형동사 had가 있는 독립절이다. 따라서 B의 세미콜론만 맞다. A는 앞에 나오는 쉼표 수식어(each addressed...) 때문에 분사구문처럼 보여 강한 오답 유인이 되므로, 훑어 읽으면 틀리는 medium 설계에 맞다. C(run-on)와 D(and 뒤 쉼표)는 상대적으로 약한 오답이지만 그럴듯은 하다.

problem.passage:
Soren left the sauna on the point with heat still rising from his shoulders, and he carried that warmth like a lantern through the frozen dark toward the next fjord. His son had gone home hours earlier, unaware of what he had left behind. The knife his son had forgotten on the ice—a bone-handled blade once owned by Soren's own father______ half-buried in snow beside the abandoned fishing hole, its edge catching the faint blue light.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Soren left the sauna on the point with heat still rising from his shoulders, and he carried that warmth like a lantern through the frozen dark toward the next fjord. His son had gone home hours earlier, unaware of what he had left behind. The knife his son had forgotten on the ice—a bone-handled blade once owned by Soren's own father______ half-buried in snow beside the abandoned fishing hole, its edge catching the faint blue light.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , lay
; lay
lay
—lay
problem.explanation: 대시로 시작한 비필수 동격어구(a bone-handled blade once owned by Soren's own father)는 같은 대시로 닫아야 주어 The knife와 동사 lay가 이어지므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표가 동격어구 뒤에 와서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 부호가 서로 맞지 않는다. B의 세미콜론은 독립절 두 개를 나눌 때 쓰는데, 여기서는 주어와 동사 lay 사이를 끊어 버린다. C는 삽입구를 닫는 부호가 아예 없어서 대시로 연 삽입구가 끝나지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The dash before "a bone-handled blade" opens a nonessential appositive, so a second dash has to close it. That lets the subject "The knife" connect to the verb "lay," which is why D is correct. A looks reasonable because a comma comes after the appositive, but you can't close a dash-opened interruption with a comma, since the pair has to match. B uses a semicolon, which belongs between two independent clauses, and here it would cut the subject off from its verb "lay." C leaves out the closing punctuation entirely, so the interruption that started with the dash never ends.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Soren travels from his coastal sauna to a neighboring fjord to retrieve his son's forgotten fishing knife, carrying warmth through the frozen dark.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The knife ... on the ice"와 동사 "lay" 사이에 대시로 연 동격어구가 삽입되어 있으므로 짝이 맞는 대시로 닫는 D가 유일하게 옳음. A(쉼표)는 부호 불일치, B(세미콜론)는 주어-동사 분리, C는 삽입구 미종결로 배제됨. 해설(한/영) 모두 정답·선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 난이도는 대시 짝 맞추기+주어-동사 연결 확인의 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합. 사소한 점: 선택지 C의 앞 공백이 두 칸으로 표기됨(내용상 문제 없음).

problem.passage:
When the first thunderclap rolled over the dyeing vats, Amira set down her scraping knife and ran for the drying shed, where Zahra, the rival whose hides had won the guild's praise three seasons running, was already pulling the last skins from the racks. For a long while the two women stood at opposite ends of the shed, listening to the rain drum on the tin ______ finally Zahra, without looking up, asked how Amira kept her indigo from streaking.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: When the first thunderclap rolled over the dyeing vats, Amira set down her scraping knife and ran for the drying shed, where Zahra, the rival whose hides had won the guild's praise three seasons running, was already pulling the last skins from the racks. For a long while the two women stood at opposite ends of the shed, listening to the rain drum on the tin ______ finally Zahra, without looking up, asked how Amira kept her indigo from streaking.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: roof, and
roof,
roof and,
roof: and
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the two women stood ... roof"와 뒤 "Zahra ... asked ..."는 각각 독립절이므로 둘을 잇는 올바른 경계가 필요하다. A는 쉼표+등위접속사 and로 두 독립절을 적절히 연결한다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 "finally"를 삽입구처럼 시작하지만 짝이 되는 쉼표가 없고, 절 사이에도 구두점이 없어 어색하다. D의 콜론은 뒤 내용이 앞 절을 설명·부연할 때 쓰는데, 여기서는 시간 순서의 사건이므로 맞지 않고 콜론 뒤 and도 부적절하다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("the two women stood ... on the tin roof") and the words after it ("Zahra ... asked how ...") are both independent clauses, so you need a proper boundary between them. A joins them correctly with a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "and." B links the two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts a comma after "and," as if "finally" began an interrupting phrase, but there's no matching comma, and there's still no punctuation between the clauses. D uses a colon, but a colon introduces something that explains or expands on the first clause. Here the second clause is just the next event in time, and "and" after a colon is inappropriate.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At the tannery, a sudden storm forces Amira and her rival Zahra to shelter together, their routine work halted by weather that demands conversation.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "the two women stood ... on the tin roof"(독립절, 분사구 수식 포함)와 뒤 "finally Zahra ... asked ..."(독립절)를 잇는 자리. A(쉼표+and) 정확. B는 comma splice, C는 and 앞 쉼표 없음·and 뒤 불필요한 쉼표, D는 콜론 뒤 등위접속사로 부적절. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 A 정답을 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 긴 수식어구(listening..., without looking up) 속에서 절의 경계를 찾아야 하고 B가 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 medium에 적합. 다만 C·D가 비교적 쉽게 배제되어 medium 하한에 가까움.

advisory.note: 긴 문장과 삽입구 때문에 절의 경계를 찾는 데 정독이 필요하다. 오답 B(comma splice)와 D(콜론)는 그럴듯하므로 medium 난이도에 맞다. C 해설의 '절 사이 구두점 부재' 설명은 다소 단순하지만 결론에는 문제가 없다.

problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, "he walked forward and rested a hand on the bell of the tuba," is an independent clause. The text after it is one too: once you set aside the interrupting phrase "he explained gently," you can see the subject "the problem" and the verb "was." A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D puts the conjunction "and" right after a colon, and that isn't how a colon is used.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Young Florian struggles to master the tuba while his mentor, the band's aging conductor, gently insists that precision is less important than presence.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 "he walked forward and rested a hand on the bell of the tuba"와 뒤 "the problem ... was not ... but ..."가 모두 독립절임을 직접 확인했으며, 삽입구 "he explained gently"를 걷어내면 주어·동사가 드러난다. 세미콜론(B)이 유일하게 적법. A는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 콜론+and 조합으로 부적절. 삽입구로 인해 두 번째 절의 독립성을 파악해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, A·D가 부분적 근거를 가진 오답이므로 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 지문은 창작 서사로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 삽입구 'he explained gently'를 걷어내야 독립절이 보이므로 판단이 두 단계로 이루어져 medium 수준에 맞음. 다만 D(': and')는 쉽게 배제되는 편임.

problem.passage:
For three seasons, Priya and Anita had measured each other in kilograms of leaf, each woman weighing her basket at dusk and glancing sideways at the other's tally. Then, on a rain-slick slope above the factory, Anita slipped and fell, her basket spilling green across the mud. Priya, the rival who had once hidden a pair of pruning shears just to slow Anita ______ beside her without a word. Their hands, blistered at the very same knuckles, met over the scattered leaves.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: For three seasons, Priya and Anita had measured each other in kilograms of leaf, each woman weighing her basket at dusk and glancing sideways at the other's tally. Then, on a rain-slick slope above the factory, Anita slipped and fell, her basket spilling green across the mud. Priya, the rival who had once hidden a pair of pruning shears just to slow Anita ______ beside her without a word. Their hands, blistered at the very same knuckles, met over the scattered leaves.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: down; knelt
down, knelt
down knelt
down—knelt
problem.explanation: "the rival who had once hidden ... down"은 주어 Priya를 설명하는 비필수 동격 표현이고, Priya 바로 뒤 쉼표로 시작된다. 따라서 이 표현은 쉼표로 닫아야 주어 Priya와 동사 knelt가 바르게 이어지므로 B가 정답이다. A의 세미콜론은 두 독립절 사이에 쓰는 부호인데, 여기서는 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 앞뒤 어느 쪽도 완전한 절이 되지 못한다. C는 닫는 부호가 없어서 동격 표현이 문장의 나머지 부분과 뒤섞인다. D의 대시도 삽입 요소를 끊을 수는 있지만, 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫으면 부호의 짝이 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "the rival who had once hidden ... down" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, Priya. It opens with the comma right after "Priya." You have to close it with a matching comma so that the subject "Priya" connects cleanly to its verb "knelt," which makes B correct. A uses a semicolon, which belongs between two independent clauses, but here it would cut the subject off from its verb and leave neither side a complete clause. C leaves out the closing punctuation, so the appositive blurs into the rest of the sentence. D's dash can set off an interruption, but an interruption that opens with a comma can't close with a dash, because the marks have to match.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On the tea estate, rival harvesters Priya and Anita compete mercilessly until an accident makes them realize they've been fighting the same exhaustion.

hardJudge.note: 검산: "Priya, [the rival who had once hidden ... to slow Anita down], knelt beside her" — 쉼표로 연 비필수 동격구는 쉼표로 닫아야 하므로 B가 유일한 정답. A(세미콜론)는 주어와 동사를 분리해 양쪽 모두 독립절이 아님, C는 닫는 부호 누락, D는 쉼표–대시 짝 불일치. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 정확, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 긴 동격구(관계절 포함) 속에서 여는 쉼표를 찾아 짝을 맞춰야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, D는 부분적 타당성을 가진 매력적 오답 — medium 적합. 지문은 창작 서사로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 동격 삽입구가 길어서 여는 쉼표를 찾아야 하는 2단계 판단이 필요하다. 표준적인 medium 문항이다.

problem.passage:
By noon the bronze mirror borrowed from the neighboring shrine was gone, packed by mistake into a tour group's luggage and now somewhere on the coastal highway. Father Ishida, who had performed the harvest rite for thirty years without once altering its order, did not cancel the ceremony ______ placed a paper lantern on the altar where the mirror should have stood and began the chant as if nothing were missing.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: By noon the bronze mirror borrowed from the neighboring shrine was gone, packed by mistake into a tour group's luggage and now somewhere on the coastal highway. Father Ishida, who had performed the harvest rite for thirty years without once altering its order, did not cancel the ceremony ______ placed a paper lantern on the altar where the mirror should have stood and began the chant as if nothing were missing.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , he
and, he
, instead, he
; instead, he
problem.explanation: 긴 비필수 관계절 뒤에 있는 'Father Ishida ... did not cancel the ceremony'는 독립절이고, 'he placed ...'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이을 수 있으며, 접속부사 instead 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 instead가 들어가 있어도 접속부사는 접속사가 아니므로 역시 comma splice이다. B는 and로 두 절을 잇긴 했지만 and와 he 사이의 쉼표가 불필요하다.
problem.explanationEn: Look past the long nonessential clause and you'll see that "Father Ishida ... did not cancel the ceremony" is an independent clause, and "he placed ..." is another one. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, and the conjunctive adverb "instead" takes a comma after it, so D is correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C is still a comma splice even with "instead," because a conjunctive adverb is not a conjunction. B does join the clauses with "and," but the comma between "and" and "he" doesn't belong there.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — During the village festival, a borrowed shrine decoration gets mixed with tourists' luggage, forcing a priest to improvise a ceremony without its centerpiece.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 'Father Ishida ... did not cancel the ceremony'와 'he placed ... and began ...'은 모두 독립절. A·C는 comma splice(C는 접속부사 instead만으로 연결 불가), B는 'and, he'의 쉼표 위치 오류. D(세미콜론 + instead + 쉼표)만 적법. 해설 한·영 모두 정답 및 오답 근거가 일치하고 선택지 글자 참조가 정확함. 긴 비필수 관계절 뒤에서 독립절 경계를 식별해야 하고, B·C가 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 비필수 관계절 때문에 주절 구조를 파악해야 하고, C(쉼표+instead)가 그럴듯한 오답이어서 medium에 맞음. B는 'and, he'의 쉼표가 불필요하므로 배제가 타당함.

problem.passage:

No one in the cramped schoolroom, not even the minister's son, who noticed everything and repeated most of ______ said a word about it. Morag, however, slid her own hands beneath the desk and began, very quietly, to count the tremors.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: For three years, Morag had watched Miss Fraser chalk the date onto the blackboard each morning, and she knew the looping shape of every numeral by heart. Today the chalk skittered, leaving a seven that wavered like marram grass in the wind off the Sound. No one in the cramped schoolroom, not even the minister's son, who noticed everything and repeated most of ______ said a word about it. Morag, however, slid her own hands beneath the desk and began, very quietly, to count the tremors.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: it,
it
it;
it—
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "No one"이고 본동사는 "said"이다. 그 사이에 쉼표로 시작하는 비필수 삽입 요소 "not even the minister's son"과 "who noticed everything and repeated most of it"이 들어가 있으므로, 여는 쉼표에 맞춰 쉼표로 닫아야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 닫는 쉼표가 없어서 "it said"가 하나로 붙어 읽히고, 그 결과 주어와 동사의 연결이 흐려진다. C의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데, 앞부분에는 본동사가 없어 독립절이 아니다. D의 대시는 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 닫을 수 없으므로 부호의 짝이 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is "No one," and its main verb is "said." Between them are two nonessential elements, "not even the minister's son" and "who noticed everything and repeated most of it." Both open with commas, so they have to close with a comma before the verb. That makes A correct. B leaves out the closing comma, so "it said" runs together and the subject–verb link gets blurred. C uses a semicolon, which needs an independent clause on both sides, but the part before the blank has no main verb yet. D uses a dash, which can't close an interruption that opened with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On the Scottish island, young Morag notices the schoolteacher's trembling hands before anyone speaks the word "illness" aloud.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "No one"과 본동사 "said" 사이에 쉼표로 연 두 개의 비필수 삽입 요소(동격 "not even the minister's son" + 관계절)가 들어가 있으므로 쉼표로 닫는 A가 유일하게 옳다. B는 닫는 부호 누락, C는 앞부분이 독립절이 아니므로 세미콜론 불가, D는 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫아 짝이 맞지 않는다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 A와 선택지 참조가 일치하고 논리가 정확하다. 긴 삽입 구조 속에서 주어-동사를 찾아야 하므로 medium에 적합하며, B·D가 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. 지문은 자체 창작으로 보여 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 삽입구가 길고 관계절과 중첩되어 있어 정답을 고르려면 주어와 동사를 추적해야 한다. 그래서 중간 난이도에 맞다. 대시와 쉼표를 짝짓는 오답도 그럴듯하다.

problem.passage:
Bjorn worked beside the old man on the cold planks of the Húsavík pier, and neither of them spoke as they mended the torn net. Gunnar, who had fished these waters for fifty-one years and would sell his boat on Monday, tied each knot slowly, pulling it tight with a small grunt of ______ watched his mentor's hands and copied every motion, as if memorizing them were the only farewell he was allowed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Bjorn worked beside the old man on the cold planks of the Húsavík pier, and neither of them spoke as they mended the torn net. Gunnar, who had fished these waters for fifty-one years and would sell his boat on Monday, tied each knot slowly, pulling it tight with a small grunt of ______ watched his mentor's hands and copied every motion, as if memorizing them were the only farewell he was allowed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: satisfaction, Bjorn
satisfaction; Bjorn
satisfaction, and Bjorn,
satisfaction Bjorn
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Gunnar ... tied each knot ... satisfaction"은 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "Bjorn watched ... allowed"도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 쉼표+and는 맞지만 주어 Bjorn과 동사 watched 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 이어 run-on 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, "Gunnar ... tied each knot ... satisfaction," is a complete independent clause, and "Bjorn watched ... allowed" is another one. You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C correctly uses a comma plus "and," but it puts an unnecessary comma between the subject "Bjorn" and its verb "watched." D has no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — An Icelandic port fisherman, Bjorn, helps his mentor salvage one last net before the old man retires, each knot a wordless goodbye.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 "Gunnar ... tied each knot ... satisfaction"(분사구 포함)과 뒤 "Bjorn watched ... allowed"는 모두 독립절이며, 세미콜론(B)으로 연결하는 것이 적절함을 직접 확인. A는 comma splice, C는 주어-동사 사이 불필요한 쉼표, D는 run-on. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 선택지 참조가 정확하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 긴 삽입절(who ... Monday)과 분사구가 첫 절의 독립성 판단을 요구하고, C가 '쉼표+and'로 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합. 원작 창작 지문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 삽입절(who had fished... Monday)과 분사구(pulling...) 때문에 주절 범위를 찾는 데 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. C는 쉼표+and라는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 갖춘 매력적인 오답이다. 중간 난이도로 적절하다.

The stranger in the gray overcoat, a man she had last seen as the boy who read Neruda aloud on her aunt's lakeside dock every evening during the summer of 1924______ lifted his eyes from his newspaper and quietly said her name.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The stranger in the gray overcoat, a man she had last seen as the boy who read Neruda aloud on her aunt's lakeside dock every evening during the summer of 1924______ lifted his eyes from his newspaper and quietly said her name.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The stranger in the gray overcoat"이고 동사는 "lifted"이다. 그 사이에 쉼표로 시작하는 긴 동격어구 "a man she had last seen ... 1924"가 끼어 있다. 비필수 동격어구는 앞뒤를 같은 부호로 닫아야 하므로 쉼표가 필요하고, 따라서 정답은 C이다. A의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데, 이 문장에서는 주어와 동사를 갈라놓을 뿐이다. B의 대시는 동격어구를 닫을 수는 있지만 여는 부호가 쉼표여서 짝이 맞지 않고, D의 콜론은 앞부분이 완전한 절이 아니며 주어와 동사 사이에 올 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is "The stranger in the gray overcoat," and its verb is "lifted." Between them is a long appositive that starts with a comma: "a man she had last seen ... 1924." A nonessential appositive has to be closed with the same mark that opened it, so a comma is needed, and C is correct. A is wrong because a semicolon needs an independent clause on each side, and here it would just split the subject from its verb. B is wrong because a dash could close an appositive, but this one opens with a comma, so the marks don't match. D is wrong because a colon has to follow a complete clause, and it can't go between a subject and its verb.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The stranger in the gray overcoat"와 동사 "lifted" 사이에 쉼표로 열린 긴 동격어구가 끼어 있으므로 쉼표로 닫아야 함(C). 세미콜론·콜론은 주어-동사 사이에 올 수 없고, 대시는 여는 부호와 짝이 맞지 않음. 해설(한/영) 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 긴 동격어구 때문에 여는 쉼표를 찾아야 하고 대시(B)가 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하므로 medium 적합. 창작 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 동격어구 때문에 여는 쉼표를 놓치기 쉽고, 대시가 그럴듯한 오답이라 비교가 필요하다. 표준 medium 수준의 쉼표 짝 맞추기 문항이다. 네루다의 1924년 시집 출간 시기와도 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Kipchoge leaned forward from the back bench of the matatu as it idled near the Kencom stage. The driver, his fingers blackened with engine grease and a toothpick rolling slowly between his lips, ______ a coil of copper wire salvaged from an old doorbell through the radio's cracked faceplate and fastened it in place with a strip torn from a faded football scarf. Every part, Kipchoge realized, carried some earlier life of the van.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Kipchoge leaned forward from the back bench of the matatu as it idled near the Kencom stage. The driver, his fingers blackened with engine grease and a toothpick rolling slowly between his lips, ______ a coil of copper wire salvaged from an old doorbell through the radio's cracked faceplate and fastened it in place with a strip torn from a faded football scarf. Every part, Kipchoge realized, carried some earlier life of the van.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: threaded
threading
who threaded
having threaded
problem.explanation: 주어 "The driver" 뒤에 긴 독립 분사구문(his fingers ... his lips)이 삽입되어 있어 문장의 본동사가 빈칸에 와야 한다. 또한 빈칸 뒤의 "and fastened"와 병렬을 이루려면 과거형 정동사가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 분사 형태여서 문장에 본동사가 없게 되고 "fastened"와 병렬도 맞지 않는다. C는 관계절을 만들어 "threaded"와 "fastened"를 모두 관계절 안에 넣어 버리므로 주어 "The driver"의 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject "The driver" is followed by a long interrupting phrase (his fingers ... his lips), so the blank has to supply the sentence's main verb. It also needs to be parallel with "and fastened" after the blank, and that calls for a past-tense finite verb, so A is correct. B and D are participles, so with either one the sentence has no main verb, and neither lines up with "fastened." C makes a relative clause that pulls both "threaded" and "fastened" inside it, which leaves "The driver" without a main verb and turns the sentence into a fragment.

problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The letter'이고, 'from the master leatherworkers of Florence'와 'with its two neat folds...' 같은 수식어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 그래서 문장에는 단수 주어와 일치하면서 과거 시제 서술('had worked', 'arrived', 'scraped')과도 맞는 정동사가 필요하다. Choice D, the past tense of "lie," meets both requirements. Choice A is a finite verb, but it's a plural present-tense form, so it doesn't match a singular subject or the past-tense story. Choice B is a participle, so the sentence would have no main verb. Choice C is a perfect tense, but "have" is plural and doesn't agree with "letter."

problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the rake'이고, 'along with the apologies...'는 삽입된 수식어구라서 동사의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. 또 지문 전체가 과거 시제(had borrowed, passed)로 서술되므로 동사도 과거형이어야 한다. 단수 주어와 과거 시제를 모두 만족하는 것은 C 'stayed'이다. A는 과거 시제지만 복수형 'were'이므로 틀리고, B는 복수형이면서 현재완료라 과거 서술과 맞지 않는다. D는 복수 현재형이라 수와 시제가 모두 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the rake." The phrase "along with the apologies..." is just an interrupting modifier, so it doesn't change the number of the verb. The passage is also told in the past tense (had borrowed, passed), so the verb needs to be in the past tense too. Choice C, "stayed," is the only option that fits both a singular subject and the past-tense narration. A is past tense, but "were" is plural; B is a plural present perfect that clashes with the past-tense narration; and D is a plural present-tense form, so it's wrong on both number and tense.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Across the stoop's worn boards, young Michael borrows a rake from aging Mr. Kowalski and keeps it through six winters, never finding the courage to return it.

hardJudge.note: 주어 'the rake'(단수) + 'along with...' 삽입구 처리 + 과거 시제 서술이라는 두 단계 판단 구조. A/B/D는 모두 복수형이라 C만 단수 주어와 일치하며, 과거 시제 서술과도 부합한다. 해설(한·영)은 정답과 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순이 없으며 영어 해설에 한글이 없다. 다만 오답 3개가 모두 수 불일치로 한 번에 배제되어 '시제' 판단은 보조적 단서에 그친다는 점에서 상위 medium보다는 전형적 medium 수준이다.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 수 일치(along with 삽입구 함정)와 과거 시제 확인을 모두 거쳐야 하는 두 단계 판단 문항이다. A는 시제 근거가, B·D는 각각 부분적인 근거가 있어 오답 설계가 적절하다. 'stayed'는 수에 따라 형태가 바뀌지 않는 형태이지만, 해설의 설명은 그래도 타당하다.

problem.passage:
The matatu lurched away from the stage on Moi Avenue, its speakers thumping, and Kamau recognized the man climbing aboard before he recognized the reason his chest had tightened. It was Otieno, who had shared his desk at the insurance office for six years, and beside him was a woman in a green headscarf, her hand resting lightly on his arm in the way Kamau's own wife once rested hers on his. Pressing his shoulder against the cold window and pretending to study the traffic outside, ______ while the woman laughed at something Otieno said and neither of them glanced toward the back row.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The matatu lurched away from the stage on Moi Avenue, its speakers thumping, and Kamau recognized the man climbing aboard before he recognized the reason his chest had tightened. It was Otieno, who had shared his desk at the insurance office for six years, and beside him was a woman in a green headscarf, her hand resting lightly on his arm in the way Kamau's own wife once rested hers on his. Pressing his shoulder against the cold window and pretending to study the traffic outside, ______ while the woman laughed at something Otieno said and neither of them glanced toward the back row.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the face of his former colleague was something Kamau watched in the smudged glass,
Kamau's eyes followed his former colleague's reflection in the smudged glass,
the smudged glass held a reflection of his former colleague for Kamau to watch,
Kamau watched his former colleague's reflection in the smudged glass,
problem.explanation: 문장 앞의 분사구 'Pressing his shoulder ... and pretending to study the traffic'은 어깨를 창문에 기대고 바깥 교통을 보는 척하는 사람, 즉 Kamau를 수식하므로 쉼표 바로 뒤에는 주어 Kamau가 와야 한다. D는 Kamau를 주어로 두어 수식 관계가 정확하다. B는 Kamau를 언급하지만 주어가 'Kamau's eyes'라서 눈이 어깨를 기대고 척하는 것이 되어 어색하다. A는 동료의 얼굴이, C는 유리창이 그 행동을 하는 것처럼 되어 수식어가 잘못 연결된다.
problem.explanationEn: The introductory phrase "Pressing his shoulder against the cold window and pretending to study the traffic outside" describes someone who leans and pretends, which is Kamau, so the subject right after the comma has to be Kamau himself. D does this, so the modifier attaches correctly. B is tempting because it mentions Kamau, but its subject is "Kamau's eyes," and eyes can't press a shoulder or pretend. A makes the colleague's face the one doing the action, and C makes the glass do it, so both leave the modifier dangling.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On the matatu, Kamau's former colleague boards with a woman who could be his wife from the life he abandoned, and neither acknowledges the other's existence.

hardJudge.note: Dangling-modifier item. Only D places Kamau as the subject after the participial phrase; B ("Kamau's eyes") is the classic possessive trap, A and C make the face/glass the agent. Korean and English explanations agree, reference correct letters, and are accurate. Original-looking prose, no copyright concern. Medium-appropriate.

advisory.note: 현수 수식어 문항. 정답 D 맞음. B(소유격 함정)가 그럴듯한 오답이고, A와 C는 수동적·우회적 구문이라 배제하기 쉽다. 중간 난이도로 적절하다.

problem.passage:
The depot sat so high in the pass that snow lingered on the tracks well into April. Javier had come there with his mother and two younger sisters intending to stay only until the road below reopened. Limping across the platform with one paw held off the frozen boards, ______ That night the family made room for it beside the stove, and by the time the road cleared, no one spoke of leaving.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The depot sat so high in the pass that snow lingered on the tracks well into April. Javier had come there with his mother and two younger sisters intending to stay only until the road below reopened. Limping across the platform with one paw held off the frozen boards, ______ That night the family made room for it beside the stove, and by the time the road cleared, no one spoke of leaving.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the stray dog caught Javier's eye just as the last train of the evening pulled away.
Javier noticed the stray dog just as the last train of the evening pulled away.
the stray dog, catching Javier's eye just as the last train of the evening pulled away.
the stray dog's thin frame caught Javier's eye just as the last train of the evening pulled away.
problem.explanation: 도입 분사구 "Limping ... boards"의 의미상 주어는 다리를 저는 개여야 하므로 주절 주어는 'the stray dog'여야 하며, 동시에 문장에는 정동사가 있어야 한다. A는 주어 'the stray dog'와 정동사 'caught'를 모두 갖추어 정답이다. B는 정동사가 있지만 절뚝이는 주체가 Javier가 되어 수식어가 잘못 연결된다. C는 주어는 맞지만 'catching'이 분사여서 정동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다. D는 정동사는 있으나 주어가 'thin frame'(마른 몸)이 되어 몸이 앞발을 들고 절뚝인다는 비논리적 수식이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The opening phrase "Limping across the platform with one paw held off the frozen boards" has to describe the limping dog, so the main clause needs "the stray dog" as its subject. The sentence also needs a finite verb. Choice A has both: the subject "the stray dog" and the verb "caught," so it's correct. Choice B has a proper verb, but it makes Javier the one limping, which is a dangling modifier. Choice C has the right subject, but "catching" is a participle, so the sentence has no main verb and becomes a fragment. Choice D has a finite verb, but its subject is the dog's "thin frame," which illogically says the frame was limping with a paw held up.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At the mountain depot, Javier adopts a dog limping through the station, and his family's temporary shelter becomes permanent in ways no one anticipated.

hardJudge.note: 도입 분사구 "Limping ... with one paw held off" 의 의미상 주어는 개여야 하고 주절에 정동사가 필요함. A만 'the stray dog' + 'caught'를 갖춤. B는 현수수식어, C는 정동사 없는 단편, D는 소유격 'thin frame'이 주어가 되어 비논리적. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 글자와 결론이 일치하며 정확함. 두 단계 판단(수식어 논리 + 문장 완결성)과 그럴듯한 오답 구성으로 medium에 적합. 지문은 창작물로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 현수 수식어 문제와 정동사 유무 판단을 함께 요구한다. B와 D는 각각 그럴듯한 근거가 있어 비교해야 배제된다. 표준 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
On the rooftop, where the monsoon rain drummed against the tin awning, Priya kept the vigil her mother had asked of her. The promise to wait, whispered to her mother and her two aunts over the sputtering wicks of the oil lamps, ______ heavier now that the letter from her estranged father lay damp in her lap, its final line insisting that she choose before the rains ended.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: On the rooftop, where the monsoon rain drummed against the tin awning, Priya kept the vigil her mother had asked of her. The promise to wait, whispered to her mother and her two aunts over the sputtering wicks of the oil lamps, ______ heavier now that the letter from her estranged father lay damp in her lap, its final line insisting that she choose before the rains ended.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: seem
seemed
were seeming
seeming
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The promise'이고, 'whispered ... oil lamps'는 주어를 꾸미는 분사구이므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하다. 지문 전체가 과거 시제(drummed, kept, lay)로 서술되므로 B의 'seemed'가 수와 시제 모두 맞다. A의 'seem'은 바로 앞의 복수 명사(aunts, lamps)에 끌린 복수형이자 현재형이라 틀린다. C의 'were seeming'은 과거 시제지만 복수 동사라 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. D의 'seeming'은 분사여서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The promise." The phrase "whispered ... oil lamps" is a participial modifier describing that subject, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. The whole passage is told in the past tense (drummed, kept, lay), so B, "seemed," fits in both number and tense. A, "seem," is plural and present tense; it agrees with the nearby plural nouns (aunts, lamps) instead of the real subject. C, "were seeming," is past tense, but it's plural, so it doesn't agree with "promise." D, "seeming," is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — During the monsoon vigil on the rooftop, Priya's mother makes her promise to wait, but the letter from her estranged father arrives now demanding she decide.

hardJudge.note: 주어 'The promise'(단수) + 긴 분사 수식구(복수 명사 aunts, lamps로 끝남) 뒤 정동사 자리. 과거 서술(drummed, kept, lay)이므로 'seemed'가 수·시제 모두 적합. A는 근접 명사 끌림 오답, C는 시제는 맞지만 복수, D는 비정형으로 정동사 부재. 수 일치 + 시제 확인의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 오답 구성도 기준에 부합하여 medium 적합. 해설 한·영 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 분사구가 끼어 있고 그 안에 복수 명사(aunts, lamps)가 있어 수 일치 판단이 흐려진다. 여기에 과거 시제 문맥까지 확인해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. A와 C는 각각 수나 시제 중 하나에서만 걸러지므로 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Breaker Room is a 2019 novel by South Korean writer Han Ji-woo.
- Its main character, Min, is a 28-year-old accountant who labels every drawer and shelf in her Seoul apartment.
- In the novel's central scene, a citywide blackout leaves Min's apartment complex dark for six hours.
- Searching for candles by touch, Min opens an unlabeled box that she had taped shut years earlier.
- The box holds letters from an older brother whom Min has told her coworkers she never had.
- Reviewers have praised Han's spare, precise prose.

The student wants to explain how the novel's central scene upsets the main character's carefully arranged life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Breaker Room is a 2019 novel by South Korean writer Han Ji-woo.
- Its main character, Min, is a 28-year-old accountant who labels every drawer and shelf in her Seoul apartment.
- In the novel's central scene, a citywide blackout leaves Min's apartment complex dark for six hours.
- Searching for candles by touch, Min opens an unlabeled box that she had taped shut years earlier.
- The box holds letters from an older brother whom Min has told her coworkers she never had.
- Reviewers have praised Han's spare, precise prose.
problem.question: The student wants to explain how the novel's central scene upsets the main character's carefully arranged life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In The Breaker Room, a 2019 novel by South Korean writer Han Ji-woo, Min is a 28-year-old accountant living in Seoul, and reviewers have praised the novel's spare, precise prose.
In The Breaker Room, Min is an accountant who labels every drawer and shelf in her Seoul apartment, a habit that Han Ji-woo describes in spare, precise prose.
In The Breaker Room, Min keeps a taped box of letters from an older brother, though she has told her coworkers that she never had a brother.

In The Breaker Room, Min, who labels every drawer and shelf she owns, must search by touch during a blackout and ends up opening a long-sealed, unlabeled box of letters from a brother she has denied having.
problem.explanation: 목표는 중심 장면이 Min의 정돈된 삶을 어떻게 흔드는지 설명하는 것이므로, Min의 정돈 습관(라벨)과 정전 장면, 그리고 그 결과 드러나는 숨긴 과거를 함께 연결해야 한다. D는 이 세 요소를 모두 결합해 정답이다. A는 작품 기본 정보와 문체 평가만 제시하고 중심 장면은 다루지 않는다. B는 Min의 정돈 습관은 언급하지만 그것이 흔들리는 장면이 없다. C는 숨긴 과거(편지)는 언급하지만 정전 장면과 정돈된 삶과의 대비가 빠져 있다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain how the central scene upsets Min's carefully arranged life, so you need to connect three things: her orderly habits (the labels), the blackout scene, and the hidden past it exposes. D combines all three, so it's the correct answer. A gives only basic facts about the novel and a comment on its prose; it never mentions the central scene. B describes Min's labeling habit but leaves out the scene that disrupts it. C mentions the hidden letters but not the blackout, and it doesn't contrast them with her orderly life.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — In the Seoul apartment complex, young Min's carefully organized life erupts when the power fails and she discovers her carefully hidden past in the darkness.

hardJudge.note: D만이 정돈 습관(라벨)–정전 장면(촉각 탐색)–숨긴 과거(형제 편지) 세 요소를 연결해 '중심 장면이 정돈된 삶을 흔든다'는 목표를 충족한다. B(정돈 습관만)·C(숨긴 과거만)는 부분적으로 관련 있어 비교가 필요하고, A는 기본 정보·문체 평가로 그럴듯한 오답이다. 노트와 선택지 간 사실 불일치 없음(D의 "every drawer and shelf she owns"는 노트의 아파트 서술과 사실상 일치). 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 정확, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 소설·작가는 허구적 설정으로 저작권 문제 없음. 난이도 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 가상의 소설로 보이며 저작권 문제는 없음. D만 중심 장면(정전), 정돈 습관, 숨겨온 과거가 드러나는 일을 모두 담고 있음. B와 C는 일부 요소만 갖춘 그럴듯한 오답이고 A는 비교적 쉽게 배제됨. 중간 난이도로 적절함. D가 다른 선택지보다 눈에 띄게 길어서 길이만 보고 정답을 고를 여지가 조금 있음.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Upriver Letter" is a 2019 short story by novelist Clara Vesey.
- In the story, a steamboat clerk named Samuel travels upriver for three days to mail a single letter for his employer, Mr. Hollis.
- Samuel guards the sealed envelope carefully, sleeping with it under his pillow.
- When he reaches the post office, he learns that Mr. Hollis had sent a telegram instructing the postmaster to return the letter unsent.
- Vesey has said the story explores how loyalty can be exploited by those who receive it.

The student wants to emphasize the contrast between Samuel's devotion to his task and the outcome of his journey. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Upriver Letter" is a 2019 short story by novelist Clara Vesey.
- In the story, a steamboat clerk named Samuel travels upriver for three days to mail a single letter for his employer, Mr. Hollis.
- Samuel guards the sealed envelope carefully, sleeping with it under his pillow.
- When he reaches the post office, he learns that Mr. Hollis had sent a telegram instructing the postmaster to return the letter unsent.
- Vesey has said the story explores how loyalty can be exploited by those who receive it.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize the contrast between Samuel's devotion to his task and the outcome of his journey. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although Samuel guards Mr. Hollis's letter so closely that he sleeps with it under his pillow, he arrives at the post office to find that Mr. Hollis had already arranged for it to be returned unsent.
Although Samuel is only a steamboat clerk, he travels upriver for three days to mail a single letter for Mr. Hollis, sleeping with the sealed envelope under his pillow.
Although Clara Vesey is known as a novelist, her 2019 short story "The Upriver Letter" follows a clerk who learns at a post office that his employer's letter will be returned unsent.
Although "The Upriver Letter" centers on a clerk's three-day journey to mail a letter, Vesey has said the story explores how loyalty can be exploited by those who receive it.
problem.explanation: 목표는 Samuel이 임무에 보인 헌신과 여정의 결과를 대조하는 것이다. A는 편지를 베개 밑에 두고 잘 만큼 지켰다는 헌신과, 고용주가 이미 반송을 지시해 두었다는 결과를 함께 제시하므로 정답이다. B는 헌신만 보여 주고 여정의 결과가 빠져 있다. C는 결과는 언급하지만 대조의 축이 작가의 경력(소설가 대 단편)이라 Samuel의 헌신이 드러나지 않는다. D는 줄거리와 작가의 주제 의도를 대조할 뿐, Samuel의 헌신과 실제 결과를 구체적으로 맞세우지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to contrast Samuel's devotion to his task with how his journey turns out. A does both: it shows his devotion (he sleeps with the letter under his pillow) and the outcome (Mr. Hollis had already arranged for the letter to be returned unsent), so A is correct. B shows only his devotion and leaves out the outcome. C mentions the outcome, but its contrast is about Vesey's career (novelist vs. short story), so Samuel's devotion never shows up. D contrasts the plot with the author's stated theme instead of setting Samuel's devotion against what actually happens.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Steamboat clerk Samuel journeys upriver for three days to mail a single letter, only to learn his employer never intended to send it.

hardJudge.note: A alone pairs Samuel's devotion (sleeping with the letter under his pillow) with the outcome (letter returned unsent). B gives devotion only; D gives theme vs. plot without the outcome; C shifts the contrast to the author's career. Distractors require comparison; difficulty appropriate for medium. Fictional source, no copyright concern.

advisory.note: A만 헌신과 결과를 모두 담음. B는 헌신만, C·D는 대조 축이 다름. 오답 각각에 부분 근거가 있어 medium 난이도에 적합.

problem.stimulus:

A는 작품 소개·배경은 있으나 이미지 없음, C는 소문 확산 과정만 있고 냄새 이미지·의미 누락(또한 '거의 모든 주민'은 노트에 없는 확장), D는 비평가 언급만 있고 배경 이야기. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 가상 작품으로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음. 오답 중 A·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하며 D도 말이 되므로 medium 적합(다소 평이한 편이나 표준 범위).

advisory.note: 냄새라는 감각적 이미지를 언급하는 선택지가 B 하나뿐이라, 'sensory image'라는 키워드만 찾아도 바로 답이 나온다. 오답들이 냄새 이미지는 넣고 그 의미를 빠뜨리거나, 의미만 넣고 이미지는 빠뜨리는 식으로 부분적인 근거를 갖고 있지 않아 비교할 필요가 없다. 그래서 medium 기준(두 단계 판단)에 미치지 못한다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Southern Wind is a 2019 novel by Argentine author Lucía Marín Ortega.
- The novel is set on an isolated sheep ranch in Patagonia.
- Its protagonist, Elena, is a shepherd who has never traveled beyond the ranch.
- During lambing season, Elena meets Tomás, a traveling veterinarian who tells her about the cities where he has worked.
- After Tomás leaves the ranch, Elena begins setting aside her wages for a bus ticket to Buenos Aires.

The student wants to describe how a particular encounter in the novel affects the protagonist. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

problem.question: The student wants to describe how a particular encounter in the novel affects the protagonist. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Marín Ortega's Southern Wind, shepherd Elena meets a traveling veterinarian named Tomás during lambing season on an isolated Patagonian sheep ranch.
In Marín Ortega's Southern Wind, shepherd Elena, who has never traveled beyond the ranch, spends lambing season on an isolated sheep ranch in Patagonia.
In Marín Ortega's Southern Wind, after a traveling veterinarian describes the cities where he has worked, shepherd Elena starts saving her wages for a bus ticket to Buenos Aires.
In Marín Ortega's 2019 novel Southern Wind, Tomás is a traveling veterinarian who has worked in several cities before arriving at a Patagonian ranch.
problem.explanation: 목표는 만남이 주인공에게 미친 영향을 설명하는 것이므로, 만남(수의사가 도시 이야기를 함)과 그 결과(엘레나가 버스표를 위해 돈을 모음)를 연결해야 한다. C가 두 메모를 결합해 이를 보여 준다. A는 만남 자체만 서술하고 엘레나에게 생긴 변화는 빠져 있다. B는 엘레나의 배경과 장소만 제시해 만남이 아예 등장하지 않는다. D는 토마스에 초점을 맞춰 주인공에게 미친 영향을 말하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to show how an encounter affects the protagonist, so you need to connect the meeting (Tomás describing cities) with its result (Elena saving for a bus ticket). Choice C combines those two notes and does exactly that. Choice A describes the meeting itself but never says how Elena changes. Choice B gives Elena's background and the setting but leaves out the encounter entirely. Choice D is about Tomás, not about any effect on Elena.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — On the Patagonian ranch, shepherd Elena meets a traveling veterinarian in the lambing season, and their brief connection reshapes what she imagines possible.

hardJudge.note: C는 만남(토마스의 도시 이야기)과 결과(버스표를 위해 임금 저축)를 인과적으로 연결한 유일한 선택지로 정답이 명확하다. A는 만남 자체를 서술해 부분적으로 목표에 부합하고, D는 토마스·도시 정보를 담아 그럴듯하며, B는 배경만 제시해 가장 약한 오답이다. 해설(한·영)은 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. D의 "several cities"는 메모의 "cities"에서 나온 가벼운 추론 수준으로 문제 없음. 난이도는 표준 SAT rhetorical synthesis 중간 수준에 해당하나, 결과를 담은 선택지가 하나뿐이어서 다소 쉬운 쪽 경계에 있음.

advisory.note: 가상의 소설로 보이며 저작권 문제는 없다. 오답 A와 D는 만남을 다루고 B는 주인공을 다루므로 각각 부분적인 근거를 가진다. 정답인 C만 만남과 그 영향을 연결한다. 전형적인 중간 난이도 문항이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Third Pour" is a 2019 short story by Ethiopian writer Hiwot Alemu.
- The story takes place during a coffee ceremony, in which coffee is traditionally served in three rounds: abol, tona, and baraka.
- During the first round, Semira is handed a letter from her eldest son, Dawit, who disappeared three seasons earlier.
- Dawit wrote the letter the week before he vanished, but a cousin forgot it in a coat pocket for months.
- Semira does not open the letter until baraka, the ceremony's final round, whose name means "blessing."
- Critics argue that the story's central idea is that love can arrive late and still be fully received.

The student wants to explain how the way the scene's events are arranged supports the story's central idea. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Third Pour" is a 2019 short story by Ethiopian writer Hiwot Alemu.
- The story takes place during a coffee ceremony, in which coffee is traditionally served in three rounds: abol, tona, and baraka.
- During the first round, Semira is handed a letter from her eldest son, Dawit, who disappeared three seasons earlier.

problem.question: The student wants to explain how the way the scene's events are arranged supports the story's central idea. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Hiwot Alemu's 2019 short story "The Third Pour," Semira is handed a letter from her eldest son, Dawit, who disappeared three seasons earlier, during the first round of a coffee ceremony.
In "The Third Pour," the letter Semira receives was written by Dawit the week before he vanished, but it was delayed for months because a cousin forgot it in a coat pocket.
In "The Third Pour," a story set during a three-round coffee ceremony of abol, tona, and baraka, critics find the central idea that love can arrive late and still be fully received.
In "The Third Pour," Semira holds her son's long-delayed letter unopened until baraka, the ceremony's final "blessing" round, suggesting that love arriving late can still be fully received.
problem.explanation: 정답은 D이다. D는 Semira가 편지를 마지막 라운드인 baraka('축복')까지 열지 않는다는 사건 배치를 '늦게 도착한 사랑도 온전히 받아들여질 수 있다'는 중심 주제와 직접 연결한다. A는 작가·작품과 편지를 받는 장면만 소개할 뿐 주제와 연결하지 않는다. B는 편지가 늦어진 이유를 설명하지만 그 지연이 어떻게 주제를 뒷받침하는지는 말하지 않는다. C는 주제와 의식의 세 라운드를 모두 언급하지만, 사건의 배치(편지를 언제 여는지)가 주제를 어떻게 뒷받침하는지는 설명하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The answer is D. D links how the scene is arranged, with Semira waiting until baraka, the final "blessing" round, to open the letter, to the story's central idea that late-arriving love can still be fully received. A introduces the author and the moment Semira gets the letter, but it never connects anything to the theme. B explains why the letter was delayed, but it doesn't say how that delay supports the central idea. C mentions both the theme and the ceremony's three rounds, but it doesn't show how the order of events, especially when Semira opens the letter, supports that theme.

quality.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — At the coffee ceremony, Semira receives a letter from her eldest son, written before he disappeared three seasons ago, and must decide what to do with delayed love.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산: 과제는 '사건 배치(편지를 언제 여는지)가 중심 주제를 어떻게 뒷받침하는가'를 설명하는 것. D만이 '마지막 라운드 baraka(축복)까지 열지 않음'이라는 배치를 '늦게 온 사랑도 온전히 받아들여짐'이라는 주제와 명시적으로 연결함. A는 사건만 서술(주제 없음), B는 지연 원인만 서술(주제 없음), C는 주제와 세 라운드를 모두 언급하지만 사건 배치와의 연결이 없어 가장 강한 오답으로 기능. 오답 중 B·C가 부분적 근거를 가지며 A도 말이 됨 → medium 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 가상의 작품이지만 노트의 커피 의식 3라운드(abol, tona, baraka) 및 baraka='축복' 의미는 실제와 부합하여 사실 오류 없음. 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 D뿐이다. 오답 B와 C는 각각 지연과 주제·의식 구조를 다뤄 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 갖고 있어, medium 난이도로 적절하다. 다만 C는 문장 구조가 약간 어색하다("a story set during..., critics find"). 가상의 작품으로 보인다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Second Horn" is a short story by the fictional author Mira Hollenbeck, published in 2019.
- In the story, Dietrich is the reserved French horn player in a village brass band.
- A newcomer named Klaus joins the band and plays the tuba without ever mentioning his past.
- Band members whisper that Klaus once performed professionally with an orchestra in Berlin.
- Dietrich begins to wonder what silence or loss led Klaus to leave the city for a small village.
- Hollenbeck has said the story explores how people carry unspoken histories.

The student wants to present the central mystery that occupies Dietrich's thoughts in the story. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

- "The Second Horn" is a short story by the fictional author Mira Hollenbeck, published in 2019.
