problem.passage:
Medieval scholastic philosophers argued at length over the status of universals—general terms such as "red" or "horse." Realists held that such terms name features that really exist in many individual things, while nominalists like William of Ockham insisted that only particular things exist and that general terms are merely labels we apply to groups of them. Historians long treated the dispute as a closed chapter of theology, of interest mainly for what it reveals about the medieval church.

Linguist and historian of ideas Mira Castell contends that this view misses how closely the old debate anticipates modern research on categorization. When cognitive scientists ask whether color categories reflect boundaries in the physical world or boundaries drawn differently by each language, Castell notes, they are restating the realist and nominalist positions in experimental form. In her account, the medieval arguments are not museum pieces but early versions of questions that laboratories are still trying to settle.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus:
Medieval scholastic philosophers argued at length over the status of universals—general terms such as "red" or "horse." Realists held that such terms name features that really exist in many individual things, while nominalists like William of Ockham insisted that only particular things exist and that general terms are merely labels we apply to groups of them. Historians long treated the dispute as a closed chapter of theology, of interest mainly for what it reveals about the medieval church.

Linguist and historian of ideas Mira Castell contends that this view misses how closely the old debate anticipates modern research on categorization. When cognitive scientists ask whether color categories reflect boundaries in the physical world or boundaries drawn differently by each language, Castell notes, they are restating the realist and nominalist positions in experimental form. In her account, the medieval arguments are not museum pieces but early versions of questions that laboratories are still trying to settle.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Castell argues that modern color experiments have finally shown that the nominalist position on general terms was correct.
Castell argues that historians have studied the medieval debate over general terms mainly to understand the beliefs of the medieval church.
Castell argues that Ockham's view of general terms was more influential in medieval theology than the realist position was.
Castell argues that a medieval dispute often seen as purely historical raises issues that researchers continue to investigate.
problem.explanation: 지문은 보편자 논쟁이 신학의 닫힌 장으로 여겨져 왔지만, Castell은 이 논쟁이 오늘날 범주화 연구가 여전히 풀려는 질문을 미리 제기했다고 본다는 내용이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 색채 실험을 언급하지만 지문은 실험실이 아직 이 문제를 '해결하려 하고 있다'고 했을 뿐 유명론이 옳다고 판명되었다고 하지 않는다. B는 첫 단락에 나오는 역사가들의 견해일 뿐이고, Castell은 오히려 그 견해를 반박한다. C는 Ockham이 언급되긴 하지만 두 입장의 영향력을 비교하는 내용은 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that historians have treated the debate over universals as a closed chapter of theology, but Castell argues that it anticipates questions modern categorization research is still trying to answer, so D is correct. A picks up on the color experiments, but the text says labs are still trying to settle the question, not that they proved nominalism right. B describes the historians' view from the first paragraph, which is the view Castell actually argues against. C mentions Ockham, but the text never compares how influential the two positions were.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The philosophical problem of universals in medieval scholasticism and linguistic categorization debates

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 지문의 핵심(역사가들의 '닫힌 장' 견해 vs Castell의 '여전히 연구 중인 질문' 주장)을 정확히 요약함. A는 색채 실험이라는 지문 세부를 차용하되 '해결하려 하고 있다'를 '해결했다'로 왜곡해 정독 여부를 가르는 좋은 오답, B는 지문에 실제 나오는 역사가들의 견해를 Castell의 주장으로 귀속시킨 오답으로 부분적 근거를 가짐. C는 Ockham 언급을 이용하지만 지문에 없는 비교로 비교적 쉽게 배제됨. 두 단락의 대비를 연결해야 하는 구조로 medium에 적합. 보편자 논쟁·Ockham 유명론 서술은 사실에 부합하며 Castell은 가상의 인물로 보임. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 참조와 결론이 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: D는 지문의 대조 구조(역사가들의 '닫힌 장'이라는 견해 vs. Castell의 '현재도 이어지는 질문'이라는 주장)를 정확히 요약한다. A는 색채 실험 세부를 왜곡해 과장하고, B는 첫 단락의 역사가 견해를 Castell의 주장으로 잘못 돌린다(부분적 근거가 있음). C는 지문에 없는 영향력 비교를 끌어들인다. 오답 대부분이 지문 세부에 기대고 있어 medium 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
In the early 1900s, many American critics treated ragtime as disposable entertainment—music for saloons and dance halls, unworthy of comparison with the European concert tradition. Scott Joplin's piano rags complicate that judgment. His "Maple Leaf Rag" (1899) follows a carefully balanced multi-strain design, with each sixteen-measure section returning and contrasting in a plan as deliberate as that of a classical march or rondo. __Joplin himself printed a warning on several of his scores that ragtime should never be played fast, insisting that the syncopations needed a measured tempo to be heard clearly.__ That instruction suggests that Joplin regarded his rags not as improvised novelties but as fixed compositions whose structure performers were obligated to respect—precisely the attitude critics reserved for "serious" music.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the early 1900s, many American critics treated ragtime as disposable entertainment—music for saloons and dance halls, unworthy of comparison with the European concert tradition. Scott Joplin's piano rags complicate that judgment. His "Maple Leaf Rag" (1899) follows a carefully balanced multi-strain design, with each sixteen-measure section returning and contrasting in a plan as deliberate as that of a classical march or rondo. __Joplin himself printed a warning on several of his scores that ragtime should never be played fast, insisting that the syncopations needed a measured tempo to be heard clearly.__ That instruction suggests that Joplin regarded his rags not as improvised novelties but as fixed compositions whose structure performers were obligated to respect—precisely the attitude critics reserved for "serious" music.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a performance practice that critics cited as proof that ragtime was mere dance-hall entertainment.
It presents a detail about Joplin's scores that the text then uses to support a claim about how he viewed his own work.
It introduces a technical feature of ragtime's form that the text then compares with the structure of classical marches.
It offers evidence that Joplin's rags were more difficult to perform than the classical works favored by critics.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 Joplin이 악보에 '빠르게 치지 말라'는 지시를 적었다는 세부 사실을 제시하고, 다음 문장이 'That instruction'으로 그것을 받아 Joplin이 자기 래그를 존중받아야 할 고정된 작품으로 여겼다는 주장의 근거로 삼으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 비평가들이 래그타임을 깎아내렸다는 내용은 지문에 있지만, 그들이 이 연주 관행을 근거로 들었다는 말은 없다. C는 고전 행진곡과의 비교가 지문에 나오기는 하지만 그 비교는 밑줄 앞 문장에서 이루어지며, 밑줄 문장은 형식이 아니라 템포 지시를 다룬다. D는 연주의 난이도를 비교한 적이 없으므로 지문 범위를 넘어선다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence gives a specific detail: Joplin printed a warning on his scores not to play ragtime fast. The next sentence picks it up with "That instruction" and uses it as evidence that Joplin saw his rags as fixed compositions that deserved respect, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text does say critics looked down on ragtime, but it never says they pointed to this performance practice as proof. C is wrong because the comparison with classical marches does appear, but it comes in the sentence before the underlined one, and the underlined sentence is about a tempo instruction, not form. D is wrong because the text never compares how hard Joplin's rags are to play with classical works.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The development of ragtime musical form and Scott Joplin's compositional sophistication challenging classical hierarchy

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장(악보의 템포 경고)은 바로 다음 문장 'That instruction suggests...'가 받아 Joplin이 자기 작품을 고정된 작곡으로 여겼다는 주장의 근거가 되므로 B가 정확함. A는 비평가의 폄하(지문 내 존재)를 끌어오지만 비평가가 이 관행을 근거로 삼았다는 언급 없음, C는 고전 행진곡 비교(지문 내 존재)를 끌어오지만 그 비교는 앞 문장의 형식 설명에 속함, D는 난이도 비교 부재—오답 구조가 medium 기준 충족. 사실 관계(Maple Leaf Rag 1899, 16마디 다중 스트레인 구조, Joplin의 'Don't play this piece fast' 경고) 모두 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: Joplin의 'Do not play this piece fast' 경고는 실제 사실이다. 오답 A와 C는 지문 요소를 부분적으로 활용하고 있어 서로 비교해 봐야 배제할 수 있으므로 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In Plato's early dialogues, Socrates rarely delivers a lesson. Instead, he asks an interlocutor to define a concept such as courage or piety, then poses questions that expose contradictions in each proposed definition. Many modern instructors cite these exchanges as a model for discussion-based teaching, in which students reach understanding by answering rather than listening. __Yet the dialogues themselves seldom end in understanding: the Euthyphro, for example, closes with its title character hurrying away, no closer to defining piety than when he began.__ Some scholars argue that this unresolved ending is the point, since Socrates' aim was to replace false confidence with an awareness of one's own ignorance, an outcome that teachers who prize tidy conclusions may overlook.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In Plato's early dialogues, Socrates rarely delivers a lesson. Instead, he asks an interlocutor to define a concept such as courage or piety, then poses questions that expose contradictions in each proposed definition. Many modern instructors cite these exchanges as a model for discussion-based teaching, in which students reach understanding by answering rather than listening. __Yet the dialogues themselves seldom end in understanding: the Euthyphro, for example, closes with its title character hurrying away, no closer to defining piety than when he began.__ Some scholars argue that this unresolved ending is the point, since Socrates' aim was to replace false confidence with an awareness of one's own ignorance, an outcome that teachers who prize tidy conclusions may overlook.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives an example showing how Socrates' questions led an interlocutor to a correct definition of a concept.
It offers evidence that modern instructors have misread which dialogues best represent Socrates' method.
It identifies a flaw in Socrates' reasoning that later scholars have tried to correct.
It introduces a feature of the dialogues that complicates the way the method is often applied in classrooms.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해, 현대 교사들이 학생이 이해에 도달하는 모델로 대화편을 인용한다는 앞 문장과 달리 대화편이 대개 결론 없이 끝난다는 점을 제시하며, 마지막 문장은 이 미해결이 의도된 것이고 깔끔한 결론을 중시하는 교사들이 놓칠 수 있다고 설명한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 Euthyphro가 정의에 도달하지 못했다는 내용과 반대된다. B는 교사들을 언급하지만, 교사들이 어떤 대화편을 골랐는지가 아니라 결말의 성격이 쟁점이다. C는 결론이 없다는 점을 소크라테스 추론의 결함으로 보지만, 지문은 그것이 의도된 목적일 수 있다고 본다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet." It contrasts the earlier claim that teachers use the dialogues as a model for reaching understanding with the fact that the dialogues usually end without any resolution. The final sentence then says this lack of resolution may be the point, which teachers who prize tidy conclusions may miss, so D is correct. A is wrong because Euthyphro gets no closer to a definition at all. B mentions teachers, but the issue is how the dialogues end, not which dialogues teachers chose. C treats the missing conclusion as a flaw in Socrates' reasoning, while the text suggests it may have been his aim.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The Socratic method as depicted in Platonic dialogues and its influence on philosophical pedagogy

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 전환해 교사들이 모델로 삼는 방법과 대화편의 미해결 결말 사이의 긴장을 도입하며, 마지막 문장이 이를 교사들이 놓칠 수 있는 지점으로 연결하므로 D가 정확하다. A는 Euthyphro가 정의에 도달하지 못했다는 본문과 모순, B는 '어떤 대화편'을 골랐는지가 쟁점이 아니며, C는 지문이 미해결을 의도된 목적으로 제시하므로 배제된다. B·C는 부분적 근거(교사 언급, 부정적 전환)를 가져 비교가 필요하고 A도 '예시 제시' 형식으로 그럴듯해 medium 기준에 부합. Euthyphro 결말·초기 대화편의 아포리아적 성격 등 사실 관계도 정확하다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 지지하며 선택지 참조가 일치한다.

advisory.note: To find D, the reader has to link the 'Yet' contrast to the last sentence. B and C both rest on partly true points (teachers, the unresolved ending), so they have to be compared before they can be ruled out. A contradicts the text directly, but it still makes sense as a choice. Euthyphro's ending is described accurately.

problem.passage:
Before the twelfth century, builders who wanted taller churches faced a stubborn problem: the outward thrust of a heavy stone vault could push the supporting walls apart. The flying buttress, an external half-arch that carries this thrust across open air to a massive pier standing well away from the building______ solved the problem with remarkable economy. Relieved of much of the load, walls could be made thinner and opened up for the vast stained-glass windows that define cathedrals such as Chartres.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Before the twelfth century, builders who wanted taller churches faced a stubborn problem: the outward thrust of a heavy stone vault could push the supporting walls apart. The flying buttress, an external half-arch that carries this thrust across open air to a massive pier standing well away from the building______ solved the problem with remarkable economy. Relieved of much of the load, walls could be made thinner and opened up for the vast stained-glass windows that define cathedrals such as Chartres.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , and it
; it
—it
problem.explanation: "an external half-arch ... away from the building"는 주어 "The flying buttress"를 설명하는 동격 삽입구이고, 쉼표로 시작했으므로 쉼표로 닫아야 주어와 동사 "solved"가 바로 이어진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 ", and it"으로 새 절을 만들어 앞의 "The flying buttress"가 동사 없는 주어로 남는다. C는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 불완전한 절이 되어 세미콜론을 쓸 수 없다. D는 쉼표로 연 삽입구를 대시로 닫아 짝이 맞지 않고, "it"이 주어를 중복시켜 앞부분이 역시 동사를 잃는다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "an external half-arch ... away from the building" is an appositive that describes the subject "The flying buttress." It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too, which lets the subject connect directly to its verb, "solved." That makes B correct. A uses ", and it" to start a new clause, which leaves "The flying buttress" as a subject with no verb. C puts a semicolon after an incomplete clause that has no verb, and a semicolon needs a complete clause on each side. D closes a comma-opened appositive with a dash, so the pair doesn't match, and "it" repeats the subject, which again leaves the first part without a verb.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The architectural innovation of the flying buttress in Gothic cathedral construction and engineering principles

hardJudge.note: 직접 검산: "The flying buttress, [동격구], solved ..." 구조에서 쉼표로 연 동격 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫는 B만 주어-동사 연결을 유지함. A·C·D는 모두 앞부분을 동사 없는 조각으로 남기거나(A, D) 세미콜론 앞 불완전 절(C)을 만듦. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조, 오류 없음. 사실관계(12세기 플라잉 버트레스, 샤르트르 스테인드글라스) 문제 없음. 긴 동격구로 주어-동사 거리를 벌려 훑어 읽으면 A/D에 끌리도록 설계되어 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구 안에 관계절('that carries...')과 분사구('standing...')가 들어 있어서, 주어와 동사 'solved'가 어떻게 연결되는지 끝까지 따라가야 풀린다. 오답 셋은 모두 'it'을 넣어 그럴듯한 독립절을 만든다. 다만 주어 'The flying buttress'에 동사가 없다는 점을 알아채면 모두 배제되므로, 오답 간 변별력은 다소 균일하다. 그래도 medium 수준에는 적합하다. 첫 열두 세기 이전의 건축 문제와 Chartres 관련 서술도 사실과 맞는다.

problem.passage:
In The Role of the Reader (1979), semiotician Umberto Eco distinguished between "closed" texts, which steer a reader toward a single predetermined response, and "open" texts, which invite many competing interpretations. Yet Eco, whose own scholarship ranged from medieval aesthetics to the conventions of spy novels, insisted that even the most open text has ______ a reader cannot, for example, decide that a novel set in a fourteenth-century monastery is secretly a recipe book.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In The Role of the Reader (1979), semiotician Umberto Eco distinguished between "closed" texts, which steer a reader toward a single predetermined response, and "open" texts, which invite many competing interpretations. Yet Eco, whose own scholarship ranged from medieval aesthetics to the conventions of spy novels, insisted that even the most open text has ______ a reader cannot, for example, decide that a novel set in a fourteenth-century monastery is secretly a recipe book.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: limits:
limits,
limits; and
limits, that
problem.explanation: 긴 삽입구(whose own scholarship ... spy novels)를 걷어내면 주절은 'Eco insisted that even the most open text has limits'이고, 빈칸 뒤 'a reader cannot ... decide ...'는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 뒤 절이 '한계'의 구체적 예시이므로 두 독립절을 연결하며 설명을 도입하는 콜론을 쓴 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 등위접속사 and를 덧붙여 불필요하게 이중 연결을 만든다. D는 that 뒤에 이미 완전한 절이 와서 관계절로 볼 수 없고, 비필수 쉼표 뒤의 that도 허용되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: If you set aside the long interrupting phrase (whose own scholarship ... spy novels), the main clause is "Eco insisted that even the most open text has limits," and the words after the blank, "a reader cannot ... decide ...," make up another independent clause with its own subject and verb. That second clause gives a specific example of the limits, so a colon, which joins two independent clauses and introduces an explanation, is correct, and that makes A the answer. B links two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C puts a semicolon and the conjunction "and" together, so the two clauses get joined twice. D doesn't work because "that" is followed by an already complete clause, so it can't start a relative clause, and "that" also isn't used after a comma that sets off nonessential information.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Umberto Eco's semiotics theory and the interpretation of cultural signs in postmodern textual analysis

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 'even the most open text has limits'와 뒤 'a reader cannot ... decide ...'는 모두 독립절이며 뒤 절이 앞 절의 예시이므로 콜론(A)이 적절. B는 comma splice, C는 SAT 관례상 세미콜론+and 이중 연결, D는 that 뒤 완전절로 비문. 사실관계(Eco 1979, open/closed text, 중세 미학~스파이 소설 연구)도 정확. 긴 삽입구를 걷어내고 절 구조를 파악해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 부합. 참고: C의 '; and'는 일부 문체 규범에서 내부 쉼표가 있는 절에 허용되나 SAT 기준으로는 오답으로 처리되므로 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 삽입구 때문에 주절 구조를 찾아야 하고, 뒤 절이 독립절인지도 확인해야 하는 두 단계 판단 문항이다. 오답 B(comma splice)와 C(세미콜론+and)는 부분적으로 그럴듯해 비교해야 배제된다. 사실관계(Eco, 1979년, 수도원 소설 및 첩보소설 연구 언급)에도 문제가 없다.

problem.passage:
In a fugue, a single melodic idea called the subject is introduced by one voice and then taken up, one after another, by the remaining voices. Bach's fugues in The Well-Tempered Clavier follow a strict plan of entries: the second voice, which enters a fifth higher than the first and is known as the ______ the first voice continues with a countersubject designed to fit against it.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a fugue, a single melodic idea called the subject is introduced by one voice and then taken up, one after another, by the remaining voices. Bach's fugues in The Well-Tempered Clavier follow a strict plan of entries: the second voice, which enters a fifth higher than the first and is known as the ______ the first voice continues with a countersubject designed to fit against it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: answer; meanwhile
answer, states the subject while
answer states the subject, while
answer, states the subject; while
problem.explanation: 주어 'the second voice' 뒤에 비필수 삽입절 'which enters ... known as the answer'가 쉼표로 열렸으므로, 'answer' 뒤에도 쉼표로 닫은 다음 동사 'states'가 와야 한다. 그 뒤 'while'은 종속절을 이끌므로 쉼표 없이 이어져도 된다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 삽입절을 닫지 않고 주어에 동사도 주지 않은 채 세미콜론을 써서 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 'which' 절이 끝나는 지점이 불분명하다. D는 삽입절은 바르게 닫았지만, 세미콜론 뒤 'while ...'이 종속절일 뿐이라 독립절이 아니어서 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject "the second voice" is followed by a nonessential clause, "which enters ... known as the answer," and that clause opens with a comma. So it needs a closing comma after "answer," and then the main verb "states" has to follow. "While" begins a dependent clause, so it can come right after without a comma. That makes B correct. A never closes the clause or gives the subject a verb, so the part before its semicolon isn't an independent clause. C leaves out the closing comma, so it isn't clear where the "which" clause ends. D closes the clause correctly, but the part after its semicolon ("while ...") is only a dependent clause, not an independent one, so the semicolon is wrong.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The compositional structure of fugal form in Johann Sebastian Bach's mathematical music architecture

hardJudge.note: 검산: 주어 'the second voice' + 비필수 which절(쉼표로 열림) → 'answer,'로 닫고 본동사 'states' 필요. B만 성립. A는 세미콜론 앞이 동사 없는 단편, C는 삽입절 닫는 쉼표 누락, D는 세미콜론 뒤가 종속절. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 B 및 오답 근거와 일치하며 영어 자연스러움. 푸가의 answer가 5도 위로 진입하고 첫 성부가 countersubject를 이어간다는 음악 사실도 통상 설명과 부합. 삽입절 경계 인식 + 세미콜론 규칙의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 C·D가 부분적으로 그럴듯해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B를 넣으면 'the second voice, which ... answer, states the subject while the first voice continues ...'가 되어 문법적으로 맞다. 정답을 고르려면 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 하나는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표이고, 다른 하나는 while 종속절 앞의 구두점이다. C와 D는 각각 둘 중 한 요소만 맞아서 비교해야 배제된다. 따라서 medium 난이도에 적합하다. 푸가의 answer가 5도 위에서 들어온다는 설명도 사실과 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Many art historians describe the minaret mainly as a symbol. In their view, the tall tower rising above a mosque was built to mark the building as a place of worship and to show the power of the rulers who paid for it. Its height, they argue, was about meaning, not use.

Text 2
Before loudspeakers, the muezzin had to climb the minaret five times a day to call people to prayer. Tests in old mosques show that a voice from the top of a tower travels much farther over rooftops than a voice from the ground. For this reason, the minaret's height was first of all a practical answer to the problem of being heard across a city.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the art historians' view described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Many art historians describe the minaret mainly as a symbol. In their view, the tall tower rising above a mosque was built to mark the building as a place of worship and to show the power of the rulers who paid for it. Its height, they argue, was about meaning, not use.

Text 2
Before loudspeakers, the muezzin had to climb the minaret five times a day to call people to prayer. Tests in old mosques show that a voice from the top of a tower travels much farther over rooftops than a voice from the ground. For this reason, the minaret's height was first of all a practical answer to the problem of being heard across a city.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the art historians' view described in Text 1?
options: By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because it showed the power of the rulers who paid for it
By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because it made the mosque look different from nearby homes
By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because loudspeakers later made the tower unnecessary
By arguing that the minaret's height mattered mostly because it helped the muezzin's voice reach distant listeners
problem.explanation: Text 1은 미나렛의 높이가 쓰임이 아니라 상징을 위한 것이라고 보고, Text 2는 높이가 소리를 도시 전체에 전달하는 실용적 해결책이었다고 주장하므로 정답은 D이다. A는 Text 1의 견해를 그대로 되풀이한 것이라 Text 2의 반응이 될 수 없다. B 역시 건물을 구별하는 상징적 기능으로, Text 2가 강조하는 점이 아니다. C는 Text 2가 확성기를 언급하긴 하지만 높이가 중요했던 이유로 제시한 것이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 says the minaret's height was about meaning, not use, while Text 2 says the height was mainly a practical way to make the call to prayer heard across a city, so D is correct. A just repeats Text 1's own view, so it can't be how Text 2's author would push back. B also describes a symbolic purpose (marking the building), which is not what Text 2 stresses. C mentions loudspeakers, but Text 2 brings them up only to describe the time before them, not as the reason height mattered.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The architectural symbolism of minarets in Islamic mosque design and muezzin acoustic function

hardJudge.note: Text 2의 마지막 문장("first of all a practical answer to the problem of being heard across a city")이 D를 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 Text 1 견해 반복, B는 상징적 기능, C는 확성기 세부사항 오용으로 전형적 오개념 역할을 하며 규칙(두 지문의 핵심 주장 대조)을 알면 즉시 배제된다. 한·영 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단일 단계 추론, 평이한 어휘로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: Text 2가 실용적 기능을 직접 밝히고 있어 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. A·B는 Text 1의 상징적 견해를 옮긴 오답이고, C는 지문에 나오는 단어를 이용한 함정이다. 모두 전형적인 오답 유형이다. 다만 C가 문장 구조상 다소 어색해 쉽게 배제될 수 있다. '흔히 ~로 묘사된다'는 문장과 음향 실험 부분은 지나친 일반화일 수 있지만, 사실 오류로 볼 수준은 아니다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- French poet Charles Baudelaire published the essay "The Painter of Modern Life" in 1863.
- In it, he defined modernity as "the transient, the fleeting, the contingent," which he called one half of art.
- The other half of art, he argued, is "the eternal and the immovable."

- Baudelaire believed the flâneur's task was to extract the eternal from the transitory scenes of urban life.

The student wants to explain how Baudelaire's ideal observer related the two halves of art he described. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

problem.question: The student wants to explain how Baudelaire's ideal observer related the two halves of art he described. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: For Baudelaire, the flâneur, wandering detached through city crowds, was meant to draw "the eternal and the immovable" out of the transient, fleeting scenes he observed.
For Baudelaire, the flâneur was an observer who wandered city crowds while remaining detached from the people around him.
For Baudelaire, whose essay "The Painter of Modern Life" appeared in 1863, modernity was "the transient, the fleeting, the contingent."
For Baudelaire, the flâneur rejected the fleeting scenes of the city so that he could devote himself solely to "the eternal and the immovable."
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 플라뇌르가 예술의 두 반쪽을 어떻게 연결했는지 설명하는 것이다. A는 플라뇌르라는 인물과 두 반쪽(영원한 것과 덧없는 것)을 함께 담고, 덧없는 것에서 영원한 것을 '끌어낸다'는 관계까지 보여 준다.
B: 플라뇌르에 대한 사실만 있고 예술의 두 반쪽은 빠져 있어 목표를 절반만 달성한다.
C: 출판 연도와 모더니티의 정의라는 두 사실을 합쳤지만 플라뇌르도 두 반쪽의 관계도 나오지 않아 목표와 무관하다.
D: 플라뇌르가 덧없는 장면을 '거부했다'는 내용은 노트에 없고, 오히려 그런 장면에서 영원한 것을 추출한다는 노트의 내용과 정반대여서 사실을 왜곡한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: Your goal is to explain how the flâneur connected the two halves of art. A names the flâneur and both halves (the eternal and the transient). It also states the relationship between them: he draws the eternal out of fleeting scenes.
B: This gives only the facts about the flâneur. It leaves out the two halves of art, so it meets only half of the goal.
C: This combines two facts, the essay's date and the definition of modernity. But it never mentions the flâneur or how the two halves relate, so this pairing doesn't serve the goal.
D: The notes never say the flâneur rejected fleeting scenes. In fact, they say he extracted the eternal from those scenes, so D distorts the notes.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 노트 2·3·4·5를 종합해 플라뇌르가 덧없는 것에서 영원한 것을 '추출'한다는 관계를 정확히 서술함. B는 플라뇌르 사실만(한쪽), C는 목표와 무관한 사실 조합, D는 노트에 없는 '거부'를 삽입해 관계 방향을 뒤집은 매력적 오답으로, 단순 사실 선택이 아니라 관계의 방향 판별을 요구함. 1863년 출판, 인용문 등 사실 관계도 정확. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 일관되게 설명함.

advisory.note: A는 노트 2·3·4·5를 하나로 묶어 '덧없는 것에서 영원한 것을 끌어낸다'는 관계를 정확히 보여 준다. D는 관계 방향을 거꾸로 뒤집은 매력적 오답이라 관계 방향 판별을 요구한다. 다만 정답 A만 두 반쪽을 모두 담고 있어 키워드만 대조해도 고를 수 있으므로 hard 정도는 중간보다 조금 높은 수준이다.

problem.passage:

problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how anamorphosis depended on an existing artistic method. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

Anamorphosis was rooted in Renaissance linear perspective: artists took that method's geometric projection rules and pushed them to an extreme, stretching images toward an unusually oblique viewpoint.
Anamorphosis, which emerged during the Renaissance, includes distorted images seen from one viewpoint, Holbein's hidden skull, and later images corrected by cylindrical mirrors.

problem.explanation:
정답 B: 목표는 아나모포시스가 기존 기법(선형 원근법)에 의존했다는 점을 강조하는 것이다. B는 원근법의 기하학적 투영 규칙을 극단으로 확장했다는 2·3번 메모를 결합해 그 의존 관계를 직접 보여 준다.
A: 홀바인 그림이라는 구체적 사례만 제시하는 지나치게 세부적인 문장으로, 어떤 기존 방법에 의존했는지는 말하지 않는다.
C: 정의·사례·거울 변형을 나열한 지나치게 포괄적인 개관이라 초점을 잃었고, 원근법과의 관계도 빠져 있다.
D: 목표와 무관한 후대의 거울 아나모포시스를 강조한다. 이는 기존 기법에 의존한 점이 아니라 이후의 발전에 관한 내용이다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: The goal is to emphasize that anamorphosis depended on an existing method. B connects it to Renaissance linear perspective and explains that artists pushed that method's projection rules to an extreme. This combines notes 2 and 3.
A: This is too narrow. It gives only one example, Holbein's skull, and never names the method that anamorphosis depended on.
C: This is too broad. It surveys several aspects of the technique, so it loses focus, and it leaves out linear perspective entirely.
D: This focuses on a different note. Mirror anamorphoses were a later development, so they don't show what anamorphosis grew out of.

hardJudge.note: 목표(기존 기법 의존성 강조)가 명확하고, 정답 B는 2·3번 메모를 하나의 문장으로 통합해 선형 원근법→아나모포시스의 의존 관계를 정확히 보여 준다. A는 홀바인 사례만 담은 과잉 구체, C는 정의·사례·후대 변형을 나열한 과잉 포괄(르네상스 언급으로 유인력 있음), D는 목표와 무관한 후대 발전. 홀바인 1533년 The Ambassadors·해골·원통 거울 아나모포시스 등 사실 관계도 정확. 해설은 정답·오답 모두 논리적으로 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 다만 목표→메모 2·3 매핑이 비교적 직접적이어서 hard 중에서는 난도가 높지 않은 편.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 2·3번 메모를 종합하고 있다. 다만 B만 'linear perspective'와 'method'를 언급해 목표에 쓰인 'existing artistic method'와 어휘가 바로 대응되고, 다른 선택지는 모두 원근법을 전혀 언급하지 않는다. 그래서 키워드 대응만으로 답이 정해진다. 범위를 가늠하거나 확실성 수준을 구분하는 등의 추가 사고가 필요 없어 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Early studies of stereotype threat showed that women who were reminded of a stereotype about gender and math before a test scored lower than women who were not reminded. Many researchers first assumed that the reminder simply lowered the women's motivation or confidence. Psychologist Toni Schmader and her colleagues offered a different account based on cognitive load theory. They noted that solving multistep math problems depends heavily on working memory, the limited mental space used to hold and manipulate information. In their experiments, women under threat did worse on working-memory tasks as well as on math problems, and the more working memory they lost, the lower their math scores fell. The researchers argued that worrying about confirming the stereotype and trying to suppress that worry take up mental resources the problems themselves would otherwise use. If so, a tool that lightens this extra mental work, such as teaching test takers that anxiety is a normal reaction to a hard task, should reduce the performance gap, and later studies have found that it often does.

According to the text, what did Schmader and her colleagues propose to explain why stereotype reminders hurt women's math scores?
problem.stimulus: Early studies of stereotype threat showed that women who were reminded of a stereotype about gender and math before a test scored lower than women who were not reminded. Many researchers first assumed that the reminder simply lowered the women's motivation or confidence. Psychologist Toni Schmader and her colleagues offered a different account based on cognitive load theory. They noted that solving multistep math problems depends heavily on working memory, the limited mental space used to hold and manipulate information. In their experiments, women under threat did worse on working-memory tasks as well as on math problems, and the more working memory they lost, the lower their math scores fell. The researchers argued that worrying about confirming the stereotype and trying to suppress that worry take up mental resources the problems themselves would otherwise use. If so, a tool that lightens this extra mental work, such as teaching test takers that anxiety is a normal reaction to a hard task, should reduce the performance gap, and later studies have found that it often does.
problem.question: According to the text, what did Schmader and her colleagues propose to explain why stereotype reminders hurt women's math scores?
options: The reminders mainly lowered women's motivation, which made them less willing to finish multistep problems.
The reminders made women less confident, which led them to choose easier strategies that produced more errors.
The reminders set off worry and attempts to control it, which used up mental capacity needed to solve the problems.
The reminders made the math problems themselves seem harder, which raised the amount of working memory the problems required.
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 Schmader 연구진은 고정관념을 확인하게 될까 걱정하고 그 걱정을 억누르려는 노력이 문제 풀이에 써야 할 작업 기억을 차지한다고 주장했으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 동기 저하를 말하는데, 이는 연구자들이 처음에 가정했던 설명이고 Schmader 연구진이 제시한 설명과는 다르다. B도 자신감 저하라는 초기 가정에 기대고 있으며, 더 쉬운 전략을 고른다는 내용은 지문에 나오지 않는다. D는 작업 기억이라는 개념을 쓰지만 문제의 요구량이 늘었다고 말하는데, 지문은 걱정이 가용 자원을 줄인다고 했을 뿐 문제가 요구하는 양이 늘었다고 하지 않았다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. The text says Schmader's team argued that worrying about confirming the stereotype, and trying to suppress that worry, takes up mental resources the problems would otherwise use. In 1968, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson reported that elementary students whom teachers had been told were about to "bloom" intellectually showed larger IQ gains over a school year than their classmates, even though the "bloomers" had actually been chosen at random. problem.passage:
Psychologist Lev Vygotsky argued that a child's learning is best understood not by what the child can already do alone but by the gap between that independent performance and what the child can accomplish with guidance from a more knowledgeable partner. He called this gap the zone of proximal development. Later researchers, building on his ideas, introduced the term "scaffolding" to describe the temporary support a tutor offers within that zone, such as breaking a task into steps or modeling a strategy.

Educational researchers have since cautioned that scaffolding is often misapplied. Some teachers keep the same level of help in place long after students have mastered a skill, which can make learners dependent on the support rather than independent. Researchers stress that effective scaffolding requires the tutor to watch the learner closely and withdraw assistance gradually as competence grows, so that responsibility for the task shifts to the student.

problem.passage:
In a 1968 study, psychologists John Darley and Bibb Latané had college students talk over an intercom with peers they believed were in other rooms. Partway through, one voice appeared to have a seizure. Participants who thought they were the only other listener almost always left their rooms to get help, and they usually did so quickly. Those who believed four other people were also listening responded less often and more slowly. Notably, the researchers did not find these hesitant participants indifferent: many were sweating and trembling, and they repeatedly asked whether someone was helping. Darley and Latané concluded that the presence of others does not make bystanders stop caring. Instead, it spreads the sense of obligation across the group, so each person feels less personally responsible for acting.

problem.passage:
Sociologist Pierre Bourdieu argued that schools, though officially open to all, often reward a kind of familiarity that children acquire at home rather than in the classroom. Students from educated families tend to arrive already comfortable with the vocabulary, reading habits, and tastes that teachers treat as signs of talent. Bourdieu called these assets "cultural capital." Because examiners judge such fluency as natural ability, the advantage looks earned rather than inherited.

According to Bourdieu, diplomas then turn this inherited ease into an official credential that employers and institutions recognize. A degree certifies the holder as competent, and in doing so it hides the family advantages that helped produce it. In this way, Bourdieu concluded, an education system that appears to judge merit can quietly pass social rank from one generation to the next.

Participants sort words and images as quickly as possible, and faster responses when, say, a group is paired with "pleasant" are taken to reveal an association the participant may not consciously endorse. problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 20세기의 점수 상승 추세가 뒤집힌 노르웨이·덴마크 자료를 제시하고, 이어지는 마지막 문장은 형제 비교라는 이 자료를 근거로 점수 변화가 가족 간 차이가 아니라 사회 전반의 변화에서 온다는 결론을 내린다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 반박의 느낌은 맞지만, 이 자료는 오히려 형제 비교를 통해 유전적 설명을 배제하는 쪽이라 '유전으로 설명하기엔 너무 빠르다'는 주장을 반박하지 않는다. B는 영양·교육을 언급한 앞 문장과 연결되지만, 밑줄 문장은 점수 하락을 다루며 그런 요인이 점수를 올린 사례가 아니다. C는 검사 자체의 타당성을 의심한다는 내용으로, 지문 어디에도 나오지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence opens with "Yet" and reports Norwegian and Danish data showing that the twentieth-century rise has turned into a decline. The final sentence then uses the brother comparisons from that data to conclude that score changes come from broad shifts in society, not from differences between families. That makes D the answer. A sounds right because the sentence does complicate things, but the brother data actually helps rule out genetic explanations, so it doesn't challenge the claim that the gains were too fast to be genetic. B ties into the earlier mention of nutrition and schooling, but the underlined sentence is about falling scores, not an example of those factors raising them. C claims researchers doubt the tests mean anything, and nothing in the text says that.

quality.seed: social science research — Flynn effect generational intelligence quotient increases and environmental factor debates

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 기존 상승 추세의 반전(노르웨이·덴마크 하락)을 제시하고, 형제 비교 자료가 마지막 문장의 결론(사회 전반의 변화가 원인)의 근거가 되므로 D가 정확하다. A는 '복잡하게 만든다'는 어조에 기대 유전 설명 반박으로 오독하기 쉬우나 실제로는 형제 비교가 유전 요인을 배제하므로 틀림. B는 앞 문장의 영양·교육과 연결되지만 하락을 다루므로 배제. C는 지문에 근거 없음. 사실관계(Flynn 효과, 노르웨이 형제 비교 연구, 덴마크 징집병 자료의 하락)도 실제 연구와 부합. 한·영 해설 결론·선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 반전 식별 + 다음 문장과의 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 노르웨이 형제 비교 연구(Bratsberg & Rogeberg 2018)와 일치함. 덴마크는 형제 내 분석 근거가 약간 덜 명확하지만 수용 가능한 수준. A·B는 부분 근거가 있는 매력 오답이고 C는 약한 편.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Linguistic anthropologist Elinor Ochs argued that most linguistic features do not point to social categories such as gender directly. Instead, a particle or intonation pattern first signals a stance, such as hesitancy or forcefulness, and listeners then link that stance to a social identity. On this view, a sentence-final particle used often by women in Japanese marks gentleness, and only through that stance comes to be associated with femininity.

Text 2
Some sociolinguists studying workplace talk report that certain hedges, like "sort of," are so routinely tied to junior employees that listeners infer rank the instant they hear them, with no apparent attention to stance. Yet these researchers also find that the same hedges, when used by senior managers, are heard as diplomatic rather than subordinate. That reversal suggests listeners still read the hedge first as a stance, tentativeness, whose social meaning depends on who is speaking.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Ochs' claim in Text 1 about how linguistic features come to be associated with social identities?

Text 1

Instead, a particle or intonation pattern first signals a stance, such as hesitancy or forcefulness, and listeners then link that stance to a social identity. On this view, a sentence-final particle used often by women in Japanese marks gentleness, and only through that stance comes to be associated with femininity.

Text 2
Some sociolinguists studying workplace talk report that certain hedges, like "sort of," are so routinely tied to junior employees that listeners infer rank the instant they hear them, with no apparent attention to stance. Yet these researchers also find that the same hedges, when used by senior managers, are heard as diplomatic rather than subordinate. problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Ochs' claim in Text 1 about how linguistic features come to be associated with social identities?
options: By suggesting that evidence seeming to challenge the claim, once examined more closely, actually supports it
By suggesting that evidence from workplace talk shows the claim applies to Japanese but not to English
By suggesting that evidence of listeners inferring rank instantly shows the claim to be mistaken
By suggesting that evidence about senior managers shows the claim exaggerates the importance of who is speaking
problem.explanation: Text 1의 Ochs는 언어 형태가 먼저 태도(stance)를 나타내고, 그 태도를 거쳐 사회적 정체성과 연결된다고 주장한다. Text 2는 처음에 'sort of'가 태도 없이 곧바로 직급을 나타내는 것처럼 보인다는 반례를 소개하지만, 고위 관리자가 쓰면 의미가 뒤바뀐다는 점을 들어 결국 청자가 먼저 태도를 읽는다고 결론 내리므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Text 2가 언어 간 차이를 주장하지 않으므로 틀리다. C는 Text 2 앞부분만 훑어 읽으면 고를 수 있지만, Text 2는 그 증거를 뒤집는다. D는 Text 2가 오히려 화자가 누구인지가 사회적 의미를 결정한다고 말하므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: In Text 1, Ochs claims that a linguistic feature first signals a stance, and only through that stance does it become linked to a social identity. Text 2 starts with what looks like a counterexample: "sort of" seems to signal rank right away. Then it shows that the same hedge means something different when senior managers use it, and it concludes that listeners still read stance first, so A is correct. B is wrong because Text 2 never says the claim works for one language and not another. C is tempting if you only skim the first part of Text 2, but the author goes on to reject that interpretation. D is wrong because Text 2 says the speaker's identity is what shapes the social meaning, which is the opposite of saying Ochs overstates it.

hardJudge.note: Text 2 presents an apparent counterexample (hedges indexing rank "with no apparent attention to stance") and then reverses it via the senior-manager case, concluding listeners read stance first — directly supporting Ochs' indirect-indexicality account, so A is correct. C is the skim trap (first half of Text 2 only); D borrows the phrase "who is speaking" but inverts Text 2's point; B introduces a language contrast neither text makes. Korean and English explanations agree in conclusion and letter references, English is natural with no Hangul. Ochs' indirect indexicality is accurately characterized. Two-step reasoning (track Text 2's reversal, then map to Text 1's claim) matches medium difficulty.

advisory.note: Text 2는 겉보기 반례를 제시한 뒤 이를 Ochs의 간접 지표성(indirect indexicality) 주장을 지지하는 근거로 재해석하므로 A가 명확한 정답이다. C는 앞부분만 훑어 읽은 독자를 노린 강한 오답이고, D는 '화자'라는 요소를 비틀어 비교가 필요하다. B는 상대적으로 약하지만(영어/일본어 대비) 말은 된다. 지문의 Ochs 관련 내용은 사실과 부합한다.

problem.passage:
In her influential analysis of what she called "Mock Spanish," linguistic anthropologist Jane H. Hill examined how English speakers in the United States borrow Spanish expressions such as "hasta la vista, baby" and "no problemo." Such phrases, often dismissed as harmless humor, can quietly reinforce negative stereotypes of Spanish ______ Hill argued that their playful tone depends on listeners recognizing the speakers being imitated as lazy, disorderly, or unserious.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In her influential analysis of what she called "Mock Spanish," linguistic anthropologist Jane H. Hill examined how English speakers in the United States borrow Spanish expressions such as "hasta la vista, baby" and "no problemo." Such phrases, often dismissed as harmless humor, can quietly reinforce negative stereotypes of Spanish ______ Hill argued that their playful tone depends on listeners recognizing the speakers being imitated as lazy, disorderly, or unserious.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: speakers, in fact,
speakers; in fact,
speakers, in fact;
speakers in fact,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Such phrases ... speakers"와 뒤 "Hill argued ... unserious"는 각각 독립절이다. 'in fact'는 뒤 절을 강조하는 부사구이므로 세미콜론으로 두 절을 나누고 'in fact' 뒤에 쉼표를 찍은 B가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 생긴다. C는 세미콜론 위치가 잘못되어 'in fact'가 앞 절에 붙는데, 그러면 강조 대상이 바뀌고 앞 절 끝에 어색하게 매달린다. D는 절 사이에 아무 경계 표시가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("Such phrases ... Spanish speakers") and the words after it ("Hill argued ... unserious") are both independent clauses. "In fact" is a transitional phrase that emphasizes the second clause, so the clauses should be separated by a semicolon placed before "in fact," with a comma after it. That's choice B. Choice A joins the two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. Choice C puts the semicolon after "in fact," so the phrase gets awkwardly attached to the end of the first clause and no longer introduces Hill's argument. Choice D has no boundary at all between the clauses, which makes it a run-on sentence.

quality.seed: social science research — Mock Spanish and Hill's analysis of language borrowing and ethnic stereotype reinforcement

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절이며, 전환어 'in fact'가 뒤 절을 이끄므로 "speakers; in fact," (B)가 표준 용법에 맞음. A는 쉼표 오류, D는 무종지문, C는 세미콜론 자체는 경계를 만들지만 전환어가 앞 절 끝에 붙어 SAT에서 통상 오답으로 처리하는 전형적 배치 오류(해설도 이를 '어색하게 매달린다'로 설명하여 모순 없음). Jane H. Hill의 'Mock Spanish' 분석 언급은 사실과 부합. 두 독립절 판별 + 전환어 위치 판단의 두 단계가 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 전형적인 SAT 접속부사 경계 문항이다. C도 문법상으로는 성립할 수 있지만, 'in fact'가 뒤 절의 근거를 이끄는 의미로 쓰였으므로 문맥상 배제된다. 해설에서도 그 점을 언급하고 있다. Jane Hill의 Mock Spanish 연구 내용은 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
In her 1990 book You Just Don't Understand, linguist Deborah Tannen argued that many men and women in the United States are socialized into different conversational styles: men more often use talk to negotiate status and share information ("report talk"), while women more often use it to build connection ("rapport talk"). Critics have charged that this framework reinforces stereotypes by treating gender as the sole driver of how people speak. Tannen, though, repeatedly cautioned that these patterns are tendencies observed across groups, not traits of every individual, and that factors such as region, ethnicity, and setting also shape speech. ______ her work is better read as a description of overlapping styles than as a claim that men and women speak entirely separate languages.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In her 1990 book You Just Don't Understand, linguist Deborah Tannen argued that many men and women in the United States are socialized into different conversational styles: men more often use talk to negotiate status and share information ("report talk"), while women more often use it to build connection ("rapport talk"). Critics have charged that this framework reinforces stereotypes by treating gender as the sole driver of how people speak. Tannen, though, repeatedly cautioned that these patterns are tendencies observed across groups, not traits of every individual, and that factors such as region, ethnicity, and setting also shape speech. ______ her work is better read as a description of overlapping styles than as a claim that men and women speak entirely separate languages.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
For example,
Similarly,
Thus,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 Tannen이 해당 패턴을 개인의 특성이 아닌 집단적 경향으로 보았고 다른 요인도 인정했다는 근거를 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 근거에서 나온 결론(그녀의 연구는 겹치는 스타일에 대한 기술로 읽어야 한다)을 말한다. 따라서 결과·결론을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 비평가의 주장과 대비된다는 느낌 때문에 끌리지만, 바로 앞 문장과 빈칸 뒤 문장은 대립이 아니라 같은 방향이다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 내용의 구체적 사례가 아니라 일반적 결론이므로 맞지 않는다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞과 비슷한 별개의 사실을 덧붙이는 것이 아니라 앞 내용에서 추론된 것이므로 부적절하다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives evidence: Tannen described these patterns as group tendencies, not traits of every individual, and she acknowledged other influences on speech. The sentence after the blank states the conclusion that follows from that evidence, namely that her work should be read as describing overlapping styles. So D, which signals a result or conclusion, is correct. A may tempt you because the passage does contrast Tannen with her critics, but the sentence right before the blank and the one after it point in the same direction; they don't oppose each other. B doesn't fit because the final sentence is a general conclusion, not a specific example. C doesn't fit because the final sentence is drawn from the previous point rather than added as a separate, parallel point.

quality.seed: social science research — Tannen gender discourse patterns and conversational styles between men and women communication

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞(집단적 경향·다른 요인 인정이라는 근거) → 뒤(겹치는 스타일로 읽어야 한다는 결론) 구조이므로 'Thus'가 유일하게 논리적. A는 지문 전체의 비평가-Tannen 대립 구도 때문에 훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉬운 강한 오답으로, 두 단계 판단(직전 문장과의 관계 확인)이 요구됨. B·C는 상대적으로 약하지만 말은 됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. Tannen 1990년 저서명·report/rapport talk 개념·비판 내용 모두 사실에 부합. 지문은 자체 작성된 설명문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: Thus가 앞 문장 근거→결론 관계에 정확히 맞음. Nevertheless는 비평가와의 대비 때문에 매력적 오답으로 작동하고, 문단 흐름을 따라가야 배제 가능해 medium에 적합. Tannen 저서 연도·개념(report/rapport talk)도 사실과 일치.

Many popular books claim that men and women speak in fundamentally different ways, as if each sex used its own version of a language. Linguist Deborah Cameron has challenged this idea. problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "For example," which tells you it backs up the claim right before it: Cameron's point that differences between men and women are small. It shows that a speaker's role predicts interrupting better than sex does, so A is correct. B is wrong because the example goes against the popular claim instead of supporting it. C is wrong because the text never says Cameron changed her view. D is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain why popular books are widely read.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 앞 문장의 Cameron 주장(남녀 차이는 작다)을 뒷받침하는 사례이며, 역할이 성별보다 끼어들기를 더 잘 예측한다는 내용은 A와 정확히 일치한다. B는 방향이 반대, C·D는 지문에 근거 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 A를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. advisory.note: 'For example' 단서가 직접 드러나 있고 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. B는 그럴듯한 오개념이고, C·D는 다소 약하지만 허용 범위이다. Cameron의 견해 서술은 실제 저작(The Myth of Mars and Venus)과 일치한다.

problem.passage:
In the late 1700s, philosopher Jeremy Bentham designed the Panopticon, a circular prison with a central watchtower. Because prisoners could never tell whether a guard was actually looking at them, they behaved as if they were always being watched. Centuries later, Michel Foucault argued that this design reveals how modern institutions control people: the mere possibility of being observed leads individuals to ______ their own behavior, so guards rarely need to use force.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the late 1700s, philosopher Jeremy Bentham designed the Panopticon, a circular prison with a central watchtower. Because prisoners could never tell whether a guard was actually looking at them, they behaved as if they were always being watched. Centuries later, Michel Foucault argued that this design reveals how modern institutions control people: the mere possibility of being observed leads individuals to ______ their own behavior, so guards rarely need to use force.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: exaggerate
regulate
abandon
celebrate
problem.explanation: 지문은 감시될 수 있다는 가능성만으로 수감자들이 늘 감시받는 것처럼 행동하고, 그래서 간수가 거의 힘을 쓸 필요가 없다고 말한다. 즉 사람들이 스스로 자기 행동을 통제한다는 뜻이므로 '조절하다, 통제하다'를 뜻하는 B가 정답이다. A(과장하다)는 행동을 부풀리는 것이라 스스로 통제한다는 의미와 맞지 않는다. C(포기하다)는 행동을 아예 그만둔다는 뜻이라 감시 때문에 행동을 조심한다는 내용과 어긋난다. D(찬양하다)는 감시를 통한 통제라는 맥락과 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says prisoners acted as if they were always watched, so guards rarely needed force. That means people control their own behavior, so B, "regulate," is the best fit. A, "exaggerate," would mean making their behavior bigger or more extreme, which is the opposite of keeping it in check. C, "abandon," would mean giving up their behavior completely, not adjusting it carefully. D, "celebrate," has nothing to do with the idea of control through surveillance.

quality.seed: social science research — Panopticon surveillance architecture and Foucault's disciplinary power social control mechanisms

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 'regulate'는 "behaved as if they were always being watched"와 "guards rarely need to use force"라는 직접 단서로 뒷받침되며, 오답 A/C/D는 문맥상 명확히 배제된다. 사실 관계(Bentham 1780년대 Panopticon 설계, Foucault의 『감시와 처벌』 논의)도 정확하다. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 단서가 명시적이고 어휘 평이하여 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 'regulate their own behavior'는 '스스로 통제하므로 무력이 필요 없다'는 단서 하나로 바로 고를 수 있다. 오답 중 D(celebrate)는 다소 약하지만 easy 난이도로는 받아들일 만하다. 벤담과 푸코에 관한 사실 서술도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Sociologist Pierre Bourdieu argued that social class is not only a matter of income but is also carried in the body. Through years of daily life, children absorb ways of speaking, standing, and eating from those around them. Bourdieu called this set of habits the "habitus." Because these habits feel natural rather than learned, people tend to ______ them without noticing, passing the same patterns on to the next generation and helping class differences persist.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Sociologist Pierre Bourdieu argued that social class is not only a matter of income but is also carried in the body. Through years of daily life, children absorb ways of speaking, standing, and eating from those around them. Bourdieu called this set of habits the "habitus." Because these habits feel natural rather than learned, people tend to ______ them without noticing, passing the same patterns on to the next generation and helping class differences persist.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: question
abandon
repeat
invent
problem.explanation: 지문은 습관이 학습된 것이 아니라 자연스럽게 느껴지기 때문에 사람들이 '알아차리지 못한 채' 그것을 다음 세대로 그대로 전달한다고 말하므로, 빈칸에는 '반복하다'를 뜻하는 C가 와야 한다. A는 의문을 제기한다는 뜻인데, 알아차리지 못한다는 내용과 모순된다. B는 버린다는 뜻이라 같은 패턴을 물려주고 계급 차이가 지속된다는 내용과 맞지 않는다. D는 새로 만들어낸다는 뜻이지만, 지문은 습관이 주변 사람들에게서 흡수된다고 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says these habits feel natural, so people act on them "without noticing" and pass the same patterns to the next generation. That means people keep doing the habits over and over, so C fits. A doesn't work because questioning a habit means noticing it, which goes against "without noticing." B doesn't work because dropping the habits wouldn't pass the same patterns on or keep class differences going. D doesn't work because the text says the habits are absorbed from others, not newly created.

quality.seed: social science research — Practice theory Bourdieu habitus and embodied social structures reproducing class inequality

hardJudge.note: 정답 C '반복하다'는 'without noticing', 'passing the same patterns on', 'persist'와 정확히 호응함. 오답 A(알아차림 전제), B(지속과 모순), D(흡수된 것과 모순)는 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 그럴듯함. 부르디외 하비투스 개념 서술도 사실에 부합. 한·영 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 어휘 평이하고 단서 명시적이어서 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 'without noticing'와 'passing the same patterns on'이 직접적인 단서로, 한 단계 추론만 필요함. 오답은 각각 단서 하나씩으로 배제됨. 부르디외 아비투스 설명도 정확함.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Anthropologist Josephine Powell studied carpet weaving in rural Anatolia (present-day Türkiye) from the 1970s to the 1990s.
- In many Anatolian villages, carpets were woven at home as a cottage industry.
- Women and girls did most of the knotting and weaving on household looms.
- Men usually sheared the sheep and took finished carpets to sell at town markets.
- Powell collected more than 1,000 textiles and weaving tools during her research.

The student wants to describe how tasks were split between men and women in Anatolian carpet production. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Anthropologist Josephine Powell studied carpet weaving in rural Anatolia (present-day Türkiye) from the 1970s to the 1990s.
- In many Anatolian villages, carpets were woven at home as a cottage industry.
- Women and girls did most of the knotting and weaving on household looms.
- Men usually sheared the sheep and took finished carpets to sell at town markets.
- Powell collected more than 1,000 textiles and weaving tools during her research.
problem.question: The student wants to describe how tasks were split between men and women in Anatolian carpet production. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In rural Anatolia, anthropologist Josephine Powell studied carpet weaving from the 1970s to the 1990s.
In rural Anatolia, carpets were often woven at home, making weaving a cottage industry in many villages.
In rural Anatolia, Josephine Powell collected more than 1,000 textiles and weaving tools during her research.
In rural Anatolia, women and girls did most of the knotting and weaving, while men sheared the sheep and sold the finished carpets.
problem.explanation: 목표는 카펫 생산에서 남녀가 일을 어떻게 나누었는지 설명하는 것이다. D는 여성은 매듭짓기와 직조를 맡고, 남성은 양털 깎기와 판매를 맡았다고 밝혀 남녀 양쪽의 역할을 모두 보여 준다. A는 연구 기간만 말할 뿐 분업은 언급하지 않는다. B는 직조가 가내공업이었다는 사실만 제시하고 누가 어떤 일을 했는지는 말하지 않는다. C는 Powell의 수집품에 관한 내용이라 목표와 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to describe how men and women split the work of making carpets. D does this because it says women and girls did the knotting and weaving, while men sheared the sheep and sold the carpets, so it covers both sides of the division. A only gives the years of Powell's research and says nothing about who did which tasks. B only says weaving was a cottage industry, without saying who did what. C is about Powell's collection, which has nothing to do with the goal.

quality.seed: social science research — Anatolian carpet weaving and gendered division of labor in cottage industry artisanal production

hardJudge.note: D는 노트 3·4번을 정확히 종합해 남녀 분업을 모두 서술하므로 유일한 정답. A·B·C는 노트에 근거한 사실이지만 목표(분업 설명)와 무관하여 규칙(목표 일치)을 알면 바로 배제되며, 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. 한·영 해설 모두 D 지지, 글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 노트 내용(Powell의 Anatolia 연구, 1,000점 이상 수집)은 실제 사실과 부합. 실제 College Board 문항 복제로 의심되는 점 없음. 한 단계 추론, 평이한 어휘로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 남녀 분업이라는 목표에 맞는 선택지는 D 하나뿐이다. 오답 선택지는 모두 노트에 있는 정확한 사실이지만 목표와 관련이 없어 바로 배제된다. 한 단계 추론으로 풀 수 있으므로 easy에 적합하다. 오답이 너무 쉽게 배제되는 경향이 조금 있으나 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 1991, anthropologist Jean Lave and computer scientist Etienne Wenger published Situated Learning, which introduced the concept of "legitimate peripheral participation."
- The concept describes newcomers learning a practice by first taking on small, low-risk tasks within a community and gradually moving toward full participation.
- Lave's earlier fieldwork among tailors' apprentices in Liberia documented that apprentices began by sewing buttons and hems before cutting cloth.
- A 2014 survey of 412 hospital nursing trainees found that those assigned graduated ward duties reported somewhat higher confidence than those given full duties immediately.
- The survey's authors cautioned that the confidence difference was modest and might reflect differences between hospitals rather than the training model itself.

The student wants to present the nursing study's finding with the degree of caution its authors expressed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In 1991, anthropologist Jean Lave and computer scientist Etienne Wenger published Situated Learning, which introduced the concept of "legitimate peripheral participation."
- The concept describes newcomers learning a practice by first taking on small, low-risk tasks within a community and gradually moving toward full participation.
- Lave's earlier fieldwork among tailors' apprentices in Liberia documented that apprentices began by sewing buttons and hems before cutting cloth.
- A 2014 survey of 412 hospital nursing trainees found that those assigned graduated ward duties reported somewhat higher confidence than those given full duties immediately.
- The survey's authors cautioned that the confidence difference was modest and might reflect differences between hospitals rather than the training model itself.
problem.question: The student wants to present the nursing study's finding with the degree of caution its authors expressed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: A 2014 survey of nursing trainees suggested that graduated ward duties may be linked to slightly greater confidence, though the effect could stem from differences among hospitals.
A 2014 survey of nursing trainees proved that graduated ward duties produce greater confidence, confirming Lave and Wenger's model of peripheral participation.
A 2014 survey of nursing trainees may have found that graduated ward duties possibly relate to confidence, though Lave and Wenger perhaps introduced peripheral participation in 1991.
A 2014 survey of nursing trainees suggested that apprentices may gain skill by sewing buttons and hems before cutting cloth, though the effect could stem from local customs.
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 효과가 '약간' 크다는 점과 병원 간 차이 때문일 수 있다는 저자들의 단서를 그대로 살려 잠정적으로 표현했다. B: 잠정적인 상관 결과를 '증명했다'·'산출한다'고 과장했다. C: 1991년 출간처럼 확정된 사실까지 'perhaps'로 불필요하게 약화시켰다. D: 신중한 어조는 맞지만 내용이 라이베리아 재단사 견습생 현장연구와 섞여 있어 간호 연구 결과를 제대로 전하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct. It keeps the authors' caution: the confidence gain was small ("slightly") and might come from differences between hospitals. B overstates a tentative, correlational result by saying the survey "proved" that graduated duties "produce" confidence. C weakens facts that are certain, such as the 1991 publication, by adding "perhaps" and stacking extra hedges where they aren't needed. D uses the right cautious tone but mixes in details from the Liberian tailors' fieldwork, so it doesn't actually report the nursing study's finding.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 확정적 사실(1991년 출간, 라이베리아 현장연구)과 잠정적 결과(2014 설문, 저자 단서)가 공존하고, A는 'suggested/may be linked/slightly/could stem from' 등으로 저자들의 신중함을 정확히 재현한다. B는 'proved/produce/confirming'으로 과잉 일반화, C는 1991년 출간이라는 확정 사실까지 'perhaps'로 약화시켜 확실성을 과도하게 축소, D는 신중한 어조이나 재단사 견습 내용과 혼동되어 목표 불충족. 단순 접속어 선택이 아니라 어떤 진술에 어느 수준의 헤지가 적절한지 판별해야 하므로 medium 이상. 다만 B·D는 비교적 쉽게 제거되어 A/C 변별이 난이도의 핵심이며, D의 'local customs' 표현은 노트에 근거가 없어 다소 작위적이지만 오답 기능에는 지장 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 하나로 확정된다. 다만 B는 '증명했다'로 과장했고, C는 모든 진술에 헤지를 붙여 어색하며, D는 주제가 아예 다르다. 세 오답 모두 쉽게 걸러져서 실제 난이도는 medium 수준이다. 'modest', 'hospitals' 같은 표현만 대조해 봐도 A를 고를 수 있다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Linguistic relativity is the idea that the language a person speaks can influence how that person thinks.
- Cognitive scientist Lera Boroditsky has tested whether language affects how people mentally represent time.
- In a 2001 study, Mandarin speakers, whose language often describes earlier events as "up" and later events as "down," answered questions about time faster after viewing vertically arranged visual primes.
- In the same study, English speakers, whose language mostly describes time with front/back metaphors, answered such questions faster after viewing horizontally arranged primes.
- In a 2010 study with Alice Gaby, speakers of Kuuk Thaayorre, an Aboriginal Australian language that uses cardinal directions instead of "left" and "right," arranged picture sequences from east to west regardless of which way they faced.

The student wants to contrast how the two groups of participants in Boroditsky's 2001 study were affected by the visual primes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Linguistic relativity is the idea that the language a person speaks can influence how that person thinks.
- Cognitive scientist Lera Boroditsky has tested whether language affects how people mentally represent time.
- In a 2001 study, Mandarin speakers, whose language often describes earlier events as "up" and later events as "down," answered questions about time faster after viewing vertically arranged visual primes.
- In the same study, English speakers, whose language mostly describes time with front/back metaphors, answered such questions faster after viewing horizontally arranged primes.
- In a 2010 study with Alice Gaby, speakers of Kuuk Thaayorre, an Aboriginal Australian language that uses cardinal directions instead of "left" and "right," arranged picture sequences from east to west regardless of which way they faced.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast how the two groups of participants in Boroditsky's 2001 study were affected by the visual primes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas many earlier researchers doubted linguistic relativity, Mandarin speakers in Boroditsky's 2001 study answered questions about time faster after viewing vertically arranged primes.
Whereas Mandarin speakers in Boroditsky's 2001 study answered questions about time faster after viewing vertically arranged primes, English speakers did so after viewing horizontally arranged ones.

Whereas Mandarin speakers in Boroditsky's 2001 study answered questions about time faster after viewing vertically arranged primes, Kuuk Thaayorre speakers in a 2010 study arranged pictures from east to west.
Whereas Mandarin speakers in Boroditsky's 2001 study could understand time only through vertically arranged primes, English speakers were unable to process vertical primes at all.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 2001년 연구의 두 집단(중국어 화자·영어 화자)을 모두 다루고, 각각 세로 배열 자극 뒤와 가로 배열 자극 뒤에 더 빨리 답했다는 서로 다른 반응을 대조한다. 목표를 그대로 달성한다.
A: 중국어 화자에 대한 결과만 담았다. 'Whereas' 뒤에 붙은 '초기 연구자들의 의심'은 노트에 없는 내용이고, 영어 화자 쪽 결과가 빠져서 목표의 절반만 이룬다.
C: 두 사실을 합치긴 했지만 대조 대상이 2010년 연구의 Kuuk Thaayorre 화자다. 2001년 연구의 두 참가 집단을 대조하라는 목표와 맞지 않는 조합이다.
D: '오직 세로로만 이해했다', '세로 자극을 전혀 처리하지 못했다'는 주장은 노트에 없다. 노트가 말하는 것은 반응 속도가 더 빨랐다는 점뿐이므로 사실을 왜곡한 선택지다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: This choice covers both groups from the 2001 study, Mandarin speakers and English speakers. It contrasts their results: Mandarin speakers answered faster after vertical primes, and English speakers answered faster after horizontal ones. That is exactly what the goal asks for.
A: This choice gives only the Mandarin speakers' result. Its contrast is with earlier researchers' doubts, which the notes never mention, and the English speakers' result is missing. So it does only half the job.
C: This choice does combine two facts, but it compares Mandarin speakers with Kuuk Thaayorre speakers from the 2010 study. The goal is to contrast the two groups in the 2001 study, so this is the wrong pairing.
D: This choice claims Mandarin speakers could understand time "only" through vertical primes and that English speakers "were unable to process" vertical primes. Neither claim is in the notes. The notes only say which primes led to faster answers, so this choice distorts the findings.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 2001년 연구의 두 집단(중국어/영어 화자)과 각기 다른 프라임 반응을 정확히 대조하며 노트 3·4를 통합한다. A는 한쪽 결과만 + 노트에 없는 '초기 연구자들의 의심'(체크리스트 4·5 충족), C는 두 노트를 결합했으나 2010년 연구로 범위 이탈(purpose_scope_calibration 요구), D는 '오직/전혀'로 속도 차이를 능력 유무로 과장(claim_certainty_discrimination). Boroditsky 2001(Mandarin 수직/English 수평 프라임), Boroditsky & Gaby 2010(Kuuk Thaayorre 동→서 배열) 모두 실제 연구와 부합. 해설은 정답 및 오답 근거를 정확히 기술하며 모순 없음. 다만 오답 A·D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되어 hard 중 하위 수준(borderline)으로 판단되며, 실질적 난이도는 C의 범위 판별에서 나온다.

advisory.note: C는 다른 연구를 끌어온 범위 오류형 오답이고, D는 결과를 과잉 일반화한 확실성 오류형 오답이다. 둘 다 hard 수준의 변별을 요구한다. 다만 정답이 'Whereas' 구조로 두 집단을 대조하고 있어 비교적 쉽게 찾을 수 있다.

problem.passage:
Code-switching, the alternation between two languages within a single conversation, was once dismissed as a sign that bilingual speakers lacked full command of either language. Sociolinguist Mariam Osei has challenged that view. Having recorded more than 300 hours of casual conversation among Twi-English bilingual teenagers in South London, ______ that the speakers' switches into Twi clustered at moments when they were asserting loyalty to friends or distancing themselves from teachers, suggesting that the practice functions as a deliberate tool for negotiating social identity.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Code-switching, the alternation between two languages within a single conversation, was once dismissed as a sign that bilingual speakers lacked full command of either language. Sociolinguist Mariam Osei has challenged that view. Having recorded more than 300 hours of casual conversation among Twi-English bilingual teenagers in South London, ______ that the speakers' switches into Twi clustered at moments when they were asserting loyalty to friends or distancing themselves from teachers, suggesting that the practice functions as a deliberate tool for negotiating social identity.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the neighborhood's secondary schools reported
Osei's published study revealed
Osei found
the teenagers themselves noticed
problem.explanation: 분사구문 'Having recorded more than 300 hours of ... conversation'은 녹음을 한 행위자를 주어로 가져야 한다. 녹음을 한 사람은 연구자 Osei이므로 'Osei found'(C)가 정답이다. A: 지역 학교들은 녹음 행위와 아무 관계없는 엉뚱한 주어로, 현수 수식어가 된다. B: 'Osei's published study'는 Osei와 관련은 있지만 사람이 아닌 저작물이다. 연구 결과물이 직접 300시간을 녹음할 수는 없으므로 수식 대상이 맞지 않는다. D: 'the teenagers'는 복수 주어와 'noticed'가 문법적으로 잘 맞고 지문에도 나오는 명사이지만, 이들은 녹음된 대상이지 녹음한 사람이 아니다. 따라서 의미상 수식어가 가리킬 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence begins with the participial phrase "Having recorded more than 300 hours of casual conversation...". Whatever comes right after the comma has to be the one who did the recording. That was the researcher, Osei, so "Osei found" (C) is correct. A is wrong because the neighborhood's schools have nothing to do with the recording, which leaves the modifier dangling. B names something closely tied to Osei, her published study, but a study is a written work, not a person. A study can't record conversations. D uses a plural subject that agrees with its verb and appears in the passage. However, the teenagers were the people being recorded, not the ones doing the recording, so the modifier can't logically describe them.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구문 'Having recorded...'의 행위자는 연구자 Osei이며 C만 이에 부합한다. A·B·D 모두 문법적으로 완전한 문장이고 시제가 동일(과거)하여 수일치·시제로는 변별 불가. B(Osei's published study)는 사람 vs 저작물 범주 함정, D(the teenagers)는 지문에 등장하는 명사이자 녹음 '대상'이라는 의미적 함정으로 설계되어 수식어-피수식어의 의미 연결 추론을 실제로 요구한다. 해설은 각 오답의 탈락 사유를 정확히 서술하며 모순 없음. 가상의 연구자·연구로 사실 오류나 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: B(Osei's study, 소유격 함정)와 D(지문에 나오는 teenagers)는 그럴듯한 오답이다. 수일치로는 정답을 가를 수 없다.

problem.passage:
In many classrooms of the early 1980s, computers served mainly to drill students on arithmetic facts and to score their answers ______ Logo, the programming language that mathematician Seymour Papert helped design, children gave commands to a screen "turtle" so that it would draw shapes, teaching the machine instead of being taught by it.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In many classrooms of the early 1980s, computers served mainly to drill students on arithmetic facts and to score their answers ______ Logo, the programming language that mathematician Seymour Papert helped design, children gave commands to a screen "turtle" so that it would draw shapes, teaching the machine instead of being taught by it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , so in
, in
but in;
, but in
problem.explanation: 이 문장은 독립절 두 개로 되어 있다. 앞 절은 컴퓨터가 아이들을 반복 훈련하고 채점하는 데 쓰였다는 내용이고, 뒤 절(in Logo ... children gave commands ...)은 아이들이 오히려 기계를 가르쳤다는 내용이다. 두 절은 서로 대조 관계이므로 쉼표에 대조의 등위접속사 but을 더한 D가 정답이다. A: 쉼표+등위접속사라는 구조는 맞지만, so는 인과를 나타낸다. 반복 훈련 때문에 Logo에서 아이들이 기계를 가르치게 된 것이 아니므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다. B: 독립절 두 개를 쉼표 하나로만 이어서 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 전치사구 'in Logo' 한가운데에 들어가 있다. 그 결과 뒤쪽은 독립절이 되지 못하고, 앞쪽도 'but in'에서 어색하게 끊긴다.
problem.explanationEn: This sentence is made of two independent clauses. The first says computers were used to drill and score students. The second (in Logo ... children gave commands ...) says children taught the machine instead. These ideas contrast, so the right fix is a comma plus the contrasting conjunction "but," which is choice D. Choice A has the right structure (comma plus a coordinating conjunction), but "so" signals cause and effect. The drilling did not cause children to program the turtle, so the logic doesn't fit. Choice B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice C puts the semicolon in the middle of the phrase "in Logo" instead of at the boundary between the clauses. That leaves "but in" hanging awkwardly, and what follows the semicolon is not an independent clause.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검증: 앞 절(computers served ... answers)과 뒤 절(in Logo, [동격 삽입], children gave commands ...)이 모두 독립절이며 대조 관계 → ', but' 적합. B는 콤마 스플라이스, C는 'in; Logo'로 전치사구 내부에 세미콜론. A(', so')는 구두점 구조는 맞으나 인과 관계가 문맥과 불일치. 수험생은 'in Logo, the programming language ..., children' 에서 동격 삽입구를 절 경계로 오인하지 않고 뒤 절의 주어(children)를 찾아내야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고가 요구됨. 유의점: A는 문법이 아닌 논리(접속사 의미)로만 배제되는 선택지로, 실제 SAT boundaries 문항에서는 다소 드문 변별 방식이나 레시피 체크리스트(항목 2·3)에 부합하므로 형식상 허용 범위로 판정. 사실관계(Logo, Papert, 거북이 그래픽, 1980년대 초 드릴 위주 활용)는 정확함.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 대조 관계(반복 훈련 대 아이들이 기계를 가르침)에 맞습니다. A는 so 때문에 인과 관계로 잘못 연결됩니다. B는 콤마 스플라이스, C는 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 세미콜론이 있습니다. 문두 전치사구와 동격 삽입구가 있어 뒤 절의 주어(children)를 찾아야 하므로, 단순한 구두점 판단보다 사고가 더 필요합니다.

problem.passage:
The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648, ended the Thirty Years' War, a conflict that had begun largely as a struggle between Catholic and Protestant rulers within the Holy Roman Empire. Textbooks often credit the treaties with inventing the modern system of sovereign states, each free from outside interference in its internal affairs. Historian Andreas Osiander and others, however, point out that the documents themselves say little about sovereignty as an abstract principle. Instead, they spend most of their pages settling specific disputes: restoring confiscated lands, confirming the rights of particular princes, and guaranteeing that Calvinism would be tolerated alongside Catholicism and Lutheranism. In this view, the treaties' lasting importance came less from any new theory of statehood than from the practical precedent they set: rulers who disagreed about religion could still negotiate a durable settlement rather than fight until one faith prevailed.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although often praised for establishing state sovereignty, the Westphalian treaties mattered chiefly because they showed that religious rivals could reach a lasting negotiated peace.
Although the Thirty Years' War began as a religious conflict, the Westphalian treaties were concerned mainly with dividing territory among the Empire's princes.
Although historians long overlooked the Westphalian treaties, recent scholars have shown that they created the principle of noninterference in internal affairs.
Although Calvinism gained toleration at Westphalia, Catholic and Lutheran rulers continued to resist that settlement for decades afterward.
problem.explanation: 지문은 조약이 주권 국가 체제를 발명했다는 통설에 의문을 던지고, 조약의 진짜 중요성은 종교가 다른 통치자들도 협상으로 지속적 평화를 이룰 수 있다는 실질적 선례에 있다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 언급된 영토 반환 같은 세부를 다루지만, 조약의 의의라는 결론은 빠져 있고 종교적 관용도 무시한다. C는 지문의 주장을 뒤집은 것이다. 지문은 학자들이 조약과 주권 원칙의 연결을 의심한다고 말한다. D는 이후의 저항을 말하는데, 이는 지문에 나오지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text questions the common claim that the treaties invented sovereign statehood. It concludes that their real significance was a practical precedent: rulers of different faiths could negotiate a durable peace. That makes A correct. B picks up details the passage does mention, like the land settlements, but it leaves out the passage's conclusion about why the treaties mattered and ignores religious toleration. C reverses the argument, because the passage says scholars doubt that the treaties established sovereignty as a principle. D describes later resistance to the settlement, which the text never mentions.

quality.seed: history and civics — The Treaty of Westphalia 1648 and its establishment of sovereign nation-state system ending religious warfare

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 지문의 양보(통설: 주권 발명)와 결론(종교적 경쟁자 간 지속적 협상 평화의 선례)을 정확히 포착한다. B는 지문에 실제 언급된 세부(영토 반환·제후 권리)를 근거로 삼아 그럴듯하지만 결론을 놓치고, C는 주장을 뒤집었으며, D는 지문 밖 내용으로 말은 된다. 역사적 사실(1648년, 30년 전쟁, Osiander의 '베스트팔렌 신화' 비판, 칼뱅주의 공인)도 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 일치하고 영어 자연스러움. 양보·전환 구조를 읽어야 하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 지문의 세부(영토 문제 해결)를 근거로 삼아 그럴듯한 오답이다. C는 주권 통설을 끌어와 훑어 읽는 수험생을 노린다. D는 약한 오답이지만 Calvinism 관용이라는 근거가 있어 말이 된다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Accounts of the Haitian Revolution often begin with the uprising of August 1791, when enslaved workers in Saint-Domingue's Northern Plain set fire to sugar plantations that had made the colony France's most profitable possession. Some historians, however, emphasize that the revolt's success depended less on that single night than on years of organizing that came before it. Enslaved people had built networks across plantations through markets, religious gatherings such as the Bois Caïman ceremony, and the movement of coachmen and drivers who carried messages between estates.

Over the following decade, leaders including Toussaint Louverture turned these networks into disciplined armies capable of defeating French, Spanish, and British forces. When Napoleon sent an expedition in 1802 to restore slavery, it was the depth of this earlier coordination, historians argue, that allowed resistance to survive the capture of Louverture himself, leading to Haiti's independence in 1804.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Connections that enslaved people had established well before 1791 help explain why the revolution ultimately succeeded.
Toussaint Louverture's military leadership was the main reason Haitian forces defeated three European powers.

problem.explanation: 지문은 1791년 봉기 하나보다 그 이전 수년간 노예들이 시장, 종교 모임, 마부 등을 통해 만든 연결망이 혁명 성공의 바탕이었다는 역사가들의 견해를 제시하며, 루베르튀르가 체포된 뒤에도 저항이 지속된 이유로 그 연결망을 든다. 따라서 B가 중심 내용이다. A는 지문이 오히려 반박하는 '단 하룻밤' 관점이다.
