problem.explanationEn: The text presents historians' view that the revolution succeeded because of years of organizing before 1791, through markets, religious gatherings, and messengers, more than because of the August uprising alone. It also says this coordination let resistance survive even after Louverture was captured. So B is the main idea. A states the "single night" view that the text pushes back against. C picks up on Louverture, but the text points out that resistance went on without him, so his leadership isn't presented as the main cause. D takes one detail too far: religious gatherings are only one of several ways networks formed, and the text never calls them the primary one.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산: 지문 1단락 "success depended less on that single night than on years of organizing" + 2단락 "depth of this earlier coordination... allowed resistance to survive"가 B를 직접 뒷받침. advisory.note: 정답 B는 지문 전체(1791년 이전 조직화→성공, 루베르튀르 체포 후에도 저항이 이어짐)로 뒷받침됨. A·C·D는 모두 지문의 세부 내용에 근거한 그럴듯한 오답이라 비교가 필요해 medium에 맞음. 사실 관계(1791년 8월 봉기, 부아 카이망 의식, 1802년 원정, 1804년 독립)도 정확함. 1802년 원정이 노예제 '복원' 목적이었다는 점은 역사학계에서 해석이 갈리지만 지문이 역사가들의 견해로 제시하므로 허용 범위로 봄.

problem.passage:
When Parliament repealed the Corn Laws in 1846, ending tariffs that had kept the price of imported grain high, many observers treated the decision as a simple victory of manufacturers over landowners. Historian Cheryl Schonhardt-Bailey has argued that this picture is incomplete. By the 1840s, she notes, many large landowners had invested heavily in railways, canals, and urban property, so their wealth increasingly depended on the same industrial expansion that manufacturers championed. For these landowners, cheaper bread for factory workers promised busier towns and more profitable investments, which made the loss of agricultural protection easier to accept. In Schonhardt-Bailey's view, repeal passed not only because industrial interests overpowered the landed class but also because the economic interests of a significant part of that class had already shifted toward free trade.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Repeal of the Corn Laws occurred mainly because landowners came to believe that cheaper bread would improve the lives of factory workers.
Repeal of the Corn Laws was made possible in part because many landowners' investments had tied their fortunes to industrial growth.
Repeal of the Corn Laws was made possible in part because railways and canals lowered the cost of importing foreign grain.

A는 지문이 '불완전하다'고 비판하는 기존 견해이다. B는 값싼 빵을 언급하지만, 지주의 동기는 노동자 복지가 아니라 자기 투자 수익이었다. D는 철도와 운하를 지주의 투자 대상이 아니라 곡물 수입 비용을 낮춘 요인으로 잘못 연결한다.

In her view, many landowners had invested in railways, canals, and urban property, so their interests had already moved toward industrial growth and free trade. That makes C the main idea. A is the older view that the text calls incomplete. B mentions cheaper bread, but the landowners cared about profits on their investments, not about improving workers' lives. D treats railways and canals as things that lowered the cost of grain imports, when the text describes them only as investments landowners made.

hardJudge.note: 지문의 중심 생각(지주의 투자 다변화로 이해관계가 자유무역 쪽으로 이동했다는 Schonhardt-Bailey의 주장)을 C가 정확히 요약함. A는 지문이 '불완전'하다고 비판하는 기존 견해, B는 '값싼 빵'을 지주의 이타적 동기로 왜곡, D는 철도·운하를 투자 대상이 아닌 수입 비용 요인으로 오독 — 세 오답 모두 지문 요소를 포함해 비교가 필요하고 D도 그럴듯함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 오답 배제 근거가 일치하며 한글 혼입 없음. Schonhardt-Bailey의 실제 주장(지주의 포트폴리오 다변화)과도 부합하여 사실 오류 없음. 지문은 자체 작성된 설명문으로 저작권 우려 없음. 중간 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: C의 'in part'가 지문의 'not only...but also'와 맞는다. A는 기존 견해를 그대로 옮긴 함정이다. B는 값싼 빵이라는 세부를 쓰지만 동기를 잘못 짚었다. D는 철도·운하라는 세부를 다른 인과에 잘못 연결했다. 오답 모두 부분적 근거가 있어 medium 난이도에 적합하다. Schonhardt-Bailey의 실제 주장(지주의 포트폴리오 다각화)과도 부합한다.

problem.passage:
The Satsuma Rebellion of 1877 is often remembered as the last stand of Japan's samurai against modernization, a romantic clash between swords and rifles. Historians who have examined the rebels' own petitions and letters, however, describe a more complicated picture. Many of the men who followed Saigō Takamori did not reject Western weapons or industry; in fact, the rebel army carried modern rifles and artillery wherever it could get them. What united the rebels was anger at the Meiji government's centralization of power in Tokyo, which had abolished the domains, ended samurai stipends, and banned the wearing of swords in public. These measures took away the status and income that had long defined the samurai class while concentrating authority in a small group of officials. Seen this way, the rebellion was less a refusal of new technology than a protest against who would hold power in the new state and on what terms.

Based on the text, how do historians who studied the rebels' writings interpret the Satsuma Rebellion?

problem.question: Based on the text, how do historians who studied the rebels' writings interpret the Satsuma Rebellion?
options: They argue that the rebels were mostly driven by a refusal to give up traditional weapons such as swords in favor of the firearms the Meiji army used.
They argue that the rebels' main goal was to get Western industry adopted faster than the officials in Tokyo were willing to allow.
They argue that the rebels objected mainly to losing their stipends and did not care how political authority was organized in the new state.
They argue that the rebels were reacting mainly to how the reforms redistributed status and political control, not to modern technology itself.
problem.explanation: 지문은 반란군이 근대 무기를 거부하지 않았고, 권력의 도쿄 집중과 사무라이 지위·수입 박탈에 분노했다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 '검 대 소총'이라는 대중적 통념을 따르는데, 역사가들은 바로 이 통념을 반박한다. B는 반란군이 서구 무기를 사용했다는 세부 내용을 확대 해석했을 뿐, 산업화를 더 빨리 하라고 요구했다는 근거는 없다. C는 녹봉 폐지는 맞게 짚었지만, 지문이 권력 집중을 핵심 분노로 강조하므로 '정치 권한에는 관심 없었다'는 부분이 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The correct answer is D. The text says the rebels didn't reject modern weapons and were angry about power being centralized in Tokyo and about losing their status and income, which is exactly what D states. A repeats the popular "swords versus rifles" image, and that's the view the historians argue against. B stretches the detail that the rebels used Western arms, but nothing in the text says they wanted industry adopted faster. C gets the lost stipends right, but it's wrong to say the rebels didn't care how authority was organized, because the text names centralization of power as a main source of their anger.

C는 녹봉 폐지라는 부분적 근거를 가지며 B는 '서구 무기 사용' 세부를 확대한 그럴듯한 오답으로, medium 기준 충족. 역사적 사실(1877년, 사이고 다카모리, 폐번치현·질록처분·폐도령, 반란군의 근대 소총 사용) 모두 무리 없음. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: D는 마지막 문장을 바꿔 말한 것이다. A는 통념, C는 일부만 맞는 오답이다. B는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 그럴듯하다. 역사적 사실(번 폐지, 녹봉 폐지, 폐도령)도 정확하다. 목표 난이도(medium)에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In March 1918, Bolshevik Russia signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Central Powers, ending its part in World War One. The terms were severe: Russia gave up Poland, the Baltic territories, Finland, and Ukraine, which together held about a third of its population and much of its coal and grain. Many historians have described the treaty simply as a humiliating defeat forced on a collapsing state. __Yet Lenin had pushed for accepting the terms over the objections of many fellow Bolsheviks, arguing that the new regime could not survive both a foreign war and the struggle to hold power at home.__ Seen this way, the treaty was a calculated trade of territory for time, and when Germany lost the war later that year, the Bolsheviks quickly declared the agreement void.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

options: It introduces a detail that complicates a common view of the treaty and prepares for a different reading of it.
It introduces a detail that explains why the treaty's territorial losses were as large as the text earlier indicates.
It introduces a detail that supports the historians' claim that Russia was a collapsing state in 1918.
It introduces a detail that shows how Germany eventually came to reject the terms of the treaty.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 조약을 단순한 굴욕적 패배로 보는 통념에 반하는 사실, 즉 레닌이 국내 권력 유지를 위해 의도적으로 조약 수락을 밀어붙였다는 점을 제시하고, 이어지는 '영토와 시간을 맞바꾼 계산된 거래'라는 해석의 토대를 마련하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 앞 문장의 영토 상실 내용과 연결되어 보이지만, 밑줄 문장은 손실 규모가 왜 컸는지를 설명하지 않는다. C는 국내 투쟁이라는 언급이 '붕괴하는 국가'와 겹쳐 보이지만, 문장의 역할은 역사가들의 견해를 지지하는 것이 아니라 그 견해를 복잡하게 만드는 것이다. D는 마지막 문장 내용과 혼동한 것으로, 조약을 무효로 선언한 쪽은 독일이 아니라 볼셰비키이고 밑줄 문장에서도 다루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and gives a fact that cuts against the common view of the treaty as nothing more than a humiliating defeat: Lenin deliberately pushed for accepting it so the regime could hold power at home. That fact sets up the next sentence's reading of the treaty as a calculated trade of territory for time, so A is correct. B links the sentence to the territorial losses mentioned earlier, but the sentence never explains why those losses were so large. C picks up on the mention of a struggle at home, which might seem to fit the "collapsing state" view, but the sentence complicates the historians' view instead of supporting it. D mixes up the final sentence: it was the Bolsheviks, not Germany, who declared the treaty void, and the underlined sentence doesn't discuss that at all.

problem.passage:
In the decades after 1937, accounts of the Nanjing Massacre, in which Japanese troops killed large numbers of Chinese civilians and prisoners after capturing the city, were often dismissed in Japan as wartime propaganda. Historians seeking to establish the scale of the atrocities therefore faced a problem of credibility: testimony from Chinese survivors, however detailed, could be waved away as biased. Some researchers responded by turning to sources that skeptics could not easily reject. __Among the most revealing of these were the diaries of Japanese soldiers themselves, several of which record executions of captives in matter-of-fact entries written with no expectation of public scrutiny.__ Because such documents came from the perpetrators' side and were not produced to persuade anyone, they made it far harder to claim that the massacre had been invented by its victims.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.passage:
In April 1955, delegates from twenty-nine Asian and African states gathered in Bandung, Indonesia, to discuss cooperation among nations that had recently won, or were still seeking, independence from colonial rule. Many Western observers predicted that the meeting would simply split into pro-American and pro-Soviet blocs, since several attending governments already had close ties to one of the superpowers. __Yet the conference's final communiqué endorsed ten principles, including respect for sovereignty and abstention from collective defense arrangements serving the interests of any great power, that nearly every delegation accepted.__ Historians now view those principles as an early basis for the Non-Aligned Movement, which was formally launched in Belgrade in 1961.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In April 1955, delegates from twenty-nine Asian and African states gathered in Bandung, Indonesia, to discuss cooperation among nations that had recently won, or were still seeking, independence from colonial rule. problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why several attending governments chose to keep their existing ties to one of the superpowers.
It identifies the specific disagreements that kept the delegations from issuing a joint statement.
It presents an outcome that runs counter to a forecast described earlier and sets up a later claim about the meeting's legacy.

problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 회의가 강대국 진영별로 쪼개질 거라던 서방의 예측과 달리 거의 모든 대표단이 10개 원칙을 받아들였다는 결과를 보여 주고, 이 원칙은 다음 문장에서 비동맹운동의 토대로 이어진다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 강대국과의 유대가 언급되긴 하지만 밑줄 문장은 그 이유를 설명하지 않는다. B는 공동 성명이 실제로 채택되었으므로 내용과 반대된다. D는 베오그라드가 마지막 문장에 나오긴 하지만 밑줄 문장은 반둥 회의의 결과를 다룰 뿐 베오그라드 상황을 설명하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet," which tells you it contrasts with the Western prediction that the conference would split into superpower blocs. It shows that nearly every delegation accepted ten shared principles, and the next sentence links those principles to the Non-Aligned Movement. That makes C correct. A is wrong because the text does mention superpower ties, but the underlined sentence doesn't explain why governments kept them. B is wrong because a joint communiqué actually was issued, so it says the opposite of the text. D is wrong because Belgrade appears only in the final sentence, while the underlined sentence describes what happened at Bandung, not the conditions in Belgrade.

problem.passage:
When East German authorities strung barbed wire across Berlin on the night of August 13, 1961, many Western observers assumed the barrier would be temporary, a crude measure that would be dismantled once the flood of emigrants slowed. Instead, over the following years the wire was replaced by concrete slabs, watchtowers, and a cleared "death strip," and the structure came to seem less like an emergency improvisation than a permanent feature of the city. For historians, this hardening is significant: it shows that the division of Berlin was not a passing crisis but had become ______ in the physical landscape itself, making the ideological split between East and West visible on every street it crossed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When East German authorities strung barbed wire across Berlin on the night of August 13, 1961, many Western observers assumed the barrier would be temporary, a crude measure that would be dismantled once the flood of emigrants slowed. Instead, over the following years the wire was replaced by concrete slabs, watchtowers, and a cleared "death strip," and the structure came to seem less like an emergency improvisation than a permanent feature of the city. For historians, this hardening is significant: it shows that the division of Berlin was not a passing crisis but had become ______ in the physical landscape itself, making the ideological split between East and West visible on every street it crossed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: concealed
contested
anticipated
entrenched
problem.explanation: 지문은 임시 철조망이 콘크리트·감시탑 등으로 바뀌며 '영구적 특징'이 되었고, 분단이 '일시적 위기가 아니었다'고 대비하므로 빈칸에는 깊이 굳어 고착되었다는 뜻이 필요하다. 따라서 D(entrenched)가 정답이다. A(concealed)는 분단이 '모든 거리에서 보이게' 되었다는 내용과 정반대이다. B(contested)는 베를린 분단이 실제로 논쟁 대상이었다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문의 초점은 영구화이지 이견이 아니다. C(anticipated)는 서방 관찰자들이 장벽이 일시적일 것이라고 예상했다는 부분과 연결되어 보이지만, 오히려 그들은 영구화를 예상하지 못했으므로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage contrasts the early view of the barrier as temporary with its transformation into concrete walls and watchtowers that made it "a permanent feature," so the blank needs a word meaning firmly and lastingly established. That makes D (entrenched) the correct choice. A (concealed) contradicts the claim that the split became visible on every street. B (contested) sounds plausible because the division was politically disputed, but the passage is about permanence, not disagreement. C (anticipated) may seem to fit the mention of observers' expectations, but those observers expected the barrier to be temporary, so its permanence was not anticipated.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 '일시적 위기가 아니라'와 '영구적 특징' 대비로 '깊이 굳어진'(entrenched)이 유일하게 정확히 맞음. 역사적 사실(1961.8.13 철조망→콘크리트·감시탑·죽음의 띠) 정확. 오답 중 B(contested)·C(anticipated)는 지문 일부와 연결되는 부분적 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하고 A는 '보이게 되었다'와 정반대로 말은 됨. 해설 한·영 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단서가 비교적 뚜렷해 medium 중 다소 쉬운 편이나 두 정보(임시→영구 전환 + '보이게' 됨) 연결이 필요하므로 적합.

advisory.note: 'entrenched in the physical landscape'는 영구화를 정확히 나타낸다. contested와 anticipated는 부분적 근거가 있어 그럴듯한 오답이고, concealed는 visible과 모순되어 배제된다. 사실 관계(1961년 8월 13일, 철조망에서 콘크리트 장벽으로의 전환)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In November 1995, delegations from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia met at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base near Dayton, Ohio, to negotiate an end to more than three years of war. Isolated on the base for three weeks and pressed daily by American mediator Richard Holbrooke, ______ a settlement that divided Bosnia into two largely autonomous entities under a single, weak central government.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In November 1995, delegations from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia met at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base near Dayton, Ohio, to negotiate an end to more than three years of war. Isolated on the base for three weeks and pressed daily by American mediator Richard Holbrooke, ______ a settlement that divided Bosnia into two largely autonomous entities under a single, weak central government.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the air force base's remote location eventually produced
the delegations' leaders eventually accepted
the leaders' signed treaty eventually established
the three weeks of talks eventually yielded
problem.explanation:
정답 B. 문두 분사구문 'Isolated on the base for three weeks and pressed daily by American mediator Richard Holbrooke'의 의미상 주어는 기지에 고립되어 중재자에게 매일 압박을 받은 존재여야 한다. 그런 존재는 사람, 즉 대표단의 지도자들뿐이므로 주절 주어는 'the delegations' leaders'가 되어야 한다.
A: 'the air force base's remote location'은 수식어와 관계없는 엉뚱한 명사다. 기지의 위치가 기지에 고립되거나 홀브룩에게 압박받을 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어(dangling modifier)가 된다.
C: 'the leaders' signed treaty'는 지도자들 자체가 아니라 그들이 만든 결과물(조약)이다. 범주가 다른 명사이므로 조약이 3주간 고립되고 압박받았다는 엉뚱한 뜻이 된다.
D: 'the three weeks of talks'는 문맥과 관련이 있고 복수 동사와도 잘 어울리지만, '3주간의 회담'이 '기지에서 3주간 고립되었다'는 것은 말이 안 되며 중재자에게 압박받을 수도 없다. 의미상 수식 대상이 될 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is B. The sentence opens with a participial phrase: "Isolated on the base for three weeks and pressed daily by American mediator Richard Holbrooke." Whatever comes right after the comma must be the thing that was isolated and pressed. Only people can be pressed by a mediator, so the subject has to be "the delegations' leaders."
A is wrong because "the air force base's remote location" has nothing to do with the modifier. A location can't be isolated on the base or pressured by Holbrooke, so the modifier dangles.
C is wrong because "the leaders' signed treaty" is something the leaders produced, not the leaders themselves. With this subject, the sentence says the treaty was isolated and pressured.
D is tempting because it fits the context and the plural verb works. But "three weeks of talks" can't be "isolated on the base for three weeks," and talks can't be pressed by a mediator. The modifier can't logically describe it.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구문 'Isolated... and pressed daily by Holbrooke'의 의미상 주어는 사람(대표단 지도자들)뿐이므로 B가 유일한 정답. A/C/D 모두 문법적으로 완전한 문장이며, 특히 D는 문맥상 관련 있는 명사(3주간의 회담)로 구성되어 의미적 연결 추론을 실제로 요구함. 모든 동사가 과거형이라 수일치로는 변별 불가. 데이턴 협상 관련 사실(1995년 11월, 라이트-패터슨 기지, 홀브룩, 두 개의 자치 실체·약한 중앙정부) 정확.

advisory.note: 이중 분사구문(isolated/pressed)의 의미상 주어는 사람이어야 한다. D(talks)와 C(treaty)는 문맥과 관련이 있어 그럴듯한 오답이다. 모든 선택지가 과거형이라 수일치로는 정답을 가를 수 없다. 데이턴 협정 관련 사실(1995년 11월, 라이트-패터슨 공군기지, 약 3주, 두 개의 자치체)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In the brewing towns of the southern Low Countries during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, a brewery's most valuable asset was often invisible: the particular yeast culture that gave its beer a distinctive flavor. Unlike a recipe, which could be copied once written down, a yeast culture had to be kept alive, carried from batch to batch, and handled with skill that only experience could teach. Brewing guilds turned this fact to their members' advantage. Guild rules limited how many apprentices a master could take on, required apprentices to serve for years before they could brew on their own, and barred journeymen from setting up rival breweries within a set distance of their former masters.

Historians have sometimes read such rules simply as tools for keeping out competitors. Economic historian Lieve Claes argues that this reading misses their main function. Because no law at the time protected a living culture as property, she contends, the guilds' control over who could learn brewing, and when, served as a substitute for patent protection: the knowledge needed to maintain a valuable strain passed only to those bound by long obligations to the brewery that owned it.

According to Claes, what was the chief purpose of the guild rules governing apprentices and journeymen?
problem.stimulus:
In the brewing towns of the southern Low Countries during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, a brewery's most valuable asset was often invisible: the particular yeast culture that gave its beer a distinctive flavor. Unlike a recipe, which could be copied once written down, a yeast culture had to be kept alive, carried from batch to batch, and handled with skill that only experience could teach. Brewing guilds turned this fact to their members' advantage. Guild rules limited how many apprentices a master could take on, required apprentices to serve for years before they could brew on their own, and barred journeymen from setting up rival breweries within a set distance of their former masters.

Historians have sometimes read such rules simply as tools for keeping out competitors. Economic historian Lieve Claes argues that this reading misses their main function. Because no law at the time protected a living culture as property, she contends, the guilds' control over who could learn brewing, and when, served as a substitute for patent protection: the knowledge needed to maintain a valuable strain passed only to those bound by long obligations to the brewery that owned it.
problem.question: According to Claes, what was the chief purpose of the guild rules governing apprentices and journeymen?
options: They kept the skills needed to maintain a brewery's yeast culture within a circle of workers committed to that brewery, protecting the culture when no law did.
They kept rival breweries far from established masters, protecting the masters' local customers when the guilds feared growing competition.
They kept written recipes within a circle of trusted guild members, protecting those recipes when copying became easy.
They kept apprentices in long periods of training, protecting the quality of guild beer when inexperienced brewers threatened its reputation.
problem.explanation: Claes는 법이 살아 있는 효모 배양균을 재산으로 보호하지 못했기 때문에, 길드가 누가 언제 양조를 배우는지 통제한 것이 특허를 대신하는 역할을 했다고 주장한다. 그래서 효모를 유지하는 지식이 양조장에 오래 묶인 사람들에게만 전해졌다는 A가 정답이다. B는 Claes가 핵심을 놓쳤다고 비판한 역사가들의 '경쟁 배제' 해석이다. C는 지문에서 쉽게 베낄 수 있다고 대비시킨 레시피를 보호 대상으로 착각한 것이다. D의 긴 수습 기간은 실제 규칙이 맞지만, 지문은 그 목적을 맥주의 품질이나 평판과 연결하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Claes argues that because no law protected a living yeast culture as property, the guilds' control over who could learn brewing, and when, worked as a substitute for patent protection. That makes A correct: the know-how for keeping a strain alive passed only to workers bound to the brewery that owned it. B describes the "keeping out competitors" reading, which is the view Claes says misses the rules' main function. C gets the thing being protected wrong, since the text contrasts written recipes, which could be copied, with yeast cultures. D mentions a real rule, the long apprenticeship, but the text never connects it to beer quality or reputation.

quality.seed: economics and business — Belgian brewing guilds and proprietary yeast strains as trade secrets enforced through apprenticeship restriction

hardJudge.note: 지문 2문단 "served as a substitute for patent protection… passed only to those bound by long obligations to the brewery" 가 A와 정확히 대응. B는 Claes가 반박한 역사가들의 해석(훑어 읽으면 고르기 쉬운 매력적 오답), C는 레시피/효모 대비를 뒤집은 것, D는 실제 규칙이나 목적 귀속이 지문에 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 모순 없음. 가상의 역사가 설정으로 사실 오류 없음. 두 관점 구분 + 보호 대상 식별이라는 2단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 실제 규칙(거리 제한)과 역사가들의 해석을 근거로 하고, D는 실제 규칙(긴 수습 기간)을 근거로 해 둘 다 부분적으로 맞는 근거가 있다. C는 레시피 대비를 잘못 읽은 경우다. 정답 A는 Claes의 주장을 정확히 바꿔 말한 것이다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Norway produces more farmed Atlantic salmon than any other country, most of it raised in open-net pens anchored in coastal fjords. Because the mesh of these pens lets water flow freely between farm and sea, parasites such as salmon lice can multiply among the densely packed farmed fish and then drift outward, where they attach to young wild salmon migrating past on their way to the ocean. Studies along the Norwegian coast have linked high lice levels near farms to lower survival among these wild migrants. Yet the farms' operating costs barely reflect this harm: a company pays for feed, labor, and treatments for its own fish, but the losses suffered by wild populations, and by the river anglers and tourism businesses that depend on them, appear on no farm's balance sheet. Economists describe such a situation as a negative externality, and some argue that Norway's recent move to tie permitted production growth to measured lice levels in each coastal zone is an attempt to make producers bear part of a cost that the open-net design had pushed onto others.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Norway produces more farmed Atlantic salmon than any other country, most of it raised in open-net pens anchored in coastal fjords. Because the mesh of these pens lets water flow freely between farm and sea, parasites such as salmon lice can multiply among the densely packed farmed fish and then drift outward, where they attach to young wild salmon migrating past on their way to the ocean. Studies along the Norwegian coast have linked high lice levels near farms to lower survival among these wild migrants. Yet the farms' operating costs barely reflect this harm: a company pays for feed, labor, and treatments for its own fish, but the losses suffered by wild populations, and by the river anglers and tourism businesses that depend on them, appear on no farm's balance sheet. Economists describe such a situation as a negative externality, and some argue that Norway's recent move to tie permitted production growth to measured lice levels in each coastal zone is an attempt to make producers bear part of a cost that the open-net design had pushed onto others.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Salmon lice that develop in open-net pens are the main reason wild Atlantic salmon populations in Norway have declined, so Norway has banned further expansion of coastal farming.
Open-net salmon farming in Norway passes parasite-related harm onto wild fish and those who rely on them without that harm appearing in farm costs, a problem some regulation tries to correct.
Norwegian salmon farms spend heavily on feed, labor, and lice treatments, which economists argue makes open-net farming more costly than alternative methods.
River anglers and tourism businesses in Norway have demanded compensation from salmon farms because lice from the pens have reduced the number of wild salmon.
problem.explanation: 이 글은 개방형 가두리에서 퍼진 연어 이가 야생 연어에 피해를 주지만 그 비용이 양식장 비용에 반영되지 않는다는 점(부정적 외부효과)과, 일부에서 이를 바로잡으려는 시도로 보는 규제를 함께 다루므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이와 야생 연어 감소의 연관은 맞게 짚었지만 '주된 원인'이라고 과장했고, 글은 확장 금지가 아니라 이 수치에 따라 성장을 허용하는 규제를 설명한다. C는 양식장이 사료·인건비·처치 비용을 낸다는 세부는 맞지만, 글의 요점은 양식장이 부담하지 '않는' 비용이고 다른 양식 방식과의 비교는 나오지 않는다. D는 낚시꾼과 관광업체가 피해를 본다는 내용은 맞지만, 이들이 보상을 요구했다는 내용은 글에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: B is correct because the passage explains that lice spreading from open-net pens harm wild salmon, yet that cost never shows up in farm expenses (a negative externality), and it presents a regulation that some see as an attempt to fix this. A rightly links lice to wild salmon losses, but it overstates them as the "main reason," and the passage describes rules that tie growth to lice levels, not a ban on expansion. C repeats real details about feed, labor, and treatment costs, but the passage's point is about the costs farms do not pay, and it never compares open-net farming with other methods. D correctly notes that anglers and tourism businesses are harmed, but the passage never says they asked for compensation.

quality.seed: economics and business — Norwegian salmon farming open-net cage externalities imposing disease spillover costs onto wild Atlantic stocks

hardJudge.note: 지문의 핵심(개방형 가두리 → 야생 연어 피해 → 비용 미반영=부정적 외부효과 → 이를 교정하려는 규제)을 B가 정확히 포괄. A는 '주된 원인'과 '확장 금지'로 과장·왜곡, C는 세부(사료·인건비·처치비)는 맞으나 요지와 반대 방향이며 대안 방식 비교는 지문에 없음, D는 피해 당사자는 맞으나 보상 요구는 미언급. 오답 셋 모두 부분적 근거를 가져 비교 배제가 필요하므로 medium 적합. 노르웨이 최대 생산국·이 수치 기반 생산 증가 규제(신호등 시스템)는 사실과 부합. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: Norway's traffic-light system (tying production growth to lice levels by zone) matches reality. The wrong options are partly right and are each ruled out for a different reason. B is a bit longer than the others, but that is within the acceptable range.

problem.passage:
In the early nineteenth century, much of the indigo grown in Bengal was sold through a few London merchant houses. These houses often agreed among themselves on what they would pay at the city's quarterly auctions. Some historians have argued that this coordination kept prices artificially low, squeezing the planters who shipped dye from India. Economic historian Priya Natarajan finds that account incomplete. __Comparing auction records with planters' private ledgers, she found that in years when the syndicates' agreed bids fell, planters' costs often fell even faster, because the same merchant houses were extending them cheaper credit against future harvests.__ In Natarajan's view, the syndicates controlled the trade less through the auction price itself than through the loans that tied planters to them season after season.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the early nineteenth century, much of the indigo grown in Bengal was sold through a few London merchant houses. These houses often agreed among themselves on what they would pay at the city's quarterly auctions. Some historians have argued that this coordination kept prices artificially low, squeezing the planters who shipped dye from India. Economic historian Priya Natarajan finds that account incomplete. __Comparing auction records with planters' private ledgers, she found that in years when the syndicates' agreed bids fell, planters' costs often fell even faster, because the same merchant houses were extending them cheaper credit against future harvests.__ In Natarajan's view, the syndicates controlled the trade less through the auction price itself than through the loans that tied planters to them season after season.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that the merchant syndicates' coordinated bidding had no measurable effect on the prices paid for Bengal indigo.
It gives evidence supporting the historians' claim that the syndicates kept prices low mainly to squeeze Bengal planters.
It explains how the London merchant houses first came to agree among themselves on bids at the quarterly auctions.
It gives evidence that complicates an earlier interpretation and leads to the alternative explanation stated afterward.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 Natarajan이 기존 해석(담합이 가격을 낮춰 재배자를 압박했다)을 '불완전하다'고 본 근거로, 입찰가 하락과 함께 신용 비용도 내려갔다는 기록 비교 결과를 제시한다. 이것이 마지막 문장의 대안적 설명(통제는 대출을 통해 이루어졌다)으로 이어지므로 D가 정답이다. A는 입찰가가 실제로 떨어졌다는 내용과 모순되며, 과장된 주장이다. B는 문장이 가격 하락을 언급하긴 하지만 기존 주장을 지지하는 것이 아니라 복잡하게 만든다는 점을 놓쳤다. C는 담합의 기원을 다루는데, 지문은 그 내용을 전혀 설명하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence gives the evidence behind Natarajan's view that the earlier account is "incomplete." Her records show that planters' costs fell along with the bids, because of cheap credit. That finding leads into the final sentence's alternative explanation, that control worked through loans, so D is correct. A goes too far and contradicts the text: the bids did fall, so the bidding wasn't shown to have no effect. B notices that prices fell, but it misses that the sentence complicates the historians' claim instead of supporting it. C is about how the agreements began, and the text never explains that.

quality.seed: economics and business — Indian indigo dye price fixing by London merchant syndicates during colonial monopoly trade control

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "finds that account incomplete" 뒤에 오는 근거이며, 마지막 문장의 대안 설명(대출을 통한 통제)으로 이어지므로 D가 유일한 정답. A는 입찰가가 실제로 떨어졌다는 본문과 모순(과잉 진술), B는 방향이 반대(지지가 아닌 복잡화), C는 지문에 없는 기원 설명. A·B는 부분적 근거(가격 하락 언급, 기존 해석 약화)를 가져 비교가 필요하고 C도 지문 소재와 연결되어 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 선택지 참조 정확, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 가상의 학자명 사용으로 사실 오류·저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: 비교가 필요한 오답은 B 하나뿐이다. A('효과 없음')는 극단적 진술이고 지문과도 바로 모순되며, C(담합의 기원)는 지문에 근거가 전혀 없어 쉽게 배제된다. 정답 D는 '반증 증거 → 대안 설명'이라는 전형적 구조라서 훑어 읽어도 고를 수 있다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져야 한다는 medium 기준에 미달한다.

problem.passage:
Accounts of colonial Potosí's enormous silver output often credit two factors: unusually rich ore and the mercury amalgamation process, which let refiners extract silver from lower-grade rock. Economic historian Rossana Quiroga argues that these accounts miss a third factor, labor costs. In the 1570s Viceroy Francisco de Toledo expanded the earlier labor demands of the encomienda system into the mita, a rotating draft that required Andean communities to send about one-seventh of their adult men to the mines each year. __Drafted workers, or mitayos, were paid wages, but officials fixed those wages at roughly a third of what freely hired miners earned for similar work.__ Since mitayos also had to pay for their own travel and food, their home villages often sent money and supplies to keep them alive. In effect, Quiroga contends, Andean communities were covering part of the mines' labor bill, and mine owners' profits depended as much on this hidden subsidy as on the quality of the ore.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Accounts of colonial Potosí's enormous silver output often credit two factors: unusually rich ore and the mercury amalgamation process, which let refiners extract silver from lower-grade rock. Economic historian Rossana Quiroga argues that these accounts miss a third factor, labor costs. In the 1570s Viceroy Francisco de Toledo expanded the earlier labor demands of the encomienda system into the mita, a rotating draft that required Andean communities to send about one-seventh of their adult men to the mines each year. __Drafted workers, or mitayos, were paid wages, but officials fixed those wages at roughly a third of what freely hired miners earned for similar work.__ Since mitayos also had to pay for their own travel and food, their home villages often sent money and supplies to keep them alive. In effect, Quiroga contends, Andean communities were covering part of the mines' labor bill, and mine owners' profits depended as much on this hidden subsidy as on the quality of the ore.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It identifies the specific arrangement that the text later shows shifted mining costs onto Andean villages.
It presents the conventional explanation for Potosí's silver output that Quiroga's argument challenges.
It offers evidence that the mita was less coercive than its description as a forced draft would suggest.
It describes a cost of the mercury amalgamation process that the text later says refiners passed on to workers.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 미타요의 임금이 자유 노동자의 약 3분의 1로 고정되었다는 사실을 제시하고, 이어지는 문장들은 이 낮은 임금 때문에 마을들이 노동자를 부양해야 했고 결국 광산 노동비 일부를 떠안았다고 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 틀렸다. 통념적 설명(풍부한 광석, 아말감 공정)은 첫 문장에 나오며, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 Quiroga의 주장을 뒷받침한다. C는 임금이 지급되었다는 점만 보고 고른 오답으로, 이 문장의 요점은 임금이 억제되었다는 것이지 강제성이 약했다는 것이 아니다. D는 아말감 공정이 지문에 언급되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 임금은 정련 공정의 비용이 아니라 노동 징발 제도의 일부이다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence states that mitayos' wages were fixed at about a third of free miners' pay. The sentences after it explain that because pay was so low, home villages had to support the workers, which meant they were covering part of the mines' labor costs. So A is correct. B is wrong because the conventional explanation (rich ore and amalgamation) comes in the first sentence, and the underlined sentence actually supports Quiroga's challenge to it. C picks up on the fact that wages were paid, but the point of the sentence is that wages were kept low, not that the system was less coercive. D may seem plausible because amalgamation appears in the text, but the wages belong to the labor draft, not to the refining process.

quality.seed: economics and business — Peruvian silver mining encomienda labor system extracting colonial wealth through forced wage suppression mechanisms

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장(미타요 임금을 자유 노동자의 약 1/3로 고정)은 이후 문장에서 마을이 노동자를 부양하게 된 원인으로 연결되므로 A가 정확하다. B는 첫 문장의 통념 설명과 혼동을 유도하고, C는 '임금 지급'이라는 표면 정보를, D는 지문에 등장한 아말감 공정을 활용한 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. 역사적 사실(톨레도의 1570년대 미타 제도화, 약 1/7 징발, 미타요 임금이 자유 노동자보다 낮음)은 통설과 부합한다. Quiroga는 허구적 학자로 보이나 SAT 관행상 문제 없음. 한·영 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 두 단계 판단(문장 내용 파악 + 이후 문맥 연결)이 요구되어 medium에 적합하다.

advisory.note: A가 정답이려면 밑줄 문장(낮게 고정된 임금)을 이후 문장(마을의 보조, 숨은 보조금)과 연결해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. B는 지문에 나오는 통념적 설명을, D는 아말감 공정 언급을, C는 임금 지급 사실을 각각 이용해 그럴듯해 보인다. 다만 B와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 역사적 배경(톨레도, 1570년대, 성인 남성 약 7분의 1)은 대체로 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In the seventeenth century, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) sought to control the global supply of cloves and nutmeg by confining their cultivation to a few islands it governed directly, such as Ambon and the Banda Islands. Company officials regularly sent expeditions to uproot spice trees growing elsewhere in the archipelago, and VOC trading posts on Java were forbidden to buy spices from local growers. Some historians have described these measures as evidence that the company feared Javanese farmers would outproduce its own plantations. __Yet the records of the trading posts themselves suggest a different worry: officials complained far more often about Javanese merchants reselling spices to English and Portuguese buyers than about the size of Javanese harvests.__ On this reading, the restrictions had less to do with how much farmers grew than with who could carry the spices to market, since any leak beyond the company's ships would weaken its ability to set prices in Europe.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the seventeenth century, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) sought to control the global supply of cloves and nutmeg by confining their cultivation to a few islands it governed directly, such as Ambon and the Banda Islands. Company officials regularly sent expeditions to uproot spice trees growing elsewhere in the archipelago, and VOC trading posts on Java were forbidden to buy spices from local growers. Some historians have described these measures as evidence that the company feared Javanese farmers would outproduce its own plantations. __Yet the records of the trading posts themselves suggest a different worry: officials complained far more often about Javanese merchants reselling spices to English and Portuguese buyers than about the size of Javanese harvests.__ On this reading, the restrictions had less to do with how much farmers grew than with who could carry the spices to market, since any leak beyond the company's ships would weaken its ability to set prices in Europe.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that Javanese harvests were too small to threaten the company's plantations, which supports the historians' view mentioned earlier.
It introduces documentary evidence that points to a concern other than the one some historians have emphasized, setting up the interpretation that follows.
It introduces a claim about English and Portuguese buyers that the rest of the text goes on to show was exaggerated by company officials.
It introduces an example of the company's policies on Java that illustrates the expeditions to uproot spice trees described earlier.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해 일부 역사가들의 해석(자와 농민의 생산 경쟁에 대한 두려움)과 달리, 교역소 기록이 재판매 문제라는 다른 우려를 보여 준다고 제시하며, 이어지는 문장이 이를 바탕으로 해석을 전개하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 기록을 언급한다는 점은 맞지만, 수확 규모가 작았다고 주장하지 않았고 역사가들의 견해를 지지하는 것도 아니라 반박한다. C는 영국·포르투갈 구매자를 언급한다는 점은 맞지만, 뒤 문장은 그 우려가 과장되었다고 하지 않고 오히려 이를 해석의 근거로 삼는다. D는 회사 정책과 연결된 것처럼 보이지만, 밑줄 문장은 정책의 예시가 아니라 기록을 근거로 한 반론이다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence opens with "Yet." It says the trading-post records point to a different worry, Javanese merchants reselling spices to rivals, not the fear of being outproduced that some historians have emphasized. The final sentence then builds its interpretation on that evidence, so B is correct. A is right that the sentence cites records, but the sentence never says Javanese harvests were small, and it challenges the historians' view instead of supporting it. C is right that the sentence mentions English and Portuguese buyers, but the text never calls that worry exaggerated; it uses the worry as the basis of its interpretation. D fails because the sentence isn't an example of a company policy; it offers evidence that pushes back on an earlier interpretation.

quality.seed: economics and business — Indonesian spice monopoly enforcement and Dutch trading post restrictions preventing Javanese cultivation competition

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 역사가들의 해석과 대비되는 기록 증거를 제시하고, 마지막 문장("On this reading")이 이를 바탕으로 해석을 전개하므로 B가 정확하다. A는 기록을 인용한다는 점만 맞고 수확 규모·역사가 지지 부분이 틀림, C는 영국·포르투갈 언급은 맞으나 '과장'은 본문에 없음, D는 정책 예시가 아님. 두 오답(A, C)이 부분적 근거를 지녀 비교가 필요하고 D도 표면적으로 그럴듯해 medium에 적합. VOC의 Ambon·Banda 집중 재배와 향신료 나무 제거 원정은 역사적 사실에 부합하며, 역사가들의 해석은 가설적 틀로 제시되어 사실 오류 없음. 한·영 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: B만 성립한다. A는 기록에 대한 부분적 근거가 있고 C는 구매자 언급이라는 부분적 근거가 있으며, D도 말은 된다. 지문은 VOC 독점 정책을 단순화해 서술했지만 문항 판단에는 영향이 없다.

problem.passage:
For decades, Merino sheep graziers in Australia sold their greasy fleece at auction and simply accepted whatever price the market offered that week. When wool futures contracts became widely available, economists expected growers to use them eagerly to lock in prices months ahead of shearing. Yet adoption among individual graziers remained low, largely because a single family farm rarely produced enough wool to match the standardized contract sizes. __Grazier cooperatives, however, could pool the clips of dozens of members into volumes large enough to trade.__ Once several cooperatives in New South Wales began hedging on their members' behalf, participating growers reported far steadier incomes than neighbors who continued selling only at auction.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: For decades, Merino sheep graziers in Australia sold their greasy fleece at auction and simply accepted whatever price the market offered that week. When wool futures contracts became widely available, economists expected growers to use them eagerly to lock in prices months ahead of shearing. Yet adoption among individual graziers remained low, largely because a single family farm rarely produced enough wool to match the standardized contract sizes. __Grazier cooperatives, however, could pool the clips of dozens of members into volumes large enough to trade.__ Once several cooperatives in New South Wales began hedging on their members' behalf, participating growers reported far steadier incomes than neighbors who continued selling only at auction.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why economists first expected graziers to adopt futures contracts eagerly.
It identifies a weakness of futures contracts that led most cooperatives to keep selling at auction.
It presents a way around the obstacle that had kept individual graziers from using futures contracts.
It gives evidence that cooperative members earned steadier incomes than growers who sold only at auction.
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 개별 농가의 생산량이 표준 계약 규모에 못 미쳐 선물 이용이 저조했다는 장애를 제시하고, 밑줄 문장은 협동조합이 물량을 합쳐 그 장애를 극복할 수 있었음을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. A는 경제학자들의 기대를 언급하지만 그 기대의 이유는 밑줄 문장이 아니라 그 앞에서 다뤄진다. B는 계약 규모 문제를 떠올리게 하지만, 협동조합은 오히려 헤지를 시작했으므로 지문과 반대된다. D의 소득 안정은 지문에 나오지만 밑줄 문장이 아니라 마지막 문장이 제시하는 결과이다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the underlined one names an obstacle: one family farm usually couldn't produce enough wool to fill a standardized contract. The underlined sentence shows how cooperatives got past that by pooling their members' wool, so C is correct. A brings up the economists' expectation, but the underlined sentence doesn't explain why they expected it. B points to the contract-size issue, but it's wrong because the cooperatives actually started hedging instead of sticking with auctions. D describes the steadier incomes, which is a result reported in the final sentence, not in the underlined one.

quality.seed: economics and business — Australian wool greasy fleece price hedging futures adoption by Merino sheep grazier cooperatives

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 직전 문장이 제시한 장애(계약 규모 대비 개별 농가 생산량 부족)에 대한 해결책(협동조합의 물량 합산)을 제시하므로 C가 명확히 옳다. A는 밑줄 이전 내용, D는 마지막 문장 내용을 가리키며, B는 지문과 반대되는 서술로 지문 요소를 재활용한 적절한 오답 구성이다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 모순 없음. 지문은 창작 서술로 보이며 저작권 문제 없음. 장애→해결 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합하다.

advisory.note: 정답을 고르려면 앞 문장의 장애와 'however'로 이어지는 해결책을 연결해야 함. B·D는 지문 요소를 부분적으로 활용한 매력적인 오답임.

problem.passage:
In many batik workshops in Pekalongan, Indonesia, design knowledge has long passed from master artisans to apprentices through years of shared work rather than written records. This informal system created a problem when Indonesia began offering copyright protection for traditional motifs: officials needed documentation of who had developed a pattern, yet the cooperative that registered one of the region's best-known floral designs, a motif refined over three generations of a single family's ______ no sketches older than a decade to submit as evidence.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In many batik workshops in Pekalongan, Indonesia, design knowledge has long passed from master artisans to apprentices through years of shared work rather than written records. This informal system created a problem when Indonesia began offering copyright protection for traditional motifs: officials needed documentation of who had developed a pattern, yet the cooperative that registered one of the region's best-known floral designs, a motif refined over three generations of a single family's ______ no sketches older than a decade to submit as evidence.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: workshop had
workshop; had
workshop, and had
workshop, had
problem.explanation: 'a motif refined over three generations of a single family's workshop'은 'one of the region's best-known floral designs'를 설명하는 동격 삽입구이다. 이 삽입구는 design 뒤 쉼표로 시작했으므로 끝에도 쉼표를 찍어 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤에 주어 the cooperative의 동사 had가 이어진다. 그래서 정답은 D이다. A는 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 삽입구가 끝나지 않는다. B의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라놓고, 세미콜론 앞부분은 독립절도 아니다. C의 and는 앞에 동사가 없는데 동사를 나열하는 꼴이 되어 주어 the cooperative에 짝지을 동사가 사라진다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "a motif refined over three generations of a single family's workshop" is an appositive. It describes "one of the region's best-known floral designs." It opens with a comma after "designs," so it needs a matching comma to close it. After that comes "had," the verb for the subject "the cooperative." That makes D the answer. A leaves out the closing comma, so the appositive never ends. B puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and what comes before the semicolon isn't an independent clause. C adds "and," which suggests a second verb in a list, but no first verb exists, so the subject is left without a proper verb.

quality.seed: economics and business — Indonesian batik textile production guild knowledge transmission and design copyright protection mechanisms

hardJudge.note: 주어 the cooperative + 관계절 + 동격 삽입구(a motif ... workshop) 뒤에 본동사 had가 와야 하므로 닫는 쉼표가 있는 D가 유일하게 올바름. A(닫는 쉼표 누락), B(세미콜론 앞이 독립절 아님), C(짝 없는 and) 모두 정당하게 배제됨. 한국어 해설의 'design 뒤'는 'designs'의 사소한 표기 차이로 판정에 영향 없음. 긴 문장에서 주어·삽입구·동사 경계를 추적해야 하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 주어 속 동격구를 닫는 쉼표 문제. 수식어가 길어서 주어-동사 연결을 추적해야 하므로 medium에 적합함. 오답들도 그럴듯함.

problem.passage:
In the Mekong Delta, many rice mills sit close together along the same canals. Economists studying the region noticed that mills in these clusters were more likely to buy modern polishing and color-sorting machines than mills located far from others. __One explanation is that when a mill owner sees a neighbor's new machine produce cleaner, export-quality rice, the owner can judge its value without taking a costly risk.__ Because buyers overseas pay more for such rice, this kind of easy, local learning may help explain why export-oriented technology spread fastest where mills were crowded together.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the Mekong Delta, many rice mills sit close together along the same canals. Economists studying the region noticed that mills in these clusters were more likely to buy modern polishing and color-sorting machines than mills located far from others. __One explanation is that when a mill owner sees a neighbor's new machine produce cleaner, export-quality rice, the owner can judge its value without taking a costly risk.__ Because buyers overseas pay more for such rice, this kind of easy, local learning may help explain why export-oriented technology spread fastest where mills were crowded together.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers a possible reason for the pattern that the economists observed.
It offers a criticism of the method that the economists used.
It offers an example of a mill that refused to adopt new machines.
It offers a prediction about how overseas rice prices will change.
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 밀집 지역 정미소가 현대식 기계를 더 많이 도입했다는 관찰을 제시하고, 밑줄 문장은 "One explanation is"로 시작해 그 이유(이웃의 기계를 보고 위험 없이 가치를 판단)를 제시하므로 정답은 A이다. B는 지문이 경제학자의 연구 방법을 비판하지 않으므로 틀렸다. C는 밑줄 문장이 기계 도입을 거부한 정미소가 아니라 이웃의 도입을 관찰하는 상황을 다루므로 틀렸다. D는 해외 가격이 언급되긴 하지만 그 변화를 예측하지 않으므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the underlined one describes what the economists observed: mills in clusters were more likely to adopt modern machines. The underlined sentence starts with "One explanation is" and gives a reason for that pattern, so A is correct. B is wrong because the text never criticizes how the economists did their research. C is wrong because the sentence is about a mill owner watching a neighbor adopt a machine, not about a mill refusing one. D is wrong because overseas prices are mentioned, but the text never predicts how they will change.

quality.seed: economics and business — Thai rice mill clustering in Mekong Delta and export-oriented milling technology adoption patterns

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장이 "One explanation is"라는 명시적 신호어로 앞 문장의 관찰 패턴에 대한 이유를 제시하므로 A가 정확. 오답 B(방법 비판), C(거부 사례), D(가격 예측)는 지문에 근거가 없으나 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯함. 한·영 해설 모두 결론·선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 단일 규칙·한 단계 추론으로 easy 적합.

advisory.note: "One explanation is"라는 명시적 단서로 한 단계 추론이면 풀린다. 오답 B와 D는 지문에 나오는 요소(경제학자, 해외 가격)를 활용한 전형적 오답이다. C는 다소 약하지만 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the late 1800s, Jamaican smallholders grew bananas on small plots and sold them to many competing foreign shippers.
- By the early 1900s, the Boston-based United Fruit Company had absorbed most rival shippers on the island.
- With few other buyers left, growers had little choice but to accept the prices the company offered—a market condition economists call monopsony.
- In some seasons, the company rejected bunches it judged too small, leaving growers with unsold fruit.
- Low earnings pushed thousands of Jamaican workers to migrate to Panama, Costa Rica, and Cuba for wage labor.

The student wants to emphasize how a change in the number of buyers shifted bargaining power in Jamaica's banana trade. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

problem.question: The student wants to present Park's research while accurately reflecting how strongly its findings are supported. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Park's 2019 study demonstrated that vertical integration, like that of Hyundai's affiliates, caused Korean shipyards to build ships at lower costs per ton than their rivals.
Park's 2019 study suggested that state-backed export credits may possibly have covered some of the financing foreign buyers used to order Korean-built ships.
Park's 2019 study found that vertically integrated shipyards tended to have lower costs per ton, though other factors, such as labor costs, may also explain the pattern.
Park's 2019 study found that shipowners likely ranked delivery speed above price, though other factors may also have influenced their choice of builder.
problem.explanation: 정답 C: Park의 결과(통합 조선소가 단위 비용이 낮은 경향)와 그 한계(인건비 등 대안 설명 배제 불가)를 그대로 반영한다. A: '경향'과 상관관계를 '입증했다', '원인이 되었다'로 부풀렸다. B: 수출 신용 이야기는 정부 기록으로 확인된 사실인데 'may possibly'로 약하게 만들었고, Park의 연구 내용도 아니다. D: 조심스러운 말투는 맞지만 Ortiz 설문 내용을 Park 연구로 잘못 붙였다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. It reports what Park actually found, that vertically integrated yards tended to have lower costs per ton, and it keeps her caveat that other explanations, like labor costs, can't be ruled out. A goes too far: it turns a tendency into proof ("demonstrated") and a cause ("caused"), even though Park's data couldn't rule out other explanations. B goes the other way: the export-credit point comes from government records, so the notes present it as established, and B weakens it for no reason with "may possibly." It also wasn't part of Park's study. D sounds appropriately careful, but the delivery-speed finding comes from Ortiz's 2021 survey, not Park's study.

hardJudge.note: 노트에 확정적 진술(정부 지정, 울산 조선소 개장, 정부 기록상 수출신용)과 잠정적 진술(Park의 '경향', 대안 설명 배제 불가)이 공존하며, 정답 C는 Park의 결과와 한계를 정확한 확실성 수준으로 반영한다. advisory.note: 정답 C는 '경향'이라는 결과와 대안 설명을 배제할 수 없다는 한계를 모두 정확히 반영함. A는 상관관계를 인과·입증으로 과잉 일반화했고, B는 확정된 사실을 과도하게 약화한 데다 출처도 잘못 붙였으며, D는 출처를 잘못 붙였음. B와 D는 출처 오귀속만으로도 쉽게 제거되므로 변별력은 다소 약함.

problem.passage:
Tardigrades, microscopic animals found in mosses and soils worldwide, can survive near-total dehydration by entering a state called anhydrobiosis, in which metabolism becomes nearly undetectable. For years, researchers assumed the animals relied mainly on the sugar trehalose, which protects dried cells in organisms such as brine shrimp. Yet many tardigrade species produce little or no trehalose. In 2017, biologist Thomas Boothby and colleagues reported that tardigrades instead make a family of intrinsically disordered proteins, which lack a fixed shape while the animal is hydrated. As water is lost, these proteins form a glassy solid that appears to trap other cellular molecules in place, keeping them from unfolding or clumping together. When the team inserted genes for the proteins into yeast and bacteria, the microbes became noticeably better at surviving drying, suggesting that the proteins themselves, rather than some other feature of tardigrade biology, provide much of the protection.

According to the text, what did Boothby and colleagues' research indicate about how tardigrades withstand dehydration?

A borrows the word "glassy," but relying on trehalose is the earlier assumption the text challenges. B is right that proteins protect the cells, but it gets their behavior backward, since the proteins lack a fixed shape and then solidify. C mentions yeast and bacteria, but those microbes received the tardigrade genes in the experiment. They weren't the source of the genes.

problem.passage:
The spots on a spotted hyena's coat vary widely among individuals, and biologists have long assumed that such patterns arise from a Turing-type reaction-diffusion process, in which interacting chemical signals spread through embryonic skin and settle into regularly spaced patches. Developmental biologist Mariam Okonjo recently tested this assumption by comparing spot size and spacing across hyena cubs from different body regions. She found that spots on the flanks and back were spaced at roughly even intervals, as a reaction-diffusion model would predict. On the legs, however, spots grew steadily smaller and more crowded toward the paws, a pattern that tracked a gradient in the concentration of a pigment-regulating protein running from the shoulder to the foot.

Okonjo argues that the reaction-diffusion process is not wrong but incomplete: it seems to generate the basic spotted arrangement, while the protein gradient modifies how that arrangement is expressed in different parts of the body. She cautions that the gradient alone could not produce spots at all, since tissue exposed to the protein in the absence of the signaling interactions develops only uniform shading.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
African lungfish survive seasonal droughts by burrowing into drying mud and sealing themselves inside a mucus cocoon, where they can remain for months or even years. For decades, researchers assumed that this dormancy, called estivation, was mainly a matter of slowing down: with no food or water available, the fish's metabolism simply drops, much as a car engine idles. However, recent studies by physiologists examining estivating lungfish tissues suggest a more active picture. Although overall oxygen consumption falls sharply, the fish increase production of certain antioxidant enzymes and convert toxic ammonia into less harmful urea, and their muscle cells switch on genes that limit the breakdown of protein. These findings indicate that estivation is not just reduced activity but a regulated state in which the lungfish's body works to protect its organs until water comes back.

problem.passage:
For decades, the woodpecker's ability to hammer its beak against tree trunks thousands of times a day without apparent harm has been cited as a model for designing protective helmets. Researchers often pointed to the bird's spongy, trabecular bone near the front of the skull, assuming that this porous tissue cushions the brain much as foam padding does. __However, when biomechanist Sam Van Wassenbergh and colleagues analyzed high-speed video of pecking birds in 2022, they found that the skull decelerates almost as abruptly as the beak, indicating that little impact energy is being absorbed along the way.__ The team argues that the woodpecker's small brain, rather than any built-in cushioning, may explain why the forces involved stay below the threshold for concussion—a conclusion that calls into question helmet designs inspired by the bird.

D is about helmets, but the text explains why designers became interested in the first sentence, not in the underlined one.

problem.passage:
Three-toed sloths descend from the forest canopy about once a week to defecate at the base of their trees, a risky trip that exposes them to predators. Biologist Jonathan Pauli and colleagues proposed that the habit is tied to moths living in sloth fur: female moths ride down with the sloth, lay eggs in its dung, and the new adults fly up to find a sloth host. Pauli's team found that sloths carrying more moths also had more nitrogen in their fur and more algae growing there. __The researchers suggest that the moths, as they die and decompose, act as a fertilizer for the algae, which the sloths may then lick from their fur as a supplement to a diet of nutrient-poor leaves.__ If so, the costly trip to the ground may help keep a cycle of nutrients going that benefits sloth, moth, and alga alike.

B is tempting, but it's the final sentence that connects everything back to the trip to the ground; the underlined sentence supplies only one link in that chain. C is wrong because the text reports no measurements about predators spotting sloths, and the underlined sentence offers a suggestion, not data.

problem.passage:
When a shark bites a hagfish, glands along the hagfish's body release mucins and protein threads that expand in seawater into a large mass of slime within a fraction of a second. The slime fills the predator's mouth and gills, making it hard for water to flow through. Rather than holding on, the shark usually spits out the hagfish and swims away choking. In this way, the slime ______ the attack, allowing the hagfish to escape unharmed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When a shark bites a hagfish, glands along the hagfish's body release mucins and protein threads that expand in seawater into a large mass of slime within a fraction of a second. The slime fills the predator's mouth and gills, making it hard for water to flow through. Rather than holding on, the shark usually spits out the hagfish and swims away choking. In this way, the slime ______ the attack, allowing the hagfish to escape unharmed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: prolongs
conceals
interrupts
encourages
problem.explanation: 지문은 점액이 상어의 입과 아가미를 막아 상어가 먹이를 뱉고 떠나며, 그 결과 먹장어가 다치지 않고 도망친다고 설명한다. 따라서 점액은 공격을 '중단시킨다'는 뜻의 C가 가장 논리적이다. A는 공격을 '연장한다'는 뜻이라 상어가 바로 뱉어 낸다는 내용과 반대이다. B는 공격을 '숨긴다'는 뜻인데, 지문은 공격을 감추는 것이 아니라 멈추게 하는 것을 말한다. D는 공격을 '부추긴다'는 뜻이라 먹장어가 탈출한다는 결과와 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the slime clogs the shark's mouth and gills, so the shark spits out the hagfish and leaves, and the hagfish escapes unharmed. That means the slime stops the attack partway through, which is why C, "interrupts," is the best fit. A, "prolongs," would mean the attack lasts longer, but the shark actually lets go quickly. B, "conceals," would mean the slime hides the attack, but the passage is about the attack ending, not about it being hidden. D, "encourages," would mean the slime makes the shark more eager to attack, which goes against the hagfish getting away.

problem.passage:
The Loess Plateau of north-central China is blanketed by fine, yellowish silt that in places lies more than 300 meters deep. For decades, geologists assumed that this sediment was carried directly from the nearby Gobi and Taklimakan Deserts by the strong winds that sweep southeastward each spring. Recent studies of the silt's mineral chemistry, however, suggest a more complicated history. Many of the grains turn out to have been ground down by glaciers and mountain erosion in the Tibetan Plateau and surrounding ranges, then washed into river basins such as the upper Yellow River, where they settled as floodplain deposits.

Only after these deposits dried out and were exposed did the wind pick the particles up again and carry them the final distance to the plateau. According to geochemist Lin Wei and her colleagues, the deserts therefore served mainly as temporary storage areas and launching points rather than as the original source of the silt. In their view, rivers and wind worked in sequence, with each process completing a different stage of the sediment's journey.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

B gets the glacial origin right but downplays wind, even though the text says wind completed the final stage. C compares the amount of silt on the floodplains with the amount on the plateau, which the text never does.

problem.passage:
Each autumn, crowds gather along China's Qiantang River to watch its tidal bore, a wall of water that can exceed three meters as the incoming tide rushes upstream against the river's flow. For decades, researchers attributed the bore's height almost entirely to the funnel shape of Hangzhou Bay, which narrows sharply and squeezes the advancing tide. Recent field measurements, however, suggest that the funnel tells only part of the story. Sensors placed below the surface recorded internal waves—oscillations along the boundary between denser salt water and lighter river water—moving ahead of and beneath the bore. When these internal waves lined up with the arriving tide, the bore grew noticeably steeper; when they were out of step, it weakened even though the bay's geometry stayed the same.

Based on the text, what did the recent field measurements reveal about the Qiantang River's tidal bore?

problem.passage:
Earth's magnetosphere usually acts as an effective shield, deflecting most of the charged particles streaming outward from the Sun in the solar wind. For decades, researchers assumed that the strength of a geomagnetic storm depended mainly on how fast and how dense the incoming solar wind was. Observations from spacecraft positioned between Earth and the Sun, however, have shown that even unusually fast, dense streams often produce only minor disturbances. What matters most is the orientation of the magnetic field carried by the solar wind. When that field points southward, opposite to the direction of Earth's field at the dayside boundary of the magnetosphere, the two fields can link together in a process called magnetic reconnection, opening a pathway for solar wind energy to pour into the magnetosphere. When the field points northward, the shield stays largely intact, and even a powerful stream mostly slides around the planet.

Meteorologists have long linked Europe's winter weather to the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO), a seesaw in air pressure between Iceland and the Azores. When the pressure difference is large, the jet stream tends to flow fast and fairly straight, steering mild, wet storms into northern Europe. Before building a wind farm, engineers usually measure average wind speed at a site for a year or more. But average speed alone can be misleading. Near the ground, air moves through the atmospheric boundary layer, where it tumbles and swirls as it passes over hills, trees, and buildings. __At one test site in Oklahoma, for example, two towers recorded nearly the same average wind speed, yet turbines near the rougher, wooded tower produced noticeably less power and needed more repairs.__ For this reason, many researchers now argue that site surveys should also measure how much the wind fluctuates from moment to moment, not just how fast it blows on average.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a new method engineers use to measure average wind speed at possible wind farm sites.
It gives a specific case showing that average wind speed alone did not predict how well turbines performed.
It presents a finding that challenges the researchers' recommendation stated at the end of the text.
It describes how hills, trees, and buildings form the atmospheric boundary layer near the ground.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'for example'로 시작하며, 평균 풍속이 같았는데도 거친 지형의 터빈 성능이 낮았던 사례를 들어 앞 문장의 "평균 풍속만으로는 오해할 수 있다"는 주장을 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 새로운 측정 방법을 소개하는 것이 아니라 기존 측정의 한계를 보여 주므로 틀리다. C는 이 사례가 마지막 문장의 권고를 반박하지 않고 오히려 뒷받침하므로 틀리다. D는 지형이 경계층을 형성하는 과정을 설명하지 않으며, 그 내용은 앞 문장의 배경일 뿐이다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "for example" and describes two towers with nearly the same average wind speed but different turbine results, which supports the earlier claim that average speed alone can be misleading, so B is correct. A is wrong because the sentence doesn't introduce a new measuring method; it shows a limitation of the usual one. C is wrong because the example supports the researchers' recommendation at the end instead of challenging it. D is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain how the boundary layer forms; that background comes in the sentence before it.

problem.passage:
Most glaciers creep downhill only a few meters each year. Surge glaciers behave differently: after decades of slow movement, they can suddenly speed up and travel many meters in a single day. Scientists think water is a major cause. During warm periods, meltwater from the surface drains down through cracks and gathers where the ice meets the bedrock below. __This trapped water acts like a slippery layer, lifting the ice slightly and reducing the friction that normally holds it in place.__ Once that friction drops, the heavy glacier can slide forward much faster than usual, sometimes until the water finally escapes and the surge ends.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.passage:
Zeolites are crystalline minerals whose aluminosilicate frameworks are riddled with pores of nearly identical width, often less than a nanometer across. Because of this uniformity, zeolites are commonly described as "molecular sieves" that admit molecules small enough to enter the pores and exclude larger ones. Yet in one of their most widespread industrial uses, separating nitrogen from oxygen to produce oxygen-enriched air, size plays almost no role: the two molecules are so similar in dimension that both slip easily into the pores of common zeolites. What distinguishes them instead is charge distribution. Nitrogen molecules have a stronger quadrupole moment than oxygen molecules do, so they are drawn more strongly to the positively charged metal ions lining the zeolite's channels. When air is forced through a bed of the material under pressure, nitrogen clings to the pore walls while oxygen passes through, and lowering the pressure later releases the trapped nitrogen so the bed can be reused.

According to the text, what allows zeolites to separate nitrogen from oxygen in the production of oxygen-enriched air?

problem.question: According to the text, what allows zeolites to separate nitrogen from oxygen in the production of oxygen-enriched air?
options: The pores of common zeolites are narrow enough to block nitrogen molecules while letting the slightly smaller oxygen molecules pass through.
Lowering the pressure on a zeolite bed causes oxygen to be released from the pore walls while nitrogen remains trapped inside.
The positively charged metal ions in zeolite channels react chemically with oxygen, removing it from the air stream.
Nitrogen's electrical properties cause it to be held more strongly by the zeolite's interior than oxygen is, even though both fit in the pores.
problem.explanation: 지문은 질소와 산소가 크기가 비슷해 둘 다 기공에 들어가지만, 질소의 사중극자 모멘트가 더 강해 채널의 양이온에 더 강하게 끌린다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 '분자체'라는 일반적 설명을 이 사례에 잘못 적용한 것으로, 지문은 이 분리에서 크기가 거의 역할을 하지 않는다고 말한다. B는 감압 단계를 언급하지만 감압 시 방출되는 것은 산소가 아니라 붙잡혀 있던 질소이다. C는 금속 이온을 언급하지만 지문은 질소가 이온에 끌린다고 했을 뿐 산소와의 화학 반응은 말하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says nitrogen and oxygen are so similar in size that both enter the pores, but nitrogen's stronger quadrupole moment makes it cling more strongly to the positively charged ions lining the channels, so D is correct. A applies the general "molecular sieve" idea to this case, but the text says size plays almost no role in this separation. B mentions the pressure drop, but what lowering the pressure releases is the trapped nitrogen, not oxygen. C mentions the metal ions, but the text says nitrogen is attracted to them and never describes any chemical reaction with oxygen.

problem.passage:
Shape memory alloys such as nickel-titanium can recover large deformations because their crystal structure switches between two arrangements: a stiff, high-temperature phase called austenite and a more pliable, low-temperature phase called martensite. When the alloy is held above its transformation temperature and then loaded, stress alone can force austenite into martensite, letting the metal stretch by several percent; once the load is removed, the martensite reverts and the part springs back to its original shape. This behavior, known as pseudoelasticity, has drawn interest from aerospace engineers designing components that must flex repeatedly without permanent damage.

Yet engineers at several research centers have found that the same transformation complicates flight hardware. Because the temperature at which the phases switch shifts with each loading cycle, a pseudoelastic part that performs reliably in ground tests may stiffen or soften unpredictably after thousands of cycles in the wide temperature swings of high-altitude flight. Consequently, teams now treat cyclic stability of the transformation temperature, rather than recoverable strain alone, as the key property to qualify before such alloys are installed on aircraft.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Because the phase change behind shape memory alloys' recoverable flexing drifts over repeated use, engineers now focus on that drift when judging whether the alloys are fit for aircraft.

It then points out a problem: the transformation temperature shifts with each loading cycle. It concludes that engineers now treat the stability of that temperature as the key property to check. Choice B captures this whole line of reasoning. Choice A reflects only the advantage described in the first paragraph and ignores the complication raised in the second. Choice C takes the detail that martensite is more pliable, but the text never says parts are designed to stay in that phase. Choice D stretches the point about ground tests too far, because the text never says ground testing was abandoned.

problem.passage:
Magnetorheological (MR) fluids are suspensions of tiny iron particles in oil. Under ordinary conditions, the particles drift freely and the fluid pours much like motor oil. When a magnetic field is applied, however, the particles line up into chains along the field lines, and within milliseconds the fluid stiffens into a semisolid that strongly resists flow. Removing the field lets the chains collapse, and the fluid returns to its liquid state just as quickly.

Engineers have used this reversible behavior to build shock absorbers whose resistance can be tuned continuously. In a conventional damper, the thickness of the fluid is fixed at manufacture, so the device is a compromise between comfort on smooth roads and control on rough ones. An MR damper, by contrast, pairs the fluid with sensors and an electromagnet, adjusting the field hundreds of times per second so that the damping matches conditions as they change. The same principle now appears in seismic dampers installed in some buildings and bridges.

problem.passage:
Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline materials built from metal clusters linked by organic molecules, and some contain so many internal pores that a single gram can have a surface area larger than a soccer field. Because hydrogen molecules cling weakly to these surfaces, researchers have long hoped MOFs could store hydrogen fuel compactly for clean-energy vehicles. Early studies focused on maximizing porosity, assuming that more surface area would always mean more stored hydrogen. Chemist Hiroyasu Furukawa and colleagues found, however, that the most porous frameworks often performed poorly at practical temperatures: their pores were so wide that hydrogen drifted away from the walls unless the material was cooled to around -196°C. Frameworks with somewhat smaller pores, tuned so that each pore wall sat close to the trapped molecules, held hydrogen more strongly and retained more of it under less extreme cooling.

problem.passage:
When tiny silica or polymer spheres of nearly identical size are suspended in a liquid and allowed to settle slowly, they can arrange themselves into an orderly, repeating lattice known as a colloidal crystal. Because the spacing between the spheres is comparable to the wavelength of visible light, such crystals reflect certain colors strongly while letting others pass, producing an iridescent shimmer similar to that of natural opals. Materials scientists have long hoped to use this effect to make fade-resistant pigments that need no dyes. __In practice, however, even small variations in sphere size create cracks and misaligned regions that scatter light randomly and wash out the color.__ Chemist Lin Okafor and colleagues addressed this problem by adding a soft polymer shell to each sphere, which lets neighboring particles shift slightly during drying and settle into a more uniform arrangement, yielding films with noticeably purer hues.

problem.passage:
Engineers who design plastic pipes, bridge bearings, and other long-lived components cannot rely only on a polymer's stiffness as measured in a quick laboratory test. Because polymers are viscoelastic, their molecular chains slowly slide past and untangle from one another under sustained load. A pipe held at constant stretch therefore gradually loses internal stress, a process called stress relaxation, while a beam carrying a constant weight continues to sag over months or years, a process called creep. __Yet a polymer that passes a one-hour strength test with ease may, after a decade of carrying a far smaller load, deform enough to fail.__ For this reason, designers increasingly use accelerated tests at elevated temperatures, which speed up chain motion, to estimate how a material will behave over its full service life.

problem.passage:
In capillary electrophoresis, a sample is injected into a narrow glass tube filled with a buffer solution, and a strong voltage is applied across the tube's ends. Charged molecules in the sample then migrate toward the electrode of opposite charge, each at a speed determined by its electrophoretic mobility, a property that depends largely on the ratio of the molecule's charge to its size. A small, highly charged ion therefore outpaces a large, weakly charged one, and molecules that entered the tube together emerge at the far end at different times. __One might expect neutral molecules, which feel no electrical pull, to remain stranded near the injection point, yet they too reach the detector, carried along by a bulk flow of buffer that the voltage generates along the charged inner wall of the tube.__ Because this flow moves every component in the same direction, analysts can detect positive, negative, and neutral species in a single run, distinguishing them by their arrival times.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

A는 '예외'라는 점은 일부 맞지만 원리가 신뢰할 수 없다고 말하지 않는다. B는 중성 분자도 검출기에 도달한다는 내용과 정반대이며, C는 중성 분자에는 전하 대 크기 비가 적용되지 않으므로 같은 원리의 추가 예시가 아니다.
